author: Xercaine
description: A customizable mod that adds small furniture.

name: Standalone Hot Spring
author: balistafreak
description: [h1]Changelog[/h1] 18 June 2025: 1.6 compatibility tentatively functional! 10 April 2024: 1.5 compatibility tentatively functional! 20 Oct 2022: 1.4 compatibility tentatively functional! 5 Jul 2021: 1.3 compatibility tenatively functional, will declare as 'definitely' once other players have more extensively used it. Many thanks to Ogliss and Wiri for their assistance with the details of the 1.2->1.3 transition! 30 Aug 2020: Chinese (Simplified and Traditional) localizations added, thanks to [url=https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198430532092]RicoFox223@ 边缘汉化组[/url] and [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/leafzxg]leafzxg@ 边缘汉化组[/url]! 25 Aug 2020: Russian localization added, thanks to [url=https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198122890724]Tkhakiro[/url]! 22 Aug 2020: Hot spring texture improved, now works with Stuff thanks to [url=https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198143995572]Vincent_Wolfgang[/url]! [h1]What this mod does[/h1] Make use of those steam geysers dotting the map for more than mere electric power! With a great deal of clever excavation deep underground, the groundwater that fuels a steam geyser can be brought gushing to the surface. A large amount of stone blocks are used to stabilize the shifted earth and form a clean, abiotic vessel in the ground, pooling the pure, steaming water into a luxurious hot spring. This gorgeous all-natural bath will be automatically used by pawns as a potent source of meditative joy, and is capable of hosting up to six pawns at once. It is of special interest to sick and/or injured colonists; the soothing heat and therapeutic trace minerals within the hot spring's waters greatly accelerate recovery from injury and illness. Colonists capable of movement can maximize their uptime on the hot spring's positive hediff by being manually directed to use it once per day, hastening their return to health as soon as possible. [h1]Hard numbers[/h1] [url=https://pastebin.com/GsT9WPrQ]Too long for Steam.[/url] [h1]How will this mod affect my gameplay?[/h1] This mod allows pre-electricity colonies to benefit from steam geysers with a non-trivial investment of 500 stony material and several days' worth of construction labor. It encourages building facilities directly around it, as it is useful for both recreation (pawns using it in an impressive room will gain an impressive rec room positive mood) and for injury/illness recovery (recovering pawns should be kept near it to minimize walking time to and from it). Colonies that have electricity must 'sacrifice' a potential geothermal generator, as steam geysers are a limited resource. You will need to find alternative sources of power. The Blood filtration buff is rather modest, equivalent to only 16% of a kidney. It will rarely be the most important factor in immunity gain. The Natural healing factor increase is very strong, as the only other (non-mod) source of increase is an implant locked behind a techprint. If this bothers you, you can easily reduce the hediff's strength or remove the effect altogether by editing the HediffDefs in the .xml. [h1]Tested With[/h1] While this mod's code was based on the hot spring from [url=https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198184990805/myworkshopfiles/?appid=294100]ssulunge[/url]'s [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1918120749]Kijin Race 2.0[/url] mod, everything in the backend was renamed and recategorized properly to ensure that the mods should not conflict on a compatibility level. Mod order seems to be irrelevant as long as it comes after Core/Royalty. [h1]Graphics[/h1] Workshop page art can be found [url=https://www.pixiv.net/en/artworks/15894645]here[/url]. It was drawn by [url=https://www.pixiv.net/en/users/979179/artworks]隂宅[/url]. The original art for the hot spring was sourced from an anonymous Mongolian cartoon-swapping website. It was further modified, enhanced, and given a stuff-mask by the talented [url=https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198143995572]Vincent_Wolfgang[/url]. [h1]About and Acknowledgments[/h1] Please let me know in the comments section if you encounter any problems with this mod. I have little experience with game modding, so any comments, feedback, and/or coding/implementation pointers are greatly appreciated. [h1]A very big thanks to:[/h1] [url=https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198184990805/myworkshopfiles/?appid=294100]ssulunge[/url] for creating the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1918120749]Kijin Race mod[/url] in the first place. His original C# code forms the basis of this mod's code; without it, I never would have even considered undertaking this project. "Wiri" (from the Rimworld discord) for taking me by the hand and teaching me about .dll decompilers, Visual Studio, and Rimworld in C# code far above and beyond what a static tutorial ever could. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/dninemfive/myworkshopfiles/?appid=294100]dninemfive[/url] for having written the Plague Gun tutorial in the first place, encouraging me to step into the world of C# properly, and for continuing to assist me with Rimworld code screwups beyond it. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198143995572]Vincent_Wolfgang[/url] for taking the fate of my ugly texture into his own two hands. He improved the original bootleg texture's linework, greyscaled the rocks to work with a stuff-mask, and made said stuff-mask almost entirely on his own initiative. author: Fluffy
description: Allows building floors out of stuff*. Important You can safely add this mod to you save games, but you can not remove it from save games. (If you really must do this, you'll have to remove all built stuffed floors added by this mod first). Features This mod does two things. First, using Architect Sense it provides a framework for modders to define their own stuffed floor types. Second, it uses this framework to create a number of new floors that are stuffed. For players Adds several new floors, and existing floors from Telkir's More Floors, CuproPanda's Extra Floors and Pravus' Fences and Floors in all types of stone, metal, wood. Works great with other mods that add more resources, e.g. Minerals and Materials Kura's Extra Minerals, Extended Woodworking, Vegetable Garden and GlitterTech. This mod also organizes and where needed, removes non-stuffed versions of the floors added by RimWorld, More Floors, Extended Woodworking, Minerals and Materials, GlitterTech, More Furniture, Vegetable Garden, and Floored. Other mods can easily add more floors using existing materials, or completely new types of materials. For modders Adds a custom FloorTypeDef that derives from TerrainDef, and allows modders to create floortypes by setting a texture and a list of stuffCategories to generate terrain defs for. Removing now obsolete terrainDefs and/or architect categories is also easily handled. See GitHub for a guide on using Stuffed Floors in other mods. Known issues While this mod will happily generate more floors for any mods that add materials to the metallic, stony and/or woody stuff types, it only cleans up the floors added by mods that are explicitly supported. Any other mods that add floor types may appear as duplicates. If you encounter such an issue, please let the author(s) of said mod(s) know so that they can correctly set up their designator groups! Powered by Harmony

name: Odyssey Shuttle Variants
author: Luke
description: Expands RimWorld's Odyssey transport-shuttle system with a family of buildable, role-distinct craft and a typed-capacity system that tracks colonists, mechs and cargo as independent pools instead of one shared mass limit. THE CRAFT - Passenger Shuttle (vanilla, folded into the system) - the balanced all-rounder: a handful of seats and modest cargo. - Troop Shuttle - fast squad insertion and extraction: many seats, light cargo, long range. - Cargo Shuttle - dedicated hauler: a large hold with just enough crew to fly it. - Heavy Cargo Ship - the flagship hauler: the biggest hold in the fleet, but slow, fuel-hungry and short-ranged. - Mechanitor Shuttle (Biotech) - a mech strike carrier flown by a mechanitor; it will not launch without one aboard. It ferries a mech warband against a bandwidth budget rather than a seat count. When landed it also doubles as a chemfuel-powered field charger: nearby colony mechs walk up to the hull and recharge from the shuttle's own fuel, no power grid required (an opt-in toggle, off by default so it never strands itself). - Transport Drone (Biotech) - a fully autonomous courier with no crew. Send it anywhere, land and hold its cargo in the field, then recall it, send it onward, form a camp, or gift its cargo to a friendly settlement for goodwill. FEATURES - Typed capacity: colonists (seats), mechs (bandwidth budget) and cargo (mass, excluding crew and mech weight) are capped independently, with clear load-dialog readouts and over-cap warnings. - Autonomous drone: hands-free supply runs and automated diplomacy gifts; it survives the origin map being abandoned. - Mech field charging at a landed Mechanitor Shuttle, run off its own chemfuel. - Mech-bay expansion research: two tiers that raise the Mechanitor Shuttle's carried-mech bandwidth (6 to 12 to 18) and widen its field-charging line (2 to 3 to 4 mechs at once). Already-built ships benefit the moment the research completes. - Every craft is research-gated off the vanilla Shuttles project, built in the Odyssey architect category, and costs a rare shuttle engine (trader/reward only; larger craft need more). - Works on other mods' shuttles: the mod options page lists every player shuttle you have installed, and any of them can be given seats, cargo mass and a mech bandwidth budget of your choosing. Craft from other mods are left exactly as their author made them until you opt them in. COMPATIBILITY - Instant Loot Shuttle: supported. Crew no longer count against the cargo hold when instant-loading, so a full squad will not refuse the launch or leave your cargo behind. MULTIPLAYER Built with the Multiplayer mod and played through multiplayer sessions without trouble. One player has reported mass and landing problems that only appear in multiplayer, which I have not yet been able to reproduce - if you run into anything like that, please say so in the comments, it genuinely helps. It also runs fine without Multiplayer installed. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2606448745 COMPANION MODS Two mods that handle the other half of the same job - getting one of these craft loaded and away without ten minutes of clicking: Crew Presets - save named groups of colonists, animals and mechs - "Strike Team", "Pack Train" - and apply them with one click in the load dialog, instead of hand-picking the same pawns every launch. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3756372833 Transporter Loadouts - every transporter and shuttle remembers its own default cargo, pre-filled each time you open its load dialog. Crew Presets picks the people; this one picks the freight. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3756377821 Requires Odyssey. The Mechanitor Shuttle and Transport Drone additionally require Biotech. CHANGES 1.0.3 - Fixed a bug in this mod that could leave the info card ("i") blank. It was our fault: the mod threw an error while adding its stats, which stopped the card drawing for everything in the game, not just these shuttles, until it was reopened. Thanks to Sebster for reporting it. - The info card and the architect menu now show cargo capacity, maximum range, passenger capacity and mech bay capacity, for both built craft and the build preview. - Mech bay capacity in the build preview now reflects completed mech-bay expansion research instead of always showing the base figure. - Painting is temporarily disabled on this mod's craft. The colour masks are auto-generated and the paint lands untidily, so the option is off until they have been reworked. 1.0.2 - Typed capacity can now be applied to any player shuttle, including craft from other mods, from the mod options page. Your other mods are untouched until you opt a craft in, and changes take effect on restart. 1.0.1 - Fixed crew being charged against cargo capacity when loading with Instant Loot Shuttle, which could refuse a launch outright or load the crew and leave the cargo behind. - A craft arriving somewhere with no room large enough to land now holds position with its cargo aboard, to be recalled or redirected, instead of being set down where it does not fit. This content/mod is not official and is not endorsed by Ludeon. AI tools were used in the making of this mod.

name: Xenobionic Patcher (Continued)

description: Original mod by SineSwiper https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1911273785 https://github.com/SineSwiper/RimWorld-XenobionicPatcher/ 1.6 Update by SmithsonianDSP: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3554676828 https://github.com/SmithsonianDSP/RimWorld-XenobionicPatcher/tree/1.6 If the original author requests it, I will remove this update. --- Removed HugsLib dependency. -- Original mod notes (1.6): Xenobionic Patcher This patcher mod looks through most of the surgery operations, and matches your modded surgeries (like new bionics) with your modded races and animals. In other words, if you have a bionic expansion mod like FSF's Vanilla Bionics Expansion, EPOE, or RBSE, and a set of modded races or animals, this patcher will match them together a few different ways (examples in quotes): 1. If the surgery works against a "Leg", and your pawn has a "Leg", your pawn gets the operation option. 2. If the surgery works against a different named part, but your pawn definition really calls it a "Leg" in the label, the body part will be mapped together and your pawn will get other "Leg" operations. 3. If the surgery is called "Install bionic arm", and your pawn also has a surgery called "Install bionic arm", the body part will be mapped together (like "Arm" -> "Tentacle") and your pawn will get other "Arm" operations. On top of the surgery-to-race compatibilities, Xenobionic Patcher will also link humanlike operations with animals and visa-versa. Think of the possibilities: * Do your animals need bionic legs or an Orion Exoskeleton from Glitter Tech? You got them! * Is your best colonist quickly dying from a shot to the heart (only alive because of Death Rattle) and the only other heart you own is some bionic animal heart you bought cheap from a trader? You can save him! * Do you want those sweet Genetic Rim animal implants for yourselves? Install them freely! This patcher does not create any items or pawns. It merely links already known operations to other races and animals. In most cases, you don't need any additional race or animal patchers. However, they shouldn't interfere with Xenobionic Patcher, even if you do. Load Order: PUT THIS DEAD LAST for best compatibility! After any race mods, animal mods, bionic mods, medical mods, surgery mods, etc.

name: Better Scenario Research and Tech Level Options (Continued)
author: large moron
description: [img]https://img.litet.net/logos/Info.png[/img] Update of large morons mod https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2870637532 - Anomaly research should no longer be unlocked when selecting Industrial or higher [img]https://img.litet.net/logos/Notice.png[/img] [table] [tr][td][url=https://discord.gg/h5TY6DA][img]https://img.litet.net/logos/Discord.png[/img][/url][/td] [td][url=https://github.com/emipa606/BetterScenarioResearchAndTechLevelOptions][img]https://img.litet.net/logos/Github.png[/img][/url][/td] [/tr] [tr] [td][img]https://img.litet.net/logos/SafeToAdd.png[/img][/td] [td][img]https://img.litet.net/logos/SafeToRemove.png[/img][/td] [/tr] [/table] [img]https://img.litet.net/logos/OriginalDescription.png[/img] [h1] Description: [/h1] This mod gives you better options for selecting your game's starting research and player faction tech level, primarily but not exclusively for use with Semi Random Research. I've been wanting this for years. Lots of mods let you start with no research, but none that I have been able to find let you start [b]with[/b] research already completed. Turns out you can just pay someone to make it for you?! I only play with Semi Random Research and I [i]strongly dislike[/i] caveman stuff flooding the queue when I'm in a higher tech game and just want to research fabrication or nuclear power or toilets. First and foremost this is a QOL mod for me. But maybe it can be for you too. While I initially only wanted something to clear out Neolithic and Medieval research so I could jump right in to the Industrial era, I figured an option for every tech tier would be a simple and welcomed addition. Why not cover all the bases in case someone wants to play as a Medieval, Spacer, or Ultratech faction and have their starting research and costs reflect that? [h1] Features: [/h1] Includes 6 Scenario options to start at the technology tier of your choosing, from Neolithic to Archotech*, with every research project [b]below[/b] your chosen tier automatically completed. *Archotech starts with all research in the game complete, including the Archotech-tier research projects from the few mods that actually have them, like More Archotech Garbage and Science Never Stops. Maybe you're making a new modpack and want to jump right in to testing conflicts and compatibility without delays. Or perhaps you're playing an Archoseed that wasn't shot in the brain by a Lancer...? This mod does not remove the [i]hidden[/i] research included in some scenarios, even if it's higher than your chosen tech level. For example: Crashlanded, Rich Explorer, and Naked Brutality all start you out with some research not mentioned on the Scenario screen, like Electricity. If you choose one of these scenarios and pick Neolithic or Medieval tech level you will still start with electricity. This is intended to safeguard scenarios with specific starting conditions and/or gameplay themes. I wouldn't want someone to pick their favorite scenario and find out, just because they wanted to skip the primitive era research, they can't play their scenario the way it was designed. Use era appropriate scenarios and/or [b]a different mod[/b] if your scenario includes said hidden research. This mod's position in your load order should not matter. If you find some incompatibility or conflict from load order placement please let me know in the comments! [h1]How do I use this?[/h1] When starting a new game click the Scenario Editor button on the bottom of the Scenario screen, select the Edit Mode red X on the left panel, click Add Part, then choose the Set Faction Tech Level option in the drop down list to add it to your scenario. From there, click the new button on the right side of your screen and select the tech level you want. [h1] Recommended companion mods, especially nice for games with longer term progression through the technological ages and generations: [/h1] If any of these interest you please make sure to click these links and read their full descriptions as written by the mod makers before asking questions. Almost all of these have mod options to customize them to your preferences. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2868392160]Research Reinvented[/url] - [i][b]Extremely[/b][/i] rad mod that makes research much more interesting and engaging. Click and behold. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2375902187]Semi Random Research[/url] is my favorite way to play. Instead of opening your research tree and picking exactly what you want, this mod will generate a random selection of research projects on which to work. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=735268789]Tech Advancing[/url] and [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2820526947]Tech Traversal[/url] allow your player faction to advance through the technology tiers so research costs are correctly adjusted and updated. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1970774610]TechBlock[/url] groups research into blocks of technology so you can progress through the research tree in a way that makes a little more sense. You must (more or less) research all of neolithic before you can start medieval, and all of medieval before industrial, and so on. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2554423472]Ignorance is Bliss[/url] prevents higher tech factions from raiding you until you're closer to on or on their same technological level. Getting obliterated by mechanoids or the blue moon corporation when your pawns are still figuring out how to make a longbow can be frustrating, although the challenge isn't always bad. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2554469600]Arcane Technology[/url] prevents you from equipping or using technology that you haven't researched. It's not 100% coherent, as it doesn't take a rocket surgeon to know how to wear a fancier hat, but that charge rifle may be a bit too advanced for your caveman whomst barely grok fire. author: A Horrible Goose

author: BotchJob
description: Adds a new medieval/fantasy faction to the game, along with a bunch of associated weapons, apparel, items, styles and more.

name: Empire Refactored
author: Matathias
description: Spread your rule across the Rimworld with self governing settlements that are loyal to you and you alone. Command them to fight in your name, and destroy your enemies. Events will periodically influence your settlements, or your faction as a whole. You must decide how best to respond to these situations. Your colonists will pay taxes, be it in silver, or goods. You can tell them where you want your taxes, and they will dutifully pay them. A fully customizable faction name and title allows you to put your own spin on your subjects. They can be feudal vassals, a megacorporation’s branch offices, or even a shining beacon of truth and liberty. It is all part of the greater story.

name: Empire Refactored: Routes & Resources
author: Matathias
description: A sub-mod for Empire Refactored, adding stockpile management and supply routes between settlements. Features a simple mode with a shared faction stockpile, and a complex mode with per-settlement stockpiles with logistics routes.

author: wowgag
description: Scout, Sabotage, Destroy! An enemy outpost overhaul mod that strengthens hostile faction bases based on technology level, tier, and role. Scout the enemy, sabotage their base, cut off their turrets, eliminate their commander, and claim the loot. Evolving Enemy Strongholds overhauls hostile faction bases into tech-based, role-driven, evolving military targets. This mod replaces enemy faction base generation. Do not use it together with other faction base generation overhaul mods.

author: IcyCheeseCake

name: Faction Control (1.4-1.6)
author: Rainbeau Flambe (original) & Kiame Vivacity (1.0 to 1.3) & TheRealLemon
description: "Faction Control" provides you with a number of configuration options that you can use to tailor which and how many faction groups and faction bases show up on your map. Simply visit "Mod Settings" from the game's "Options" menu. You can define the total number of faction groups which should appear on your world map (anywhere from 0 to 30), as well as individually adjust the minimum number of groups from each faction which should be present, even removing some factions entirely if you prefer. So you could, for example, play on a planet without any tribal groups, or without any outlanders, or on a planet with no pirates, or perhaps on a planet on which the only faction groups are pirate bands. The mod also gives you the same level of control over individual factions added by mods (up to 42 total) that it provides for vanilla factions. So, for example, if you're playing with a mod that adds several related factions, only some of which you actually want to have present on your world, well, you'll be able to tailor the planet accordingly. (This also gives you the ability to pick and choose which modded factions you want to use in any particular game without having to disable or uninstall the mods that add them.) As you increase the total number of faction groups on your world, the number of groups which are hostile to you will scale upward, as well. So unlike most mods which increase faction counts, this one won't allow you to create a world with 30 faction groups of which only three are hostile. You can also adjust your world map's faction base density, so you can create planets on which each faction group has only a few bases, or heavily populated planets with settlements everywhere. The mod also gives you the option to organize bases geographically, with each faction group's bases in close proximity to each other, so that the planet looks like it's populated by actual nations, rather than just having bases scattered all over the map randomly. - Rainbeau Flambe (dburgdorf) (original) - Kiame Vivacity (previous versions 1.0 to 1.3) - TheRealLemon (current) ===== Compatibility: Since "Faction Control" does nothing but alter initial world generation, adding it to or removing it from a game in progress will have no impact. It should be compatible with any other mods, though it should (and most likely will) override any other mods that alter faction generation. ===== Credits: The mod utilizes Pardeike's "Harmony Patch Library." (No additional download is required, as the library is included with the mod.) [b]Designer225[/b] for improving map generation and allowing this mod's settings to apply to new settlements after world generation. This means that to access the faction customize menu from now on, you need to click the "FC" icon letters that should be down to the right of your screen --- This mod will enable you to --- - Rename the AI factions and leaders. - Modify or load in new ideology - Change faction relationships - Change faction colour - Change the names of settlements - Relocate settlements [For 1.6 and forward] - Create new settlements - Delete settlements - Adding new factions - Randomize names of all existing factions

author: jaeger972

name: Forsaken Faction For Alpha Genes
author: Matsay, Major_Quadrangle
description: Adds a faction for Alpha Gene's version of the Forsaken, along with a few quests/events to allow easier player interaction.

name: Go Explore!
author: Albion
description: This mod adds various new world events. Lost city - The location of a ruined city is discovered. It is dangerous but there is loot from the former inhabitants. Ambrosia addicted animals - A large ambrosia sprout happened nearby. However some animals seem to be hooked in the fruits and defend them. Ship core startup - You detect a nearby energy signature of a ship reactor powering up. Go investigate. New settlement - Some faction founded a new settlement in your general area. Prisoner camp - A non-hostile faction asks you to free some of their prisoners held on a site near your colony. Research request - Another faction is requesting the help of your best researcher in exchange for some insight and a relationship boost. Intercepted message - You intercepted a message that indicates an item stash. Is it a trap or will you find some loot? \nIncludes spanish, french, russian and ukranian translation.

name: Kiiro Story: Events Expanded
author: Ancot
description: Events expanded for kiiro race, add specific events and new interactions related to kiiro faction. Should be load after kiiro race mod.

name: Mechanoids: Total Warfare
author: Nyarlathotep
description: Thanks for subscribing to "Mechanoids: Total Warfare" MOD! This mod's difficulty primarily centers on new mechanical enemies and their accompanying enhancement systems. These enhancements gradually unlock as players trigger specific conditions during gameplay, delivering an extremely hardcore trial while avoiding unnecessary power creep. If you feel excessive pressure during play, please prioritize your experience - you can reduce raid intensity or disable mechanoid enhancements in settings. ● Total Warfare provides deep expansion to RimWorld's original mechanoid content, offering: Richer mechanoid unit options Unique combat mechanics Epic-scale battles ● Total Warfare features progressive difficulty design. The mod reconstructs vanilla combat logic, expands battle scale, and adds about a dozen distinctive mechanoid units. Early-game content focuses on exploring new elements, allowing you to naturally familiarize yourself with numerous new items and mechanics while enjoying gameplay, establishing a solid foundation for late-game challenges. Please note that for late-game challenges, we recommend utilizing the mod's new mechanics, mechanoids, and structures - using purely vanilla tactics against new enemies may significantly increase combat difficulty. ● Additionally, Total Warfare introduces the hidden faction NCL. By constructing an NCL Quantum Communication Console, you can establish contact to: Trade valuable resources for colony expansion Request deployment of Titan class Mechanoid Archowrom as garrison reinforcements 『Archowrom Garrison Feature: This worm can dramatically reduce raid difficulty. If you wish to avoid frequent interruptions during construction, you can use it to eliminate threats. Please note its combat methods may cause unexpected damage to your base facilities.』

name: Medieval Total Rim: The Ottoman Empire
author: Athelas
description: Medieval Total Rim: The Ottoman Empire is a new faction mod inspired by the Turks faction from Medieval II: Total War. The mod introduces new unit types, backstories, a unique Turkish culture, a custom ideology, scenarios to play, and a new fully Medieval Overhaul compatible faction.

name: No Disabled Factions In Quests
author: kathanon
description: Prevents generation of quests that call for threats that are not possible with the current settings - such as a mech cluster with the mech faction disabled.

name: Nomad Friendly Quests
author: jaeger972
description: Makes it so any temporary map like camps or ancient complexes count as player homes. This is done internally by the first map that could become a permanent settlement like it is one already. This only takes effect if you don't have a settlement. This also removes the minimum colonist count for quests. In theory this means that every quest will be available even for solo nomads that only use camps.

name: Orc Clan + Xenotype
author: Karew
description:
Adds a new orc clan faction and an orc xenotype.

The orc clans are proud, industrial-era rimworld denizens who heavily favor melee combat. Battle the orcs as raiders or become their trade partner and ally.

All genes are inheritable, and orcs are an available xenotype at colony start.

name: Real Ruins
author: mr.teterew
description: "Everyone is dead or gone. This story is over. Perhaps someone else will find a use for the ruins of this place." Have you ever wondered who is that person which will find a use for those ruins? With this mod it might be any other RimWord player, and you will find ruins of other players' bases as well. This mod periodically uploads your base to the server database, and when a new map is generated, this database provides pieces of those stored bases as templates for abandoned ruins. Probably you'll find just an empty dirty shelter with badly damaged wooden bed and a pair of chairs. Probably you'll be lucky enough to find someone's silver vault before scavengers from the nearest settlement arrive. This mod can be added anytime, it won't break your saves and will take effect when you enter into a new map, either starting a new game or with a caravan.

name: Reel's Insector Faction
author: Reel
description: !!! Requires Vanilla Races Expanded - Insector !!! !!! Requires Vanilla Factions Expanded - Insectoids 2 !!! !!! Requires Biotech DLC !!! Welcome to Reel's Insector Faction! After spending thousands of hours playing RimWorld, I've always longed for a faction that truly embraced the Insectoids. The Serketist structure and the Insectoid Supremacy meme from Vanilla Ideology Expanded - Memes and Structures fueled this desire even more. With the introduction of Vanilla Races Expanded - Insectors, we now have the xenotype we needed, but something still felt missing: true integration between Insectors and Insectoids. Sure, I could’ve used a mod to force the Insector xenotype to generate within an existing faction, but what's the point of an insectoid-related faction without the Insectoids? That’s where Reel's Insector Faction comes in! With this mod, your colony will face raids from both Insectors and Insectoids. Imagine a large Insector raid party supported by a pack of Spelopedes and Megaspiders. Plus, this mod offers seamless integration with Vanilla Factions Expanded - Insectoids 2, meaning all the new bugs will join the fray as well. You'll face combined raids featuring both Insectors and Insectoids, making for a more immersive and challenging threat. The mod also adds custom base generation, a new trader type, and a unique ideology culture, along with custom pawn names to enhance your RimWorld experience. Plus, it's fully compatible with Vanilla Ideology Expanded - Memes and Structures, ensuring everything fits seamlessly into your game. So what are you waiting for? Will you befriend the Insectors and forge a powerful alliance? Or exterminate every last one of them? Remember, the only good bug is a dead bug!

[*]mlie: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2201715440 (1.1 - 1.3) [*]AngryHornet: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2896988266 (1.4) [/list] [hr][/hr] [h2]Please remember to unsubscribe to previous versions to avoid mod conflicts if you are playing RimWorld 1.5.[/h2] [hr][/hr] [h2]Original mod description[/h2] [h3]Edit scenarios midgame[/h3] [b]NB![/b] This mod has been reported to have an issue where the Save-button not working. This is either a mod conflict or a recent game update having changed some code. I have not looked into this yet, and can not make any promises that I will in the foreseeable future. [b]About scenarios[/b] A scenario is the basis of a new game. You choose starting pawns, some items, maybe disable infestation-incidents, and so on. At the start of a game, the scenario sets everything according to your choices. Likewise, when you click [i]Save[/i] in the scenario editor in Scenario Amender, it will grab your newly edited scenario settings and apply them to your game. This is complex, and can have unforeseen consequences with mods that do things I have no knowledge about. [b]DISCLAIMER[/b] Backup your save before using this! Especially if you're using mods that extend or alter scenario options. I am not responsible for broken games. [b]Usage[/b] Load your save, open the [i]Main menu[/i] tab and click [i]Review Scenario[/i]. Click [i]Edit[/i], make your changes, and click [i]Save[/i]. Done. [b]Notes:[/b] - Changes to starting pawns do not affect existing pawns, only new ones. - Changes to starting items, such as silver and equipment, do not work. - Changes to player faction do not work. - Adding starting research will not remove finished research - only add to it. - Safe to add and remove from existing saves. - Edited scenarios retain their changes even without [i]Scenario Amender[/i] active.

description: With this mod, you can start your game at any tech level, from protohuman Animal to mysterious Archotech. For every level, there is a unique player faction with its own perks (such as forageability and, if you own Ideology DLC, disallowed precepts). All technologies from previous tech levels will be known to you, and respective research bonuses/maluses will be applied. Optionally, you can also have appropriate starting techs like in vanilla (e.g. Electricity for Industrial level start). The mod adds a new screen after you choose your starting location, where you can pick the tech level and other options. Just select the level of your choice or let the RNG do it for you, decide whether you need the starting techs, and click Next. Want vanilla experience this time? Then simply leave the choice as Default, no need to disable the mod. This mod should work well with any other mods except those that add/replace/remove player factions. Recommended mods: - Tech Advancing (allows you to upgrade your tech level) - Primitive Workbenches (for Animal and Tribal starts) Github: https://github.com/GarwelGarwel/StartingTechLevel

name: [Alpha] Anomaly Remix: Gray Pall
author: 1trickPwnyta
description: A thick, ominous fog settles across the planet. You and your fellow researchers feel a sense of dread as the wind stills and the smell of rotten flesh enters your nostrils. You were only here to collect rock samples, but your curiosity overtakes you, and you wander off on your own, hoping to find the source of the murky haze. Suddenly, a gigantic monolith appears before you. You can feel it speaking into your mind, beckoning you, but you decide to make your way back to the research base so you can show your colleage. After a short hike back to where you spotted the monolith, the two of you are surrounded by shrieking inhuman creatures that appeared out of nowhere. One of them got a little too close and gouged your left eye out of its socket. Thinking quickly, you light a flare to ward them away for now. As the researched you brought along with you tends to your open wound, you peer into the fog, looking for the monolith, but you can't seem to find it anymore. "I swear it was here!" you reassure her. But there's no trace. Defeated, you return to the base and climb into bed. You'll find it again tomorrow. Somehow you know that if you could study it, you could figure out how to stop the gray pall and the terrifying entities it summons. <size=18px><color=#5aa9d6>What this does</color></size> Anomaly Remix: Gray Pall introduces a new Anomaly playstyle different from Standard or Ambient horror. This new playstyle is called Gray Pall. With the Gray Pall Anomaly playstyle enabled, gray palls control when Anomaly threats occur. By default, Anomaly threats do not occur unless there is a gray pall active, and then Anomaly threats are the only threats that occur. To play with the Gray Pall playstyle, start a new colony, and on the storyteller selection page, click on Anomaly settings, and then select Gray Pall. You can fiddle with the threat sliders for a custom experience, and if you select a custom game difficulty, there are additional options for Gray Pall mode in the custom difficulty settings. <size=18px><color=#5aa9d6>Coming soon</color></size> A future version of this mod will include a unique starting scenario that utilizes the Gray Pall Anomaly playstyle and includes a new way to win the game. ________________________________________________ <size=18px><color=#5aa9d6>Credits</color></size> • Mod icon: twitter.com/mouse_draws

description: 메카노이드에게 인공 자궁을 이식해 인간 아이를 잉태시키는 시스템을 추가하는 프레임워크 모드입니다. 메카나이터 솔로 플레이를 위해 설계되었습니다. 인공 자궁을 연구한 뒤 직접 제작하여 호환 메카노이드에 이식하면, 그 메카는 정해진 주기에 따라 배란합니다. 임신에는 두 가지 경로가 있습니다. 배란 중인 메카에게 추출한 정자를 주입하거나 함께 시간을 보내 자연 임신을 시도할 수 있습니다. Biotech의 난자 추출과 수정 절차로 만든 인간 배아를 인공 자궁에 직접 이식하는 것도 가능합니다. 배아 이식으로 태어난 아이는 난자 제공자와 정자 제공자의 유전자 및 친부·친모 관계를 이어받으며, 아이를 품은 메카 역시 부모 관계와 모성 기록을 남깁니다. [자궁 3종] - 인공 자궁 (산업): 배란 24일 / 임신 18일. 일정 확률로 신생아가 약하게 태어날 수 있습니다. - 생체공학 인공 자궁 (우주): 배란 20일 / 임신 15일. 일정 확률로 메카나이트 강화 아이를 출산합니다. - 초월공학 메카노이드 자궁 (초월공학): 제작 불가, 희귀품으로만 획득. 배란/임신 모두 10일. 어떤 결함도 없는 메카나이트 강화 아이를 안정적으로 출산하며, 사랑 시 추가 무드 보너스를 제공합니다. [메카나이트 강화 아이] 혈관에 메카나이트 입자가 통합되어 신체 능력이 강화되며(혈액여과/혈액순환/이동/청각/시력 +25%, 받는 피해 80% 감소), 어떤 학습이든 본능적으로 빨리 익히는 유년기 백스토리를 가집니다. [특징] - 프레임워크 구조: 간단한 패치로 모든 메카노이드 호환. 모드 메카도 자동 적용. - 자궁 적출 및 재이식 지원 - 자연 임신과 Biotech 수정 배아 이식 지원 - 메카 연인·배우자 관계 탭에서 일반/피임/임신 시도 설정 지원 - 친부·친모 유전자, 제노타입 및 가족 관계 보존 - 자궁 티어별 배란 주기, 임신 기간 및 출산 보정 - 임신 단계에 따른 이동 속도와 전력 소모 변화 - 출산 추출 시스템: 임신 만료 후 메카나이터가 직접 아기를 꺼냄 - 한국어 / 영어 번역(AI) 포함 오류가 발생하면 댓글로 알려주시면 감사하겠습니다. 호환 추가할 메카노이드 추천도 받습니다.

description: Tired of always playing on the same boring earthlike worlds? So am I. This is a mod framework for creating entirely new types of planets, fully integrated with Worldbuilder. Does not include any planet types on its own, check the linked steam collection for a few official ones. <size=24>FAQ</size> <size=16>What can this do that Worldbuilder can't?</size> Worldbuilder is first and foremost a map creator. A mod can define the exact tiles/settlements/etc that should be generated, but it can't easily generate custom planets on the fly. This framework allows mods to do things like: - Restrict which biomes should generate - Replace ocean tiles and textures, or remove oceans outright to have a fully solid world - Change the global average temperature to anything they want - And more! All while keeping the vanilla world generation fully intact. Also note that while Worldbuilder has first-class support and I fully recommend using it, the mod can also work without it. In standalone mode, which planet type to generate can be selected in the mod's settings. <size=16>Is this compatible with X?</size> Most likely yes. I tested it with ~1200 mods and it worked perfectly well, but if you come across something that breaks please let me know. <size=16>How can I create a custom planet type using this?</size> Check the source code, documentation's all there: https://codeberg.org/maevi/rimworld-mods/src/branch/main/alien-worlds

name: Asimov
author: Neronix17
description: After several human sacrifices and a pact made with a crossroads demon I bring to you a foundation mod. Not a framework but a foundation, frameworks have no content built into it, this does, so it's a foundation to build on. No more having half a dozen different batteries/power cells/chargepacks or charging platforms/ports/sockets/plugs to fuel your varied autonomous worker collective from several mods, now just one set usable by any and all that opt to do so. The only cost is a small fragment of your soul and maybe a moment of time configuring it. If you don't need any of that content though, it won't be visible on the player end outside of messing with DevMode tools. The primary purpose of this is for the creation of Automatons (autonomous working "animals" and non-living pawns like robots, golems, zombies, etc). [b]Automatons[/b] To be clear, since people would ask and probably will anyway because y'all have literacy issues and fail to read the most basic descriptions, this does not include any Automatons, it is a tool for modders to create them without having to create an entire energy need and functionality for them. These Automatons are typically just simple robots tasked with one or two jobs, like Biotech mechanoids in a way, unlike those however the player has control over the jobs they can currently do with a simple set of toggles, and they don't have any of the Mechanitor mechanics involved. [b]User Features:[/b] You will not see these in-game if there is nothing capable of using them installed. If you have a mod using this foundation just to create golems without an energy need then these things will not be enabled, it's that simple. - Charging Ports - Wall mounted ports where Automatons can charge directly from, they'll take a moment just like you fleshy meatsacks do when eating but without the mess and disgusting sounds. - Wireless Power - There are both mid and late game methods for wireless power, Automatons will not seek it out however so you'll just have to be strategic with your placement. - Chargepacks - Food packets for Automatons essentially. They'll leave behind empty chargepacks which can be recharged in a Chargepack Recharger. - Recharger - Recharges chargepacks, automated so does not require pawns to work at the building, just needs empty packs brought to it and it'll dispense charged ones over time. Simple and cost effective. [b]Modder Features:[/b] - Easy creation of new Automatons that can function fully on their own. - Automatons can be drafted, but only if set up to be able to do so, they can even equip weapons if set up to be able to do so. - Individual colour mask selections, repaint Automatons whatever colour you want and individually, and use two different colours for even more visual customisation. - Control over which charging methods they can use, users can still override in the settings if they prefer so they don't have to come to you about it, you just decide the defaults. - Can also be used to handle animals/golems/zombies/etc capable of doing jobs too, the energy need is not a mandatory component and associated buildings/items are hidden when not needed! - Lightweight race framework for handling non-human pawns, nowhere near as flexible as Humanoid Alien Races as it's mostly just to have pawns not be treated as 'living' but if you only need some small changes and explicitly no gene mechanics on the race, this does the job! [b]FAQ[/b] [list][*][b]Why does a framework have CONTENT?[/b] [i]If you install this and nothing else, you should not be able to SEE that content outside of developer options. If a building isn't able to be used by any Automatons loaded, it will be hidden from the Architect menu, same goes for Chargepack recipes and charger, they'll all be disabled if you do not need them.[/i] [*][b]Why use this?[/b] [i]If you don't want to you don't have to. Unless you want to use a mod that needs it to function, in which case I guess you do have to.[/i] [*][b]Does this alter how Biotech mechanoids work?[/b] [i]Not without a patch mod specifically for doing so, no. I actively avoided even looking at Biotech's mechanoids so it would not require the DLC, even though you definitely should get the Biotech DLC regardless, it's good.[/i] [*][b]Why "Asimov"?[/b] [i]After Isaac Asimov, the famous writer that came up with the three laws of robotics. I'm not creative at coming up with good names for things so I thought that was as good as anything else and more unique than "Robot Framework".[/i] [*][b]Why not use Humanoid Alien Races for races?[/b] [i]No particular reason not to, in fact for anyone else I'd freely encourage them to if it suits their needs better. If you want to know details why as a modder, I suggest examining the differences yourself, you know what you want to make and I don't, so you'll know better which is more useful to you.[/i][/list]

However please keep in mind none of the gene stuff will work without Biotech, and the precept thought workers will usually require both Biotech and Ideology. [img]https://i.imgur.com/0gYfTPj.png[/img] - Stats that alter deathrest, pregnancy, and blood recovery speeds. - Create basic resource genes like Hemogen using just xml - Locking equipment based on genes, xenotypes, and hediffs, using required or forbidden options. - Locking genes and xenotypes to only use certain equipment, or have certain equipment forbidden. - Create thoughts that check for trees similar to the Trees Desired precept. - Create mood curves based on how many people are in the colony. - Create hediffs that damage and even completely remove specific parts. - Other stuff I'm sure. [url=https://github.com/KonradHeinser/EBSGFramework/wiki/Updates]To read about past updates and the next major update (if I'm presently working on it), take a look at the updates page on the wiki.[/url] [img]https://i.imgur.com/o3vWOw6.png[/img] - CE has marked some of the mods that depend on this framework as compatible, so I assume most of this framework is compatible. - HAR may not be compatible with the fertility curve. Awaiting large scale input from community. - No other issues are known at the moment. If you encounter a bug, please make sure you force Steam to redownload this framework and verify file integrity to ensure Steam has not been skipping updates again. If the issue persists, feel free to make the report below, but if there are errors or warnings in your log, send the entire log rather than just that specific bit as those individual bits can often be missing a lot of required context. [img]https://i.imgur.com/TdjmzJr.png[/img] [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/Sovereign484854/myworkshopfiles/]Sovereign[/url] has helped come up with several of the ideas in the mod, and, more importantly, has helped me with art stuff to compensate for my inability to do art stuff. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561199377833097/myworkshopfiles/]The preview and mod icon were made by Elseud[/url] SmartKar allowed me to take a bunch of stuff from the Athena Framework [url=https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198159316632/myworkshopfiles/?appid=294100]Matsay[/url] helped create some of the comps in this framework If you're interested in downloading manually, casually looking at the code, or taking a look at its functions to use in your own mods, click the Github link. While I do encourage looking at the C# if you want an example on how to do something, you do NOT have permission to just copy my code into your own mod without attribution. If you want to use something directly from this, it's generally better to just make this mod a dependency. In the event that I unexpectedly completely vanish for some reason, this and all my other mods use the [url=https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/]CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license[/url] as normal. As you can imagine for big mod lists this leads to tons of missing linkable connections and endless XML patches. Linkable Groups introduces a central framework that handles linkables in a clean, modular way. Instead of every building having to list every possible facility, linkables are organized into groups, like "Cooking" or "Smithy". But this is not just a naked framework. Can I use this? Certainly, respect the license and you may use any feature to any extent you desire. Can I request a feature? Not really, the framework is mostly for personal use, with free usage rights for everyone else. If you have a feature you'd like to see, feel free to fork and provide a pull request for me to merge, but please don't just ask for features. Does this work in 1.X? Maybe. name: 1trickPwnyta's Anomaly Patch
author: 1trickPwnyta
description: This mod makes a handful of small tweaks to the Anomaly DLC that are intended to make the game a bit more enjoyable without changing the gameplay too much. Each tweak can be toggled on or off in the mod settings. <size=18px><color=#5aa9d6>Anomaly incidents</color></size> • Pawn silhouettes (when zoomed out) are no longer hidden in unnatural darkness. • Death pall resurrection messages no longer make a noise so you won't get inundated with beeps during death palls. Don't worry - you'll still see the message, and you'll still hear the gross corpsey sound of them resurrecting nearby. • Pit gates don't cause horror music to play unless you go into them, and horror music stops when you leave, and enemies in the undercave don't cause combat music to play unless you're in there with them, and combat music stops when you leave. • When returning from the labyrinth created by a warped obelisk, any items transferred to your home map will be set to forbidden unless they appear in the home zone. • Bug fix: Certain Anomaly incidents (Unnatural darkness, Sightstealer arrival) can spawn on a different colony map than the one whose wealth was used to generate their threat points. <size=18px><color=#5aa9d6>Study, suppression, and containment</color></size> • Enables study and suppression of entities, including non-living entities such as obelisks, by default • Pawns will not study entities if no Anomaly research project is active and studying the entity provides no other benefits (like learning about obelisks or how to destroy the golden cube) • Colonists are no longer forced to finish suppressing obelisks in order to take breaks (useful for pawns with lower psychic sensitivity). • When multiple obelisks reach dangerous (90%) activity levels, the alert on the right side of the screen will show the highest activity level instead of showing no acitivty level. • Selecting multiple bioferrite harvesters shows the total amount of bioferrite contained (and increase per day) in all of them • The "extract bioferrite" option is enabled automatically when capturing entities if there is no attached bioferrite extractor. • When working, colonists will try to find a spot to stand in that doesn't hold a containment cell or prison door open if possible. This way they won't compromise entity containment while building flooring etc. in a containment cell or allow a prisoner to escape. • Holding platforms needed alert is disabled. <size=18px><color=#5aa9d6>Psychic rituals</color></size> • The psychic ritual dialog sorts pawns by psychic sensitivity or by age, at your option. • Colonists will adhere to zone restrictions while gathering offerings for psychic rituals and while moving to the psychic ritual spot. • Suppresses the "Colonist needs rescue" alert for targets of psychic rituals • Bug fix: Void provocation rituals can spawn devourer water assaults on maps with no valid water to spawn from, resulting in the ritual doing nothing <size=18px><color=#5aa9d6>Dark entities</color></size> • Corpses initially spawned around the void monolith are forbidden by default. • Disables "Disturbing vision" letter because it doesn't actually do anything other than remind you that the monolith exists. • Certain entity stats are no longer hidden (nociosphere, metalhorror, revenant). • Ghouls can hunt prey just like your animals can. • Caravan dialog food auto selection prioritizes twisted meat for ghouls and carniverous animals, then human/insect meat, then other meat. • Dead ghouls remain in the colonist bar until buried/destroyed, just like colonists do. Ghouls are also shown in the caravan colonist bar. • Creepjoiners and non-creepjoiners can now form romantic relationships with each other. • Bug fix: Female creepjoiners use male body type <size=18px><color=#5aa9d6>Miscellaneous</color></size> • The "need warm clothes" alert on the right side of the screen won't show up if you have a powered and fueled atmospheric heater. • Prevents inhumanized pawns from having any personal feelings (mood bonuses/penalties) about their pregnancies • Pawns will avoid wearing dread leather if they don't like it ________________________________________________ <size=18px><color=#5aa9d6>Updates</color></size> 04/29/2026: Stop enabling bioferrite extraction by default once bioferrite harvester research is unlocked 11/29/2025: Added option to enable bioferrite extraction by default on contained entities 11/06/2025: Split doorway work option into two options: one for containment cells, one for prisons 10/14/2025: Add Sightstealer arrival event to bug fix for incidents spawning on the wrong map 08/08/2025: Fixed bugs with containment/prison door feature. 06/12/2025: Updated to 1.6, updated settings UI 03/12/2025: Add a few new tweaks, make creepjoiner love feature require restart when changing to deal with mod compatibility issues 01/29/2025: Fix incompatibility with Big and Small Framework 01/28/2025: Show ghouls in the colonist bar any time a colonist would be, allow creepjoiners to love non-creepjoiners, fix unnatural darkness void provocation bug, disable disturbing visions, adjust ghoul hunting logic 12/15/2024: Fix bug where archonexus structures are study-enabled by default 10/10/2024: Remove friendly shambler in schedule tab bug fix (fixed in vanilla now) 07/09/2024: Fix friendly shambler in schedule tab bug for human shamblers too! 07/09/2024: Sort prisoners and downed colonists last in psychic ritual dialogs, fix friendly shambler in schedule tab bug 06/10/2024: Added many new tweaks, added settings to toggle each tweak 05/08/2024: Fixed world map bug when selecting any tile on starting world map screen, or selecting any tile while multiple bioferrite harvesters are selected <size=18px><color=#5aa9d6>Credits</color></size> • Mod icon: twitter.com/mouse_draws

Each tweak can be toggled on or off in the mod settings. <size=18px><color=#5aa9d6>Children</color></size> • The Child Labor: Encouraged precept requires children to be scheduled for at least 4 consecutive hours of work instead of requiring no scheduled recreation, since children don't recreate anyway. • The text for the right-click command "Prioritize growing growth vat" is changed to "Prioritize loading growth vat". • Children will not automatically gain a weird nickname like "Man" or "Dude" or "Bicep" at growth moments. • Children are called by their first names by default, instead of sometimes going by their last names. • Growth moment dialog trait/passion choices are colored. This adds a checkbox to the health tab. • No more message spam when extracting hemogen from a prisoner of a hostile faction. • No more message spam when wastepacks deteriorate outside of the home area. ________________________________________________ <size=18px><color=#5aa9d6>Updates</color></size> 07/06/2026: Fix startup error when Achtung! is enabled 04/28/2026: Fix bug with growth dialog UI not showing proper passion skill name color when conflicting with a poor aptitude gene 04/22/2026: Add more error checking 01/18/2026: Add ability to hemogen farm any colonist, add kill thirst satisfaction for any melee combat, show mech charge level in colonist bar instead of mood, remove fixes/features that have since been added in vanilla, bug fixes with pawn names and mechanitor mechs. 10/07/2025: Fix errors when pawn nicknames are handled outside gameplay 09/10/2025: Fix children first name feature 06/16/2025: Update to 1.6, remove features now vanilla 05/21/2025: Fix conflict with Pawn Name Variety, fix pawn name errors when reloading saves 04/13/2025: Fix conflict with Character Editor <size=18px><color=#5aa9d6>Credits</color></size> • Mod icon: twitter.com/mouse_draws • Positive thoughts: Viewers like you

name: Delmain Tweaks - Role Apparel
author: Delmain
description: A relatively simple mod that enables the player to customize which clothing pieces are available to be assigned to any given Ideology role. This applies to the player's faction, as well as all factions that generate in the world. This mod allows you to go into the mod's settings and choose, on a per-role basis, which apparel items are available in the drop-down list of requirements for that role in the Ideology set-up screen. If you want your leader to request to wear Cataphract Armor, you can do that. If you want your melee specialist to demand that they be given a cowboy hat, you can do that, too. It should support all modded apparel AND modded ideology roles, but please contact me if you find something that doesn't work as expected. There are some limitations at this time, mainly that groups of items filling a single requirement (such as the Cape/Eltex Cape, or Crown/Stellic Crown) must be hand-coded to be supported. If there is a mod that adds an entire category of clothing that you would like supported, leave a comment in the Requests thread and I will take a look when I am able. An important thing to note here, as with other mods that perform a similar action, this WILL slow down your world generation. Every faction that generates during WorldGen will try to make combinations of roles with all the apparel that is available to them, so the slowdown can get extreme if you enable a great many options for each role. I highly recommend using the default options for each role and only enabling the one or two additional items that you want to use for your own ideology, as opposed to enabling all of the ones that sound fun. If you want to change them up entirely, you are free to do so, but be warned that WorldGen will get slow!

name: Grenade Sacrifice
author: Legator
description: Adds a "Pull Pin" gizmo to any drafted colonist holding a grenade. Pull the pin, the grenade's own fuse starts hissing, and a few seconds later it detonates centered on the pawn - wherever they ran to in the meantime. The blast uses the grenade's own explosion stats, and the grenade is consumed. The pin cannot be put back in, and the grenade is locked in the pawn's grip until it detonates - no dropping, stripping or weapon-swapping a live grenade. A confirmation dialog guards against misclicks (toggleable in mod settings). RimWorld Multiplayer is supported via the Multiplayer API. Only pawns with the hands and brains for it can pull a pin: humans, sapient humanoid androids (Android Tiers) and weapon-wielding automatroids and synthroids (The Dead Man's Switch). Animals, hauler bots and cargo drones (Misc. Robots, Project RimFactory - Drones, Machines of War) never get the gizmo, even when carrying a grenade. Explicitly compatible with: - Vanilla Weapons Expanded - Grenades - Grenade Variety for Combat Extended - More Useful Grenade (frag, thermite and flashbang only - gadgets and C4 have no pin to pull) Works automatically with most modded grenades: any equippable weapon in the Grenades category with an exploding projectile gets the gizmo. Molotovs are excluded (there is no pin on a bottle). Mod authors can opt in or out with a simple PullPinExtension patch (weapons) or PullPinRaceExtension patch (races).

name: Hard Vacuum
author: PeteTimesSix
description: 10 seconds of useful conciousness, 30 seconds until severe long term damage, 90 seconds until death. -NASA, probably Modifies Odyssey's vacuum exposure mechanics to be more true to life. Short term exposure will no longer result in instant vacuum burns. Longer exposure is no longer instantly lethal upon hitting 100%, but vacuum burns accumulate much faster and can also affect soft tissue (eyes, tongue, nasal cavity, lungs and stomach), potentially destroying the affected body part entirely. Additionally, severe exposure to vacuum will also result in delayed-onset decompression sickness.

name: I Know Where You Sleep
author: Harmonea
description: A small mod that allows a pawn to attempt to execute any unconscious or sleeping target. To use it, draft a pawn capable of violence, right click any sleeping target, and select the relevant menu option. - New in v1.1: Now also adds execution of downed (but not unconscious) targets if a mod that adds that option (i.e. Allow Tool) is not already loaded. Humanlikes Humanlike targets will be assassinated in one shot. If the target is friendly, you'll have to hold shift to enable the option, and your assassin will receive guilt. Why would you assassinate a friendly target, you ask? I'm a strong believer in the player actively crafting the story alongside Cassandra and co., and in certain scenarios, having a true villain in your group just fits. Animals Animals of body size 1 or lower will be slaughtered in one shot. For balance purposes, any animal larger than body size 1 will receive heavy damage to a critical part but not die immediately; the slaughterer will have to face an increased revenge chance (by 50%) as retaliation for the surprise attack. I don't recommend a solo hunter using this on e.g. Thrumbos and Megasloths. Once the bodysize gets that high, the initial attack is not enough to bleed them out; you'll just be making them mad, and you'll be starting within easy reach of them showing you exactly how mad. Bonded animals will require the player to hold shift. The bond will suppress revenge chance and cause guilt to apply, as well as the usual consequences for death of a bonded animal. Others? This mod is built on the vanilla execute/slaughter calls, so I don't expect it to function on other targets that can't typically be the target of such actions (like mechanoids). It's not a bug, and I have no plans to change this. That said, my test against dormant mechanoids made me giggle, so I left the menu option in. Performance? Should have no more impact on performance than vanilla executions. Mod recommendations [list] [*] Custom Guilt Duration - I left all the guilt durations at the default of one day specifically because this mod exists. Realistically, your stabbypawn should face pretty severe consequences, but that's your story to tell. [*] Grim Reality (reported working in 1.5) - to make vanilla death thoughts more impactful. I was originally going to add some fear thoughts to the colonists to express discomfort about violence against their own, but I didn't like balancing that part and scrapped it. Grim Reality will help cover that gap. [*] BoomMod Expanded if you plan to use this against any exploding animals. [/list] This mod is distributed under the MIT License.

name: Ideology: More Precepts
author: llunak
description: This mod provides additional precepts for ideoligions in the Ideology DLC. This is work in progress, more are planned. Precepts: - Alcohol - If Alcohol precept is set, it controls alcohol usage instead of the more generic DrugUse precept. - Comfort - Added values that make pawns want comfortable furniture sleeping and sitting, pawns will try harder to find suitable furniture, very demanding pawns may refuse to use facilities that do not have sufficient furniture. - Compassion - Allied, not hostile, not guilty or all incapacitated pawns should not be left to die helplessly. - Drug posession - Pawns will dislike presence and trading of hard, social (non-alcohol) or all non-medical drugs. - Elderly - Old people may be viewed with respect or contempt. Results in mood and social buffs and debuffs. When elders are respected, too young pawns are considered inexperienced for important roles. - Newcomer attitude - Pawns may be excited when new pawns join the colony (even temporarily) but will get bored if that does not happen for a while, or will be distrustful of newcomers, especially if they walk around the colony armed. - Nomadism - Pawns will dislike or want to abandon their settlement. - Superstition - Strong, mild or contempt. Superstitious pawns will get mood changes from some events, pawns with contempt will dislike others being superstitious. - Taking from downed - Pawns will dislike stripping incapacitated pawns in order to take their equipment. - Traps - Use of traps may be disapproved. Analogous to the 'Autonomous weapons' precept, but for traps. - Violence - Harming other people, ranging from pacifists that refuse to harm others to essential that makes pawns unhappy after a while of no violence. Includes a defense-only option. Memes: - Nomadism - Hight impact, requires Nomadism:Essential or Nomadism:Wanted. Unlocks animal specialist role. - Pacifism - High impact, requires Violence:Pacifism or Violence:Horrible. Rituals: - Animal duel - Like gladiator duel, but one of the participants is an animal. - Drinking party - A party focused on drinking, pawns will gather and drink what drinks are available and allowed. - Feast - A party focused on eating meals, pawns will gather and eat available meals. - Funeral pyre - An alternative to funeral, body is burned on a pyre. Ritual outcomes: - Raid - Colony may get raided after a noticeable ritual (drum party, sacrificing a prisoner or symbol burning). Chance is higher for Violence:Wanted or Violence:Essential precepts. - Venerated animals wander in - Like farm animals wandering in outcome, but for venerated animals. GitHub: https://github.com/llunak/rimworld-moreprecepts The mod is updated only for the latest RimWorld version, content for older versions is kept but not updated anymore.

name: Mechanoid Execution
author: np
description: [EN] Mechanoids have remembered that they are killing machines. Any humans lying on the ground must be disposed of immediately. This mod allows mechanoids to automatically deliver a "finishing blow" to downed enemies. During combat,mechanoids focus on the enemies in front of them, but once there are no threats nearby, they will automatically go around executing nearby downed enemies. Once they reach the target, they will ensure death within a few seconds. Because they prioritize active threats during combat, they will not leave themselves vulnerable by attempting unreasonable executions. Since there is a risk of being killed even after being downed, it can be used as a high-difficulty mod (probably). Update: Added the ability to change the execution functionality of friendly Mechanoids in the settings. [JA] メカノイドは、自分が殺戮兵器だったのを思い出しました！ 倒れている人間が居たら、そいつは即座に処分すべきです。 メカノイドが、倒れた敵に自動で「とどめを刺す」ようになるModです。 戦闘中、メカノイドは目の前の敵を倒すことに集中しますが、周囲に脅威がいなくなると、近くのダウンしている敵を自動的に処刑して回るようになります。 対象に到着すると、数秒で確実に死亡させます。 戦闘中の脅威を優先するため、無理な処刑を行って隙を晒すことはありません。 ダウンしても助ける前に殺される可能性があるので高難易度化Modとして使えます。(多分) 更新： 味方のメカノイドの処刑機能を設定から変更できるようになりました。

name: New Ritual Reward
author: Gilith
description: [h1]What does it do?[/h1] This mod adds a large number of possible rewards to your rituals (21 for vanilla and DLC games, 3 for mods). Your raider ideology rituals can finally detect innocent miners and lumberjacks. More of a mercenary or hero type? Your rituals will guide you toward enemy camps, attract mechanoid clusters around your colony, and even intercept distress calls. Explorers or adventurers? You can dance or chat your way into discovering traces of ancient shrines, warehouses and stockpiles at landmarks, unearth sites containing gravcores on land or in space, and even distant item stashes. [h2]New rewards list[/h2] This mod follows a simple logic regarding the sites that appear on the world map: for each new reward, it mimics the behavior of the base reward "Discover Ancient Complex." A site of the type defined by your reward will appear a few hours or days' travel away from your colony. Discover worksite : a worksite will spawn near your colony in the world map. Discover item stash : an item stash will spawn near your colony in the world map. Discover enemy camp : an enemy camp (the one looking like a tower) will spawn near your colony in the world map. Intercept Distress Call (requires Anomaly) : you will intercept a distress call from a site near your colony on the world map. Discover ancient structure (requires Odyssey) : a warehouse or a stockpile, from the landmark system, will spawn around your colony in the world map. Discover ancient shrine : a special site will appear on the world map near your colony. Inside, you will find one or two ancient dangers. Alert mechanoid cluster - world map (requires Royalty) : a mechanoid cluster of a random nature (EMP, smoke machine, downer, etc.) will spawn near your colony in the world map. Alert mechanoid cluster - current map (requires Royalty) : a mechanoid combat cluster will land directly on your current map. Discover ancient gravcore structure (requires Odyssey) : a site related to gravcore discovery will spawn in the world map. It could be any of them: stockpiles, ancient reactor. Only the terrestrial ones. Discover orbital structure (requires Odyssey) : a site related to gravcore discovery will spawn. Only the ones in outer space. Discover ancient mercenaries (requires Odyssey) : you will discover the location of a company of mercenaries. Survivor drop pod : a survivor will crash in a transport pod near your colony. You can configure which types (factionless, non-hostile, hostile) in the settings. Call caravan trader : a caravan trader will visit your colony. Call orbital trader : a trade ship will pass near your colony. Requires a working comms console. Communion : the social bonds among ritual participants will grow stronger for 15 days. Random quest : a random quest will be offered to you. Human raid : hostile humanoids will attack your colony. Mechanoid raid : mechanoids will attack your colony. Insectoid raid : a horde of insects will attack your colony. Compatible with VFE Insectoids 2 genelines. Anomaly raid (requires Anomaly) : an occult threat will strike your colony (shamblers, gorehulks, chimeras, hate chanters, or cultists). Manhunter pack : a pack of man-hunting beasts will attack your colony. Infestation : giant insects will tunnel into your base and emerge inside. Summon insect lair (requires our mod: Insect Lair Incident) : an insect lair will spawn somewhere inside your current colony map. Discover biolab (requires the mod: Alpha Genes) : you will discover a biolab near your colony in the world map. [h1]Do you want to know more?[/h1] All rewards can be enabled or disabled in the settings menu to avoid cluttering the ideology window. Sites that normally contain gravcores can be configured to offer an alternative reward. Vanilla quests remain untouched. You can also disable specific sites to prevent them from being selected. If you have other ideas for possible rewards, or other mods to integrate, feel free to suggest them in the comments. We promise nothing, but who knows? [h1]Compatibility[/h1] This mod is not compatible with our other mod New Reward for Rituals: Worksite (it is included in this one). This mod only adds rewards to rituals. We have not encountered any incompatibility during our tests, even on a run with a long mod list (300+). [h1]Performance[/h1] No impact. [h1]Savegame compatible[/h1] Can be added to an existing save without issues. During our tests, we were able to remove the mod even with rituals containing one of our new rewards. You will just need to re-edit your ritual to give it a vanilla reward.

name: No More Lethal Damage Threshold
author: Jdalt40
description: Did you know pawns can only have a total of 150 damage across all body parts before the pawn dies for no reason? This mod fixes that by telling ShouldBeDeadFromLethalDamageThreshold to go **** itself! Should be compatible with all mods and is save compatible!

name: Not My Fault
author: Vesper
description: Picture this - You get a new notification, a trade a caravan! How exciting! Except... No, guys, please don't walk through the cave filled to the brim with angry genetically engineered insects... Aaaand your visitors are all dead. And now their faction hates you for some reason. "Not My Fault" is a simple mod. It removes the -5 penalty you get from visitors dying on your map tile due to events you had no control over. No more faction reputation loss because your visitors picked a fight with a wild manhunting grizzly bear. Or perhaps they lit themselves on fire because they somehow missed the fact that a dry thunderstorm turned your rice fields into a raging inferno. Or maybe one of their own has a mental break and decides to go on a grenade throwing spree. Either way, you wouldn't have been penalized if this happened on the tile directly adjacent to your map. Why should you be punished for it now? It should be noted that this mod does NOT remove penalties for intentionally harming visitors. That being said, this is still not a "balanced" mod in that there are definitely ways to exploit this system. Up to you how you would like to use it. Credit: Programmer: Vesper Commissioner: Foxy Carter Compatibility: As the mod replaces the -5 faction penalty in the vanilla source code with 0, there should be no issues with mod compatibility. If any bugs are found, please let me know in the comments!

name: Nudge Me - Pathfinding Fix
author: Tascani
description: Nudge Me is a targeted bug-fix mod for melee combat pathing. As of RimWorld 1.6, pawns can get stuck while attacking enemies. Pawns may idle behind other pawns even when a valid path to the target exists. This can occur even with just two pawns attacking a single enemy. The mod detects pawns that become stuck during melee engagement. When a pawn is stuck, it nudges the pawn to forget its current path. The game then generates a new path. The mod runs for all pawns that are not player-faction humanlikes. Your colonists will never be nudged or have their paths reset. The biggest benefit is visible for released animals, manhunter packs, and enemy melee fighters.

author: Usagirei

name: Punch Button
author: Fuu Chan
description: An unarmed prisoner is escaping! Quick, slice their limbs off with a plasmasword! I'm sure we all wish we could simply order colonists to punch without unequipping them (or can't even unequip if they have implanted weapons). So here's a punch button! Primary Changes Adds a punch button that appears while colonists are drafted, which forces them to only use unarmed attacks (won't use implant weapons like elbow blades either)! Compatibility *Near 0% performance impact (0.001ms in Dub's Performance Analyzer to draw the button when a pawn is selected). *Safe to add and remove mid-game. *Independent, isolated, and minimal in scope, with no modifications to vanilla behavior/code required: This simply uses the same code as social fighting, so it should be compatible with nearly every mod, will leave no permanent changes to your saved game, and will not brick your game. *Confirmed compatible with Combat Extended, Vanilla Expanded series, Alpha series, Dubs series, Simple Sidearms, and hundreds more. Updates ~3.0 update: Now compatible with 1.5! ~2.02 update: Added priority so punches are always preferred over headbutting and biting. ~2.01 update: Removed punch button from appearing on player controlled mechanoids (They're not capable of punching). ~2.0 update: Now compatible with 1.4! Github Link: https://github.com/tenguin/Rimworld_PunchAttack Credits to: sakino_shingetu, Inugami Korone, and Princess Connect: ReDive for the art sources used in the thumbnail and tanosii_chan for the upvote animation! Give them a visit!

name: Raiders Will Never Be Satisfied
author: STEVESCRIGGINS
description: Raiders will patrol around your base making sure that the rest of the survivors bleed out or starve until they get bored (10 to 15 hours, same as vanilla). Afterwards, they'll kidnap anyone who's still alive and steal anything not nailed into the ground. V3 Update: Raiders now have their own "steal" function which lets them pick up multiple items at once . If nothing of value is available, raiders will carry up dead comrades and colonists away from the map to honour/eat them. Performance was improved from V2 (0.031ms during post raid scavengin').

name: Research-Based Raids Difficulty
author: Leo39994
description: In vanilla RimWorld, "Wealth Management" often feels like a tedious chore. Why should a colony be punished for having a gold statue in the dining room, while a squad armed with Charge Rifles and Power Armor gets a free pass just because they sleep on the floor? It targets players who find the vanilla scaling nonsensical or the endgame too easy. By linking raids to your Research, you can no longer "hide" your strength by staying poor. Hostile factions are now more threatened by your actual capabilities than your furniture. If you want the best tech, you'd better be ready to defend it.
