name: Zealot Specialist
author: Sierra's Online Entertainments
description: Adds the Zealot specialist role to the Proselytizer and Loyalist memes. Zealots have even less certainty loss than other specialists, convert with more power and frequency, and have a lower mental break threshold. They can also use the Holy Fervour ability which drives colonists into a berserk trance, increasing their melee prowess but losing control.

name: 1trickPwnyta's Ideology Patch
author: 1trickPwnyta
description: This mod makes a handful of small tweaks to the Ideology DLC that are intended to make the game a bit more enjoyable without changing the gameplay too much. Each tweak can be toggled on or off in the mod settings. <size=18px><color=#5aa9d6>Ideology Memes and Precepts</color></size> • Sets the default physical love precept to free so that people can have premarital sex like they did before Ideology. • Sets the default female clothing requirement for ideologies to groin covering only, as it is for men. • Changes the nudity precept "Pants at most" to "Pants only", which does the same thing but is worded correctly. • Ranchers no longer get upset about planting "human food crops". They already get a mood penalty for eating vegetables; they don't need another one just for planting them. Besides, who says you're planting them in order to eat them? Maybe you just want to make chemfuel. Or you want to have food onhand that you can use to train your animals. • Adds the Corpses: Don't Care precept to the Bloodfeeding meme (because cannibalism). • Disables the darkness mood debuff for the Tunneler meme (specifically the Fungus: Preferred precept, because if you like fungus you shouldn't hate planting it). • Newly built lights default to darklight setting if the player's primary ideology prefers darklight. • Starting research that unlocks things that "require memes that none of your people believe" no longer triggers a pop-up unless ALL of the unlocked things require such memes. In other words, you won't be bothered if there's anything that you CAN build. <size=18px><color=#5aa9d6>Slaves</color></size> • Slaves do not count as quest-related guests, ever. This fixes an issue where enslaving a quest-related guest, such as a refugee, prevents you from doing many things with them, such as sending them on caravans, extracting their genes, assigning them apparel policies, etc. • Slaves will begrudgingly put on human leather slave gear instead of running around naked, as long as it's allowed in their apparel policies. • Slaves can no longer run wild. <size=18px><color=#5aa9d6>Ideological Practices</color></size> • When you receive a letter for finishing converting a prisoner, the Jump to location link selects the prisoner that was converted rather than the person who did the converting. This makes it easier to select a new prisoner interaction such as Recruit. • When beginning a role change ritual, the role selected by default will be an unfilled role unless all roles are filled so you don't accidentally assign the moral guide role twice and make someone unhappy, for example. • Shows a message when an ideology ritual comes off cooldown so you don't forget to perform it again. • Brings back the "Look change desired" mechanic that mysteriously disappears with Biotech enabled. • Pawns with ideologies that prefer "negative" apparel such as blindfolds will now automatically wear that apparel anyway without being forced. <size=18px><color=#5aa9d6>Miscellaneous</color></size> • Gauranlen tree-connected pawns will no longer ignore their needs for hours at a time while pruning the tree. It's not like the tree is the golden cube. • Dryads no longer wander further from their tree than the building radius warning (12 tiles -> 7.9 tiles). This makes it more intuitive to build a wall around the tree just outside the warning radius to keep the dryads safe from raiders. • If your ideology has only one relic and you bring it with you to a new colony in the archonexus quest, it will not retrigger the "all relics collected" mood boost. • Corpses that spawn near archonexus structures are forbidden by default. • Faction relationship levels start inside their natural range, so you won't get annoyed by early-game messages telling you that some rough outlander faction relation has soured out of nowhere. • Spikecore plates and floor slabs are now paintable. ________________________________________________ <size=18px><color=#5aa9d6>Updates</color></size> 05/30/2026: Add null check when setting faction of a thing 02/11/2026: Fix performance issue with styling station UI 11/20/2025: Added compatibility patch for Humanoid Alien Race mod 08/27/2025: Fixed startup error when missing Biotech, fix bug with Genies (and others) always desiring a look change in certain conditions 07/03/2025: Fixed bug that causes faction relations to reset on game reload 06/14/2025: Categorized the settings UI 06/13/2025: Update to 1.6 12/12/2024: Fix the "Look change desired" mechanic with Biotech enabled and add negative apparel desire feature 10/22/2024: Add message for ideology ritual cooldown ending 08/02/2024: Remove patch from 1.4 version 06/25/2024: Use darklight by default in darkness ideologies 06/11/2024: Add settings to toggle each tweak 05/24/2024: Remove artificial enhancement calculation change. Genies were not bugged after all. 04/29/2024: Prevent pawns from pruning the tree non-stop while ignoring their own needs 04/09/2024: Stopped pawns against recreational drug use from using recreational drugs 03/20/2024: Update to 1.5 08/28/2023: Fixed prosthetics count bug 08/18/2023: Renamed Pants at most to Pants only 08/17/2023: Disabled the darkness thought for fungus: preferred, associate corpses: don't care with bloodfeeding meme 10/26/2022: Removed debugging messages from the dev log 10/26/2022: Added the default physical love precept <size=18px><color=#5aa9d6>Credits</color></size> • Mod icon: twitter.com/mouse_draws

name: 1trickPwnyta's Odyssey Patch
author: 1trickPwnyta
description: This mod makes a handful of small tweaks to the Odyssey DLC that are intended to make the game a bit more enjoyable without changing the gameplay too much. Each tweak can be toggled on or off in the mod settings. <size=18px><color=#5aa9d6>Space travel</color></size> • Gravship takeoff/landing cutscenes can be skipped by pressing Enter. • Gravship substructure can be set to shown always, never, or only while the grav engine is selected (setting to always makes planning easier). This can be set via grav engine or field extender gizmo. • While selected, build radii for gravship components is displayed separately instead of merged with other components. • In addition to substructure capacity used, inspect pane for grav engine now also shows how much capacity remains. • The radius for a gravship shield generator is shown while placing it, even when hovering over an invalid location. • Pawns can grab food, medicine, and drugs from a parked shuttle, just as they can from a pack animal. This can be toggled via shuttle gizmo. • You can park a shuttle anywhere it is possible to place a shuttle blueprint, so landing shuttles aren't blocked by wall lights, floor coverings, etc. • In space, vacuum intensity is shown in the room stat display and while holding the alt key. • Bug fix: When placing floors, it is erroneously possible to place them under gravship hulls, which has no benefit. • Bug fix: With pawn dot silhouettes enabled, they are erroneously shown during gravship cutscenes. • Bug fix: When landing a gravship, deathresting pawns pop out of their beds due to erroneous sunlight detection. • Bug fix: When landing a gravship and thus removing any map designators, buildings that were designated for flicking the power switch enter an erroneous state. • Bug fix: Saving the game with a shuttle that has been built but not yet interacted with causes an error. • Bug fix: Floors on top of substructure erroneously use the filth rate of the substructure instead. <size=18px><color=#5aa9d6>Fishing</color></size> • You can copy settings between fishing zones. • Pawns can stop fishing if their basic needs are unmet instead of literally fishing until they catch something or collapse. • No letters for fishing misses - if a pawn is hurt, just a message at the top, and if not hurt, no notification at all. <size=18px><color=#5aa9d6>Outfit Stands and Statues</color></size> • You can change the body type of outfit stands to other vanilla body types, such as female or hulk. This can be set via outfit stand gizmo. • Grouped outfit stands can be the target of bills (you can look for ingredients only in such a group, or you can take product specifically to such a group). • Pawns are allowed to remove items from outfit stands by default. You don't need to toggle it each time. • Removing items from outfit stands is no longer automatically disabled when a pawn is ordered to equip the outfit. • Items stored on outfit stands can't decrease beauty, but they can still increase it. • Allow hiding statues' headgear via gizmo. Default value is based on whether headgear is visible in the colonist bar. • Bug fix: Statues can erroneously reload with different dominant genes. For example, when reloading a save file, a statue of a pawn with the Neanderthal xenotype may reload as a standard, hulk, or fat body type. This fix does not apply to statues created before installing this mod. <size=18px><color=#5aa9d6>Miscellaneous</color></size> • Searches in the world view can now search all world tiles for map features instead of only occupied ones. This must be toggled specifically in each search box due to the performance impact. • Warnings when settling in orbit or in "dangerous" Odyssey biomes such as lava fields are disabled. Note that scarlands are always polluted and will therefore still warn about the pollution. ________________________________________________ <size=18px><color=#5aa9d6>Updates</color></size> 06/08/2026: Change patched method name according to new RimWorld update, to prevent startup errors 05/01/2026: Fix bugs with placing floors and with room stats gizmo 04/26/2026: Add additional space travel options 04/22/2026: Remove overhead for outfit stand groups when option is disabled, fix fishing bug with body mastery 04/01/2026: Remove an accidental fix meant for the unstable branch 04/01/2026: Make world search patch require restart to toggle for improved mod compatibility 01/07/2026: Fix bug where wild animals can grab food from shuttles 01/07/2026: Fix bug with shuttle food feature being disabled preventing pawns from feeding patients 11/02/2025: Add support for changing body type of modded outfit stands, add fix for substructure filth rate bug 11/01/2025: Allow parking shuttle in more places, fix shuttle save bug, reduce letter spam when fishing, hide statue headgear, fix statue xenotype bug 10/09/2025: Fix performance issue with scanning shuttles for supplies, enforce correct load order with Improved Map Search mod 10/08/2025: Add several new features under Space Travel and Miscellaneous 10/08/2025: Add additional null check when scanning shuttles for supplies 10/07/2025: Support modded shuttles for the shuttle supplies feature (as long as they use the Building_PassengerShuttle class) 10/02/2025: Fix startup errors with modded BodyTypeDefs <size=18px><color=#5aa9d6>Credits</color></size> • Mod icon: twitter.com/mouse_draws

name: Allied Ideologies
author: HeartRay
description: Allied Ideologies lets you set any two ideoligions as equals or with one dominant over the other, removing passive conversion, ideological conflicts, and opinion penalties between them — with its own mood effects for dominant/subordinate relationships.

name: ANDH - Animals Nuzzling Detects Horrors
author: latta
description: Give your cats and yorkies a chance! An animal nuzzling can reveal a metalhorror infection with a moderate chance. Bonded animals nuzzling their owners have much higher chance. Fully customizable. There must be at least one colonist near the metalhorror-infected colonist. The colonist must be able to hear or see. They must not be infected with a metalhorror, downed, or in a mental state.

name: Big Bed Buff
author: AmCh
description: If a pawn have a big bed to themselves they get a +4 mood buff.

name: Caravan Adventures
author: iforgotmysocks
description: Version 1.8.3 Caravan Adventures aims to transform traveling around the world into a fun adventure by providing new features to replace the annoying micromanagement, make traveling more fun and give you a sense of purpose doing so. Quick heads-up, about 25% of this mod's content is the Storyline, which requires Royalty. Everything else can be used without it, don't worry. Join us on Discord (https://discord.gg/KwaRubs2kx) All mod details available in the Mod's Wiki (https://github.com/iforgotmysocks/CaravanAdventures/wiki) Automatic Camp Setup * Settle on tiles by having your pawns set up a camp first, before you even get involved. * If you prepared and have enough spacer tent supplies, you will be able to stay in high quality camp sites, if not, your pawns will divert to make shift materials. * You pawns automatically build enough tents for your individual number of travelers and prisoners. Pawns also choose their tents based on their relationship. * Choose to either leave the bulk of most items strapped to your animals or create enough storage tents, so all your equipment is tugged away "safely". * Choose to pre-apply basic jobs, like creating a set of fresh clothes, butcher animals or grill some stakes * Leave the camp site immediately if you want to, just for the impatient ones Caravan forming / trading presets * Set up 3 presets in mod settings, that allow you to quickly select all items for travel, or create specific trade filters to select all you may want to sell at once. * More basic selection options for all items or none * Keep the automatic supplies disabled with a toggle, to avoid some lag when it's active every time you open up the dialog * Have selected pawns and items on the map automatically enabled in the caravan forming dialog Mechanoid Bounty * Initially part of the story, but also separately available * Hunt mechanoids to receive bounty credits with the faction that called out the bounty * Get assistance from said faction on any map you currently have pawns located (they can help engage hostile locations) * Hire veteran soldiers for a hefty large amount of bounty credits, which come with a lot of experience and you're able to choose some of their traits * Purchase valuable items in exchange for bounty credits * Improve relations to other factions in exchange for bounty credits * Buy bounty credits for a large amount of silver Immersion - Travel companions * Pawns start out disliking the newcomers due to uncertainty and some lack of trust * Pawns individually bond with each other over time which can turn the initial distrust into a true friendship Caravan Incidents * More smaller events that do not always have to end in a fight (currently only 1) Storyline (requires Royalty) * A storyline that gives you a reason to travel the world * Form a bond with a new faction sharing your troubles on a new world * Encounter a dangerous threat that endangers the entire world * Fight bosses to claim treasures, learn powerful spells and prevent the end of all living beings General travel support (disabled at default, enable in mod settings) * auto clean up settlement remains * Increase food and silver available for settlements to trade * Increase ancient shrine spawns and reward changes * Increase skill decay level from 10 to 15 * Enable a side bar icon allowing to remove letters (All categories can be enabled or disabled and further configured to your liking in the mod's settings) Credits Artwork: Artwork and the preview image generously provided by Shakesthespeare, thank you mate, u're awesome! Portal in Ancient master shrine by gecko-kobold Shortcut-button icon for forming/trade preset settings by Madman666 Sounds: Anima tree whisper by zapsplat (zapsplat_whispers.mp3) from https://www.zapsplat.com Earthquake by zatar (zatar_earthquake.mp3) https://freesound.org/people/zatar/sounds/514381/ slice1 by audione https://freesound.org/people/audione/sounds/52458/ slice2 by freefire66 https://freesound.org/people/freefire66/sounds/175949/ slice3 by TheBuilder15 https://freesound.org/people/TheBuilder15/sounds/434896/ slice4 by Aleks41 https://freesound.org/people/Aleks41/sounds/449552/ Translations: ChineseSimplified translation by MZM_GOW and ameki ChineseTraditional translation by MZM_GOW and ameki Korean translation by inbae SpanishLatin translation by Evilservant6 CE Patch done by DkPepper Thanks to the testers who helped to get this mod on the road!

name: Caravan Ghouls
author: Nepenthe
description: This mod allows Ghouls to carry items when forming a caravan, allowing you to use your friendly ghouls as pack animals. Don't forget to pack plenty of raw meat. This is done by removing the code that flags mutants as being unable to ever carry anything, allowing an adult-sized ghoul to carry 35kg of items just like the rest of your colonists. If combined with a mod that allows ghouls to pick up and use items like [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3223881925]Humanlike Ghoul[/url] this mod will prevent problems caused by the ghoul not being able to pick up items because of their weight. New in version 1.1: the mod now has a settings page in Options -> Mod options where you can decrease or increase the carrying capacity of ghouls. Note that if you you have Vanilla Expanded Framework installed you need to enable the VFE fix right below the slider to prevent the weight modification from being applied twice. Or leave it unchecked and max out the slider so your ghouls can carry 30 tonnes of cargo, I'm not going to stop you. This mod is safe to add/remove mid-save.

name: Caravan Mood Buff
author: Syrus
description: Adds mood buffs for caravans: - while traveling in a caravan - while on a map that is not player controlled, like event sites or battles - when a carvan site that is being visited has no more enemies - when winning a caravan battle All buffs are adjustable in the settings. Using this, caravans should be a bit less painful when it comes to constant mood breaks.

name: Cellcycle Acceleration
author: THERMAL CONTACT
description: This mod adds a new implant and a disease that accelerate a pawn's biological aging.

name: Cooking Specialist
author: Sierra's Online Entertainments
description: Adds the cooking specialist to the cannibal meme. The specialist as boosts to cooking speed, butchery speed and efficiency, as well as a reduced chance to poison food. The prepare feast ability grants nearby pawns increases to the same stats but to a lesser degree.

name: Food Poison Nerf
author: Geraldo Da Ravioli
description: This mod simply lessens the effects of food poison hediffs. Removes conciousness debuffs from all stages of hediff. I feel like the pain offset essentially serves the same role and the two together result in an absurdly powerfull debuff.

name: High Life Drug Cooking Speed
author: BigTortoise
description: Simple patch that makes the High Life precept now also increase drug cooking speed, not just drug sysnthesis speed.\nNow your colonists can not only make yayo faster, but also make smokeleaf and beer faster too!\nThe drug cooking speed stat scales off of cooking instead of intellectual skill and affects smokeleaf, beer, and psychite tea production.

name: Hospital
author: Adamas
description: Run a hospital: if you have this mod enabled (and settings allow you to receive patients) and you have plenty of medical beds patients will knock on your door asking for help with their disease, wounds or a surgery.

name: In Memoriam
author: Astryl
description: [h1]◆ In Memoriam ◆[/h1] The colony forgets its dead. The moment a colonist falls, the game discards them, their face, their history, who they were to everyone left behind. In Memoriam refuses to let them go. It opens a quiet, dark memorial from your main bar that remembers every soul the colony has lost, and writes each of them a eulogy! [h1]✦ A Memorial on the Main Bar[/h1] [list] [*][b]One click away[/b], a new memoriam button sits on the bottom bar. Open it any time to see everyone the colony has buried. [*][b]Captured at the moment of death[/b], name, exact date, cause, portrait, and every relationship are frozen the instant a pawn dies, so the record survives even after the game throws the body away. [*][b]Pin who matters[/b], pin any soul to keep them at the top of the list. [/list] [h1]✦ Every Soul Remembered[/h1] [list] [*][b]Colonists[/b], everyone who lived and died as part of your colony, including the prisoners you recruited into the fold. [*][b]Bonded animals[/b], the faithful companion who never left a colonist's side is remembered too, with their own story. [/list] [h1]✦ A Life, Written[/h1] Click any memorial to open their full remembrance, written like a eulogy by someone who knew them: [list] [*][b]Their story[/b], childhood and adulthood woven into one flowing passage, no dry stat sheets. [*][b]Character[/b], who they really were, their nature drawn from their traits in natural prose. [*][b]Life with the colony[/b], what they actually did: the fields they sowed, the meals they cooked, the stone they mined, the foes they felled. [*][b]Greatest achievement[/b], their single finest deed, picked from a lifetime of records and told as the story it deserves. [*][b]Remembered by[/b], every colonist they left behind, and how each one felt about them. [/list] Every memorial is generated uniquely, seeded by the pawn, so no two read the same. [h1]✦ Find Their Rest[/h1] Double-click any memorial and the camera flies to their remains, their grave, their sarcophagus, or the body where it fell, on any map. Say goodbye in person. [h1]✦ Plays Well With the Rim[/h1] Every integration is optional, detected at runtime, and silently does nothing when the other mod is absent. Each has its own toggle in settings. [list] [*][b]Karma & Reputation[/b]: a soul's moral standing colours the tone of their eulogy, from the quietly good to the honestly damned. [*][b]Pawn Chronicles[/b]: the narrative epithet history gave a pawn is woven into their remembrance. [*][b]Epitaph[/b]: the inscription carved on their grave is shown inside the memorial, and their eulogy closes on it. [*][b]Days Matter[/b]: a recurring remembrance day is added on each death anniversary, so the colony gathers to honour them every year. [*][b]Memorial Stele[/b]: the stele's view button opens this window instead of its own list. [/list] [h1]✦ Hold a Funeral[/h1] With Ideology active, a Hold Funeral button appears on any memorial whose remains can still be honoured, and begins the real funeral ritual for them, without hunting across the map for the grave. [h1]✦ Styled Like the Modern Suite[/h1] A flat, dark, card-based memorial that matches the rest of the Modern UI family, clean grayscale icons, slim auto-hiding gray scrollbars, dimmed portraits, and a quiet memorial-red accent. It reuses the suite's pin, info, and close icons so it feels like home. [h1]✦ The Modern Family[/h1] Shares its look and feel with [b]Modern Quest Menu[/b], [b]Modern Social Tab[/b], [b]Modern Bio Tab[/b], [b]Modern Needs Tab[/b], and the rest of the Modern UI suite, one consistent interface across your whole colony. [h1]✦ Requirements[/h1] [list] [*][b]Harmony[/b] (brrainz.harmony), the only dependency. [/list] Safe to add to an existing save at any time. Fully standalone. [hr][/hr] [i]Built for RimWorld 1.6. Lest the colony forget.[/i] [h3] My Quality Commitment:[/h3] [list] [*] [b]Fully Tested:[/b] Every feature and line of code has been thoroughly tested in-game to ensure it functions as intended and integrates smoothly. [*] [b]Active Support:[/b] I am fully committed to maintaining this mod. If you encounter any bugs, compatibility issues, or unintended behavior, please report them in the comments or a dedicated discussion thread. [*] [b]No Abandonware:[/b] I will actively patch, refine, and update this mod to keep it working and up to standard. [*] [b]No Coffee:[/b] I will never ask for donations for AI created / assisted mods. I share these in the hopes they spark joy for someone, making AI generated content and then begging for money that could go to artists and people more deserving is NOT responsible AI usage. [/list]

name: Initial Motivation
author: cedaro
description: Freeze joy need in the first three days after settled.

name: Lovin' Is Messy (and fun)
author: XandrMoro
description: Doin lovin is fun and recreational*, but sometimes leaves quite a cleanup to be done. If you dont have Dubs Hygiene, if will leave some love juice on the bed. If you do, it will also significantly increase hygiene need for participants - you can even oblige them to take a bath afterwards! *toggleable in settings

name: Medieval Drug Production
author: RizzlyBear
description: This mod changes Drug Production and other drugs (Penox, Flake/Yayo, Go-Juice, Wake-Up) to the Medieval tech level along with removing industrial requirements from the Drug Lab. I recommend using Farmable Neutroamine Medieval by JoeOwnage for maximum usability. Taking the responsibilty of medieval drugs from SirMashedPotato, thank you for your dedication please let me know if you have any issues with this.

name: Mood Matters
author: Imranfish
description: Makes various stats scale to the colonist's mood. Mood now slightly affects a colonist's general efficiency at all times, and so it is more important to manage. Low mood causes colonists to perform worse, but having high mood will give them an increase in efficiency. Fully customizable in the settings menu.

name: No Factory Floor Requirement
author: ferny
description: Removes the need for factory floors in factories.

name: Nuzzle Me
author: ChaoticEnrico
description: Allows you to command your colonists to pet animals to receive a nuzzle mood buff on demand.

name: Passive Research
author: komunre
description: Adds passive research so your colony won't stagnate. Research will get assigned amount of points (default 0.7) each simulation tick, making your research to progress without need to assign scientist. However, assigning someone to research, will speed up research, just as in normal vanilla. Count it as invisible friend who does research for you while you're busy. To change points amount (and so research speed), open my mod in mod settings menu.

name: Progression: Therapy
author: ferny
description: A mod that adds a therapy system, allowing colonists to improve their mood and composure.

name: RescueeJoinsPlus
author: Ogliss
description: Made for Rabbitt Rescuees shouldn't just join your colony, they should need permission... Now they do! They also provide more information about themselves, a summary and the option to view their infocard

name: Roo's Painting Expansion
author: Rooboid
description: • I’m an artist. Can I sculpt? Not for toffee. Can I paint? Well, not really. Nevertheless, what I’m saying is that your artist pawns should be capable of so much more than just sculpting. ------------------ • This mod adds in a new art form: paintings. Pawns can create either classical or modern paintings that draw from a unique pool of graphics and descriptions. • The mod works without any DLC or other mods. But when Ideology is installed, what your pawns paint depends entirely on your ideological style. • Research the arts, construct an easel and start painting. Decorate your art studio with cosmetic props, such as canvases and paint spills- or even construct an art cabinet to help catalyse your artist’s next masterpiece. Pawns can be decked out with artsy-fartsy apparel and tattoos too, because what’s art without getting to wear a fancy beret? • In total, with Ideology installed, there are over 40+ unique paintings your pawns can create. • Credits: - Freesounds for always being nice to my wallet when I need new sounds for mods. - Pixabay and Unplash, for royalty-free references and vectors used to make this mod. - Kyle T. Webster for his insanely amazing Photoshop brushes. - Zelan, for listening to my mod-related rants at 3am.

name: Scanning Thoughts
author: Leto
description: A little flavor mod that adds mood modifiers for boddy modders and purist after getting scanned. Body modders will get a small buff (+4) to there mood while body purist will hate (-4) to be scanned.

name: Slaughtering Meme
author: Rince
description: Unleash your inner cultist — the Slaughtering Meme mod lets your pawns embrace ritual sacrifice without guilt or penalty. Add a new meme to your ideology that fully legitimizes the execution of prisoners, colonists, and raiders alike. No more mood debuffs, no more moral questions — just blood, belief, and power. Perfect for dark religions, tribal blood cults, or anyone who thinks mercy is overrated.

name: Smarter Visitors
author: Mlie
description: [img]https://img.litet.net/logos/Self-Info.png[/img] Since visitors decide when they want to leave, it may not always happen at the best time. This mod checks the map when visitor-groups decide to leave and can delay this from happening. Included in the mod is also a Visitor-spot that lets you set a specific spot where your guests will hang around. This can make it easier to protect them from dangers. You can select what type of conditions should delay visitors from leaving in the mod-options: [list] [*] Dangers on the map. These are things like raids, maddened animals, toxic fallout etc. If present visitors will ask you if they could stay for another day. You have the option to deny this to make them leave anyway, approve it to make them try again in 24 hours or just ask again in an hour. [*] Health-issues. If any pawn in the group are suffering from health-issues that require medical rest, they will check again in an hour until all pawns are healthy enough to travel. [*] UV-sensitivity (Biotech gene). If any pawn have the intense UV-sensitivity gene, the group will delay their travel until the sun has gone down. This also includes Vampires from [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1187010034]Rim of Madness - Vampires[/url]. [/list] There is also an option for visitors getting negative thoughts if staying around longer than they planned. This increases for longer delays. You can also add extra food-rations to visitors inventories to make longer delays less of a problem. The mod works well with the excellent mod [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=753498552]Hospitality[/url] by Orion. The check for dangers on the map is adapted from the same check that hospitality-groups do when entering the map. The mod only triggers when visitors leave triggered by time, things like low temperatures or hostile actions are not affected. You can also ask visitors to leave, similar how to dismiss traders. If you have any other ideas on what visitors or other groups should check when leaving, please leave a comment and Ill try to implement it! name: The News
author: The Doctor
description: The News adds a living world to RimWorld - distant events arrive as radio intercepts, traveler reports, and diplomat dispatches, and they reach into your colony in ways you'll feel. When a war erupts nearby, trade routes close, prices spike, and colonists grow anxious. When plague hits a neighboring faction, their caravans carry sickness to your gates - and some survivors may beg to join your colony. Coups destabilize factions and can end wars. Alliances between former enemies cancel conflicts. Famines drive desperate wanderers toward any colony that will take them. Colonists passively react to the world around them: ongoing wars and plagues press on their mood every few days whether or not they've heard the formal report. A plague subsiding brings genuine relief. An alliance forming between hostile factions changes how every colonist feels about the news. Events span 20+ types: wars, coups, plagues, alliances, famines, espionage scandals, economic crises, technological breakthroughs, rising cults, pirate fleets, ancient site discoveries, environmental catastrophes, and more. Each has cause-specific narrative text, dedicated gameplay consequences, and colonist thought reactions. Build radio equipment, staff monitoring shifts, issue colony advisories, deploy diplomats, run covert operations, and shape what your colony knows and believes before distant crises arrive at your map.

name: Ritual Size Attenuation
author: Rachek128, Delmain
description: Continued for Rimworld 1.5 by Delmain Original details below: ==================================================================================== Automatically scales the required population count in rituals to accomodate different sized colonies. This will currently affect: [list] [*] Required participants in most rituals [*] Drums in drum parties (only ever scaled down) [/list] [h1]Features[/h1] A configurable population percentage in the mod settings controls how much of your population is necessary for rituals. Defaulting to 75%, this will allow a few colonists to miss a ritual in smaller colonies without suffering quality loss. By default, this mod will scale down ritual participation requirements for small colonies, but leave the default cap in place. So long as you have a large enough population to support the default requirements (taking the population percentage into account), ritual behavior will be identical to vanilla. However, there are a few options available for uncapping rituals in large colonies. [list] [*] Scaled: Scales up the ritual requirements in the same way they're scaled down. Larger colonies will require additional participants to maximize quality. [*] Bonus: Once the default cap is reached, adding extra participants will confer a configurable quality bonus, with diminishing returns. Hopelessly unbalanced, but someone might find a use for it. [/list] [h1]Compatibility[/h1] This is a tiny Harmony mod that patches a few ritual outcome comps to override how they calculate attendence requirements and quality, and should be compatible with most other mods. It doesn't add anything additional to the game or your save. You should be able to freely add or remove it at any time. Mods that add custom rituals may or may not be scaled depending on whether they use some sort of custom attendance tracking. [h1]Support[/h1] If you find any issues that I don't notice myself or have suggestions for additional features, open up a discussion and I'll take a look as soon as I have a chance.

name: Configurable Deconstruct Percentage
author: AmCh
description: In the vanilla game after 1.5, deconstructing/failing to construct/cancelling/destroying a building return 50%/50%/100%/25% of the used building materials, and cancelling an in-progress worktable item returns 75% of the materials, this mod makes them configurable (100%/80%/100%/50%/90% by default). There are many mods out there that do similar things, but to my knowledge, none else can configure all of these. You can also config to keep the last X of each resource (default X = 1), so you get to keep your Nano Structuring Chip when you deconstruct your Wastepack Atomizer. No reload required upon setting change as it takes effect immediately. There should be negligible impact on performance. Not all buildings are affected equally, some buildings have their own special destruction effect and some (such as walls) explicitly blacklist materials from ever being returned; this mod respects those cases. This is my take on Neceros' [99 Percent] Mod ( https://github.com/Neceros/99percent , https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1267149586 ) since they are no longer maintaing their mods. I took their idea but not their codes as this is a C# rewrite that adds configurability. Since there is no Harmony for RimWorld 1.0 and 1.1, in those two game versions only the deconstruction return setting is available. This is my second C# mod, let me know if you notice any incompatibilities.

name: [ETF] Butchering Now Yields Hemogen!
author: echotidefish
description: =================> WHAT THIS MOD DOES The goal of this mod is simple: whenever you butcher a corpse, you will receive Hemogen. It also includes a full mod settings menu that lets you customize how it works, from what types of Hemogen packs drop to how much you get and more. --- =================> THE SETTINGS The settings menu is the heart of this mod and should be the first place you visit before starting a new playthrough. • Master Toggle (Master Control System): This single button enables or disables the mod's Hemogen production function. Use it if you want to temporarily stop the feature without removing the mod from your save, which can cause issues. You can always turn it back on later. Most players will keep it enabled by default. • Output Type Configuration (Hemogen Category Menu): This menu determines what type of Hemogen is produced based on the type of creature being butchered. Two different option sets appear depending on whether you are using VRE - Sanguophage or not. Without VRE - Sanguophage: Available options: Hemogen Pack or Disabled (no yield). Default for all categories: Hemogen Pack. With VRE - Sanguophage: Available options: Disabled, Hemogen Pack, Hemogen Pack (Animal), Hemogen Pack (Corpse), Hemogen Pack (Sanguophage). Default per category: • Extracted from Animals - Hemogen Pack (Animal) • Extracted from Humanoids - Hemogen Pack (Corpse) • Extracted from Sanguophages - Hemogen Pack (Sanguophage) • Yield and Quantity Settings: This section controls how much Hemogen is produced, the chance of success, and any scaling conditions. You can choose between: - Manual Mode: full control over extraction yields. - Base Body Size Mode: automatic yield scaling for balanced results. Extraction Success Chance is self-explanatory. Butchery Efficiency Scaling (default: off) allows Hemogen output to scale with the butcher's efficiency stat, just like meat yield. If your butcher's efficiency is above 100%, expect bonus Hemogen. Below 100%, expect reduced amounts. This depends on where and how the butchery occurs (for example, Butcher Spot or Butcher Table). Tip: Always double-check your settings before starting a session. This mod rewards fine-tuning! There are other smaller settings and quality-of-life options you can explore on your own. --- =================> COMPATIBILITY Fully tested and confirmed to work with a wide range of popular mods, furniture packs, and xenotype expansions. Confirmed Compatible: • Auto Cutter (04/09/26) • Vanilla Races Expanded - Sanguophage (03/20/26) • Small Furniture, Small Butcher Table, Electric Butcher Table (03/20/26) • Tiny Utilities, Vanilla Furniture Expanded - Production (03/20/26) • Vanilla Quests Expanded - Ancients, and many others (03/20/26) About Sanguophage Detection: For the Extracted from Sanguophages category, the mod checks a custom list of supported xenotypes whenever a corpse is processed. If the corpse belongs to one of these xenotypes, the appropriate Hemogen type will be produced automatically. Currently Supported Xenotypes: • Biotech • Alpha Genes • VRE - Sanguophage • Meta's Genelines - Vampires • Big and Small - Vampires and the Undead • Whiteglove's Hemokomori Xenotype • Big and Small - Simply Robots --- =================> FINAL NOTES I hope you enjoy the mod! If you have ideas for compatibility or new xenotype support, feel free to share them in the comments. Source Code: https://gitgud.io/etf_rimworldprojects/etf-butchering-now-yields-hemogen

author: Dizzy Ioeuy

name: Bed Rest For Food Poisoning
author: 1trickPonyta
description: If you're constantly vomitting and can barely move, would you go hunting? No, you would rest in bed. Now your colonists can too. This mod makes pawns consider food poisoning to be an affliction worthy of bed rest (as prioritized in the work tab). You can adjust the range of food poisoning severity that warrants bed rest in the mod settings. This means you won't have to find Horton on the other side of the map hauling the rat meat from the sky while she can barely move, stopping every five seconds to vomit before dropping the rat meat and trying to get to the freezer to satisfy her empty food bar only to go slaughterer before she even makes it back into the base, killing your bonded yorkie and then collapsing on the ground in pain shock. === Updates === 09/05/2025: Added mod setting to adjust food poisoning severity range for bed rest 08/17/2025: Fixed language bug so non-English works 06/11/2025: Updated to 1.6 03/19/2024: Updated to 1.5 10/26/2022: Updated to 1.4 === Credits === Mod icon: twitter.com/mouse_draws

author: Linnun

name: Keep Burning, Corpse!
author: Tixiv
description: Have you ever wondered why the fire goes out when a pawn that is on fire dies? It doesn't seem realistic, and with Shamblers an Death Pall it's a real nuisance. Turns out this is actually a bug, as Rimworld has specific code to keep the fire when a pawn dies. It just doesn't work out of the box since the check for the fire is done after the fire is already removed. This mod fixes that: If anything dies while on fire, the corpse will keep burning with this mod. That's all it does.

name: Political Compass - Mort's Ideologies
author: Mort Strudel
description: Adds four Ideological memes representing the four traditional sides of the political compass, and a moderate number of precepts to give these memes a lot of unique mechanics. Want to play as a Socialist Democracy? An Anarchist Free Market? An Absolute Monarchy? A Communist Dictatorship? That's precisely what this mod is for! In order to make them actually work in Rimworld, these political concepts have of course been simplified and made to fit into neat little boxes. Don't expect a political science masterpiece here, we're just trying to make a rough analogue that's good enough to make each meme feel like it meaningfully shapes the politics of your colony. Any complaints about the depiction of your most cherished or hated political systems can be directed towards the workshop comments, which I assume will be full of worthless vitriolic sludge. Government Power: Liberty and Authority The Government Power axis determines how centralized authority is in your colony. The biggest effect of this is that the Liberty and Authority memes each come with precepts that determine how your leader is selected. Each Leader precept only takes effect when it's part of the primary ideoligion of the colony. With Authority, your leader is either chosen through Dictatorship or Monarchy. Under a Dictatorship, leaders are chosen for life. Once a leader has been set, they can only be reassigned after the death of the leader, or due to a change in the colony's primary ideology. Under a Monarchy, the leader of the colony will automatically be set to whoever has the highest-ranking title within the Fallen Empire. Long Live the King! With Liberty, your leader is either chosen through Democracy or Anarchy. Under a Democracy, election rituals are held where your pawns can choose their leader based on popular opinion. Under Anarchy, you won't have a leader! Your leader will be automatically unassigned if you try to appoint one. Economic Distribution: Equality and Stratification The Economic Distribution axis determines how equally, or unequally, your colonists expect their rooms to be. Colonists who believe in Wealth Equality will be upset if any colonist has a more impressive room than any other, while Colonists who believe in Wealth Stratification will demand that commoners have worse rooms than them if they have a royal title or ideological role. This is my first Rimworld mod, and as such it maybe be rough around the edges in places. Please inform me of any bugs you encounter, and let me know if you have any suggestions about the way the different memes and precepts should work. Consider the comment section to be an absolute dictatorship, as I reserve any and all right to delete your weird political rants at my whim.

name: Rimbody
author: Maux
description: # Rimbody ## Features * Gain/lose muscle and fat based on pawn's diet and activities * Dynamic Bodytype based on muscle and fat * Workout schedule * Strength, Balance, Cardio workouts ## Description Rimbody allows your pawns to gain or lose muscle and fat based on their diet and activities, and change their body type accordingly. This mod includes a patch for GetRimped that fixes its bugs and enables your pawns to use workout machines to actually get ripped. I highly recommend using it, as Rimbody currently does not offer any strength training on its own. The aim of this mod is not to accurately emulate real life, but to add consequences to the type of work pawns do by creating tangible differences between pawns who mostly sit around all day and those who engage in hard manual labor. Pawns who do not use their bodies as much will need to spend time working out to compensate for their lack of activity in order to stay fit.

name: Rimbody - Stat Module
author: Maux
description: # Rimbody_StatModule Stat Module for Rimbody, a RimWorld Mod. This module integrates Rimbody’s Muscle Mass and Body Fat into pawns' stats. ## Features * Muscle is mostly beneficial to the stats, as most work needs muscle, and you don't gain muscle easily. * Fat is not so beneficial, but high fat will come in handy when you are starving, and having low fat can be deadly when you have no food. * Rimbody is also designed so that Fat helps pawns keep their muscle (bodyfat lowers muscle loss), so having a moderate, healthy amount of fat can be beneficial.

author: Zaljerem
description: Original mod by Oskar Potocki, Smash Phil https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2443118113 CC-ShareAlike license Received permission from Oskar for the continuation (thanks ferny!) -- This storyteller makes pretty deep changes to the game. Accordingly, this mod is presented as-is. It is highly unlikely I will do any compatibility or additional work on it. -- Original mod notes (1.4): Vanilla Storytellers Expanded is a mod series featuring standalone storytellers, bringing new, unique mechanics to the game. "Oskar Obnoxious holds no regard for ongoing stories. Things will turn on their heads countless times before a colony goes down in flames. Frequently released Patch notes can alter the values of the game, changing almost anything in the game completely by a random number." Oskar Obnoxious comes with the following traits: Patch Notes This storyteller releases patch notes every few days, changing the game drastically. Patch notes change random values of random Defs into random numbers. This can result in items becoming incredibly unbalanced, overpowered or worthless. Hard Difficulty This storyteller has hard difficulty. It will favour bad events, and any events that happen are tailored to your colony based on it’s wealth, past events, amount of colonists and other factors. Random Events This storyteller will fire random events without any regard for how your colony is doing. Whilst the events still scale with wealth, their type - good, neutral, bad - is completely random, just like with Randy.

name: Yaoma Storytellers - Jianghu Jin
author: Zaljerem
description: Spun out from "Yaoma Storytellers (Standalone)" by Zomuro https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3030767805 MIT license, and the original author allows re-use of the code with credit, but my primary rule still applies: If the original author requests it, I will remove this update. New art by pochi (provided by Zomuro) https://vgen.co/pochikocchi https://x.com/delulouch https://pochidayo.carrd.co/ Previous Jianghu art by Visandar_the_Unliving Underlying preview art by DetVisor Compatible with ferny's "Progression: Storytellers" - category: Chaotic -- Jianghu Jin - Lady of the Mountains and Seas Jianghu Jin knows the marvels of many natural landscapes. At regular intervals, she will transform the map to display the majesty of the planet, while respecting indoor rooms and any area in range of a stabilizer, either in the form of a buildable totem or a rare array. In addition, she will provide a boon to pawn construction and mining speed. She does not concern herself with tampering with chance otherwise. [Randy Random-based] -- See mod settings to customize the experience in various ways. Additional mod settings: change hilliness, change biome, verbose logging Please note: A "Too many signals" error may be thrown after terraforming; it seems to be ignorable, and sometimes occurs with other mods that change the map as well (VE structure generator, etc.). I've tried to minimize it in the code as much as possible, but it still sometimes occurs. If the terraforming process crashes to the menu completely, this is usually due to a biome that may need to be blacklisted. I've tested against many biomes, but if this does occur, please turn on verbose logging to get a full log of the biome-scoring process.

Giddy-Up allows pawns to ride animals around on the map, or even use them as battle mounts.

author: Adamas
description: Adds a storefront tab to the cash register. Assign a colonist with a high social skill to sell goods in the shop. Works standalone — vanilla caravan visitors and friendly faction pawns will automatically browse and buy from open stores. If the Hospitality mod is also installed, Hospitality guests are fully supported as before.

name: PocketMap Architect Fix

name: Social Experience from Trade
author: Krelinos
description: In RimWorld, every skill gains experience when it is practiced. Every skill, except social when trading (and stonecutting but that mod exists already). If you ever felt like your trade negotiator should have really learned a thing or two after settling a deal worth 10000+ silver, this mod does just that with plenty of tweaks to satisfy your preferences. When buying goods, experience gain is (by default) based on the standard market value of that good. Buying a single plasteel always nets you 9 experience regardless of how much it actually costs, multiplied by the colonist's passion and global learning factor. When selling goods, experience gain is based on the negotiated value of that good. A single gold bar sold for 8 silver nets you 8 experience, multiplied by learning factor. As social skill improves, better deals are negotiated by the colonist, resulting in more experience at the later levels.

name: Ultimate Storyteller [1.4-1.6]
author: GoldenLumia, Beast(Original)
description: This is a quick update of the https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2557208773 mod for 1.4-1.6. The directory structure for the storyteller texture is slightly different and I set it to appear slightly lower compared to my other modded storytellers. Want to make this harder by adding RNG psycasters (from Vanilla Psycasts Expanded) for your pawns and raids? Check out the Basilicus Patch!: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2928443788 === original description === An attempt to combine the best aspects of each storyteller, with some additional aspects: - Like Randy, events can spawn randomly and in rapid succession. - Event difficulty is slightly randomized, between 75% and 125% threat points. - Like Cassandra regular raids are guranteed. - Like Perry, quests, trading caravans and travelers are much more frequent. - Population curve is like vanilla. (Though like Randy, population events can still happen through sheer random chance.) In the end I wanted a storyteller which feels more like an adventure rather than a survival simulator. Could be easier, could be harder, but at the very least something is always happening. Very simple mod, no scripting nor patching, should be compatible with anything.

name: Vehicle Framework - Local Flight Systems
author: NuanKi
description: "Give Your Vehicles the Ability to Reposition Anywhere on the Map – No World Travel Required! (Perfect for when walking around the map feels *too peasant-like*)" What It Does: Map-Local Flight: Launch and land vehicles anywhere on the same map. *Parking ticket fees not included.* Fuel-Driven Short Hops: Fixed 5 chemfuel cost per jump. *Because chemfuel doesn’t grow on trees (unless you modded that in).* Safety First: Blocks launches under roofs. *Your shuttle is not a chandelier.* Configurable Pilot Policy: Toggle pilot requirements in settings. *For when your "pilot" is busy sobbing in the freezer over that one time they ate without a table.* Disclaimer: Not responsible for: - Shuttles fused with ancient mechanoid architecture (*"modern art"*) - Pilots unionizing after learning they’re “optional” - Mechanoids taking notes on your sweet moves - The 5-chemfuel cost awakening a primal hoarding instinct in your colony

name: We Are United
author: Sl4vP0weR
description: Unite with others, together We Are United! "We Are United" formerly "Family Reunion" - allows you to recruit pawns who are related to your colonist or has no home. Usage: Right-click on the pawn with selected colonist and 'Ask to unite'. [Sometimes option doesn't appear, just try a few more times in a different parts of texture] When you 'Ask to unite', selected colonist will try to recruit targeted pawn with some chance. Chance of success is calculated considering: 1. Relation importance (Spouse is the most important relation in game, chance will be affected by 25%) 2. Opinion of target about colonist (Max opinion of 100, chance will be affected by 50%) 3. Social skill of colonist (Max skill level of 20, chance will be affected by 50%) Idea: When I was playing, parents of my colonist wander in with other faction, and only thing I could do - arrest them. It's just sad to see when related pawns wander in and all you can do for reunion is arrest... This mod is friendly solution for reunion, faction will not consider reunion as a hostile act. Supported languages: - English - French - German - Korean - Russian - Portuguese Brazilian - Spanish

description: Progress Renderer Original Mod: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1438693028 Automatically create scheduled renderings of the full map or only a chosen part of it. name: RPG Wound Descriptions
author: Tony NG
description: Rewrites vanilla wound descriptions with immersive, weapon-aware prose. Every wound is described in two beats: a visceral verb followed by a clinical anchor, written in a past-tense field-medic register. The same hit feels different depending on what caused it. A shotgun shreds, a longsword opens, a warhammer pulps, a frag grenade peppers, a rocket caves. == Features == - Severity-tiered wound labels (pulped, mangled, deep puncture, gaping gash, compound fracture, deep cut, bone bruise, flayed open, grazed) - Weapon-aware prose: bullet, blade, bludgeon, shrapnel, explosive, energy, fang, claw, fire each have their own voice - Armor-padded hit detection: light wounds caught by armor read differently than wounds that bypass it - Body-part-aware phrasing: wounds to the head, chest, limbs, and organs each get appropriate language - Per-instance variation: 9 prose variants per wound type per tier keep reads fresh across a long colony - Vanilla-safe: pure XML + C# Harmony patches. No def overrides, no save-game changes. Add or remove mid-save. == Compatibility == - Combat Extended: damage classification works through CE's preserved vanilla damage def names - Nice Health Tab: compatible - Compact Hediffs: compatible - 800+ mod packs: tested against a heavy modlist with no conflicts Made by Party.gif.

A massive content expansion focused on enhancing the late-game experience. It introduces new offensive measures against mechanoids, ways to produce previously uncraftable recipes, and brings your colony one step closer to becoming a glitterworld paradise.

You can expect:

 • Combat quests for obtaining unique items
 • A brand-new production chain

name: Faster Game Loading - Continued
author: 綠菇
description: === Does loading take forever? This mod is for you! === Sick of staring at the loading screen every time you start RimWorld? This mod cuts down startup time using several tricks that work in the background, so the game loads faster without changing any gameplay. --- What it does --- - Early mod content loading: Starts loading pending mod content during idle loading gaps before RimWorld's normal ReloadContentInt pass reaches those mods. (enabled by default) - Multi-threaded preloading: Speeds up XML loading and type resolution by utilizing multiple CPU cores. (enabled by default) - XPath cache: Caches XML queries during load and safely releases it on main menu initialization to prevent runtime conflicts and free up memory. (enabled by default) - Delay graphic and icon loading: Delay loading non-essential textures (like background objects) until after you enter a game — weapons, clothing, food, pawns, and furniture are always loaded right away so nothing looks broken. (disabled by default) - Adaptive atlas baking: Automatically adjusts batch sizes based on your GPU speed and keeps RimWorld 1.6 vanilla atlas pre-inserts intact. (disabled by default) - Verbose logging: Outputs debug messages to the console. (disabled by default) - Texture downscaler: Reduces the file size of high-resolution textures to save VRAM and speed up loading. Your original mod files are never touched, downscaled copies are stored in a separate folder, and you can delete them anytime to go back to full quality. (disabled by default) --- Things to know --- - The game may briefly freeze or feel unresponsive during startup. This is normal — the mod is doing work in the background. - It may take a while to get any sound after entering the main menu, which is normal; sound playback is released automatically after deferred sound definitions finish resolving. - When delay graphic loading is disabled, static atlases are not baked again by the delayed startup cleanup, preventing duplicate atlas VRAM usage with large race or texture-heavy mods. - ChezhouLib's AssetBundle reload patch runs before FGL's duplicate-reload guard, so ChezhouLib-managed bundles can refresh correctly during development reload paths. - Early mod content loading now includes official Core/DLC packs as well as player mods. - If you are using Image Opt, this mod's texture downscaler will step aside, while early content loading remains enabled. Invalid Image Opt .dds / .dds.zstd cache files are cleaned in texture folders only, in the background, so Image Opt can fall back or regenerate cleanly. For Graphics Settings+ or RimSort (Optimize Texture), the texture downscaler will step aside. (Converting to DDS is actually more efficient and has higher quality than directly downscaled images, so it is recommended to use the texture downscaler only when you cannot use such tools) --- Works well with --- - Loading Progress - Missile Girl - Performance Mod or DefLoadCache (choose one) - Image Opt - Graphics Settings+ --- Works best with a lot of mods. Zero impact on gameplay or saves. --- Original mod by Taranchuk. This is a maintained fork with bug fixes and improvements.

name: Ideo Tick Optimization
author: Sakura_TA
description: Tired of your TPS dropping to 15 because you have too many ideologies? This mod optimizes ideology ticking by skipping precept ticks for ideologies that have no pawns assigned to them. Inspired by a player who discovered that using the dev tool to reduce all unoccupied ideologies to a single precept more than doubled their TPS. Now you can keep your ideologies clean without the dev tools - let your colonists focus on their crusades while the mod handles the rest! Performance impact: - Ideologies with no pawns: 0 precept ticks (previously full tick cost) - Ideologies with pawns: unchanged, full tick as normal - Recount every 1000 ticks to keep things accurate Compatible with Multiplayer mod. No new saves required, can be added/removed mid-game.

name: 1trickPwnyta's Defaults
author: 1trickPwnyta
description: Description Tired of having to go through the same ritual every time you start a new colony of configuring your colonists' schedules, setting your quest reward preferences, turning down the medicine setting so you don't waste your good medicine on bruises, and more? This mod allows you to customize various default settings to use during gameplay, such as the default schedules your colonists will assume. See below for a full list of settings. This mod's config file (your settings for this mod) gets pretty big and complex and it would kinda suck if something happened and you had to reconfigure everything from scratch. So now you can back up this mod's settings through the mod settings window (in General settings). Automatic periodic backups are enabled by default. Compatibility Supports all DLC and can be safely added mid-playthrough, however many settings will only apply to new colonies. Default Settings Categories Default storyteller settings Set the default storyteller/difficulty settings to use for a new colony, including custom difficulty settings. Default world settings Set the default world, map, and faction settings to use for a new colony. Default colonist schedules Set custom default schedules for colonists. You can create alternating schedules and the mod will cycle between them when assigning them to new colonists. Default policies Set custom default apparel, food, drug, and reading policies that will be copied to each new colony. ☼ Includes additional settings to automatically assign certain policies to certain types of pawns. For example, you can ensure new children to the colony get the no-drug policy. Default baby feeding settings Set the default autofeed setting for colonists based on relationship to baby and whether they are lactating. Also allows you to set which foods babies can be fed by default. Biotech only. Default medicine settings Set the default medicine settings to use for a new colony. ☼ Includes additional settings for default medicine type and amount to carry and whether guests should carry your medicine as well. Default reward preferences Set the default reward preferences to use for a new colony. Default expanded resource categories Set which resource tree categories are expanded by default in categorized mode. Default storage settings Configure the default settings for stockpile zones, dumping stockpile zones, and storage buildings such as shelves. You can also create your own custom stockpile zone types with their own settings. ☼ Includes an additional setting for allowing removing items from outfit stands by default (Odyssey only). Default workbench bills Set default bills for workbenches that will populate automatically upon building a workbench. ☼ Includes additional settings for default ingredient search radius, skill range, and store mode. You can remove the limit of 15 bills per workbench as well. Default allowed areas Create default allowed areas for new colonies and control which types of pawns get automatically assigned to which areas. ☼ Includes additional settings for whether parent allowed areas are still inherited by their children. Default fishing zone settings Configure the default settings for fishing zones. Odyssey only. Default work priorities Create default work priorities for new colonists based on their passions and skills. ☼ Includes an additional setting for using manual work priorities by default. Default play settings Configure default play settings. These are generally the toggle buttons in the bottom-right corner of the screen. Miscellaneous defaults Other default settings that don't fit neatly into one of the other categories. These include: • Starting xenotype: Set the default xenotype for colonists in the character creation screen. (Biotech only.) • Hostility response: Set the default hostility response to use for new colonists. • Pregnancy approach: Set the default pregnancy approach that new romantic colonist relationships will take. (Biotech only.) • Plant type: Set the default plant type for new growing zones. • Auto-select caravan supplies: Choose whether this option will be enabled when opening a dialog to form a caravan. • Temperature targets: Set the default temperature targets for heaters and coolers. • Mech work modes: Set the default work modes for the initial two mechanitor control groups as well as a mode for all additional control groups granted by control sublinks. name: [ARY] Automatic Stump Chopping [1.5 - 1.6]
author: Arylice
description: Arylice's Automatic Stump Chopping #arylice #aryasc Have you ever watched your lumberjacks chop down trees, only for them to leave those annoying stumps behind, and felt that urge to have everything perfectly tidy? You wish they’d just finish the job completely? This mod will solve this issue in an automatic way! Safe to add, remove and change its custom settings mid-save! You get the following options that you can enable or disable anytime in-game: * Automatically Designate The Stump For Chopping After cutting down an almost fully grown tall tree, your worker will instantly designate the spawned stump for chopping, which usually makes them chop down the stump right away as it would be the closest next job to do! * Automatically Designate Blighted Plants For Cutting Whenever your crops become blighted in the future, the blighted plants will instantly designate themselves to be cut down. This means even if the blight spreads to other plants nearby, it will spawn with a cutting job on itself automatically! * Chopped Tall Trees Have Falling Visual Effect For most tall trees almost fully grown, when they are chopped, there will be a little visual effect of a falling tree (almost like in Stardew Valley, but not really)! This feature is not perfect, but it can be nice to look at! Young and small trees will not have that small visual effect. You also get Order buttons to chop and harvest more precisely: * Chop only stumps (Stumps of special DLC trees included). * Chop only fully grown trees with a 100% growth (Special DLC trees will not be marked). * Harvest only fully grown crops with a 100% growth. This mod requires Harmony! DLC are not required, but works well with them nonetheless!

name: Achtung!
author: Andreas Pardeike
description: Command your colonists like a boss! The Achtung! mod enhances how you control RimWorld. You will get more control on how to position your colonists and how they take job orders. In a nutshell you can: - position your drafted colonists along a line - move them in formation - give orders to multiple colonists at once - force jobs so they get uninterrupted attention - haul and repair outside allowed areas EXAMPLES (*) Save time by issuing a command with more than one colonist selected. For example: select three brawlers and right click an enemy, then choose "melee". Done. (*) In combat, position colonists equally spaced in door openings. Select multiple drafted colonists and with the right mouse button drag a line. Achtung! will move your colonists to equally spaced positions in real time. 10 colonists into 10 doors? No problem! (*) Fall back a few steps with a group of colonists? Easy. Select them and hold the configured key to move them relative to their current formation. You can even rotate the formation with the standard rotation keys. (*) Make sure that wall and the sandbags are build before the raid arrives. No cloudwatching or eating allowed! Use the [Force] button that Achtung! adds to all "Prioritize..." menus and you can be sure that all assigned work will be done. (*) Want one colonist harvest and another sow these three fields? Force them to their tasks and queue up non-adjacted fields by simply adding forced work on them (like ordinary jobs but without the shift key). (*) Treat all injured colonists in their beds? Select a doctor, choose "Prioritize tending... [Force]" and increase the search range so nearby patients will be included (you will see a small "!" on all forced job). Then focus on other important stuff because you can be sure it's done. The original three Achtung! commands "Clean Room", "Fight Fire" or "Sow Zone/Room" still exist because they do stuff a bit smarter than the build in prioritized work commands. SETTINGS Achtung uses the default way to access mod settings. There, you find switches to turn certain features on/off and you can change the default keys to your liking. ADDING AND REMOVING: Achtung can be added to any existing game. It usually does not modify save state for saved games to avoid a dependency on it. However, a side effect of the provided custom jobs is that when save the game and your colonists are actively running an Achtung job this will be saved too thus creating a dependency to Achtung. Workaround: open the saved game with Achtung, cancel all Achtung jobs and save it again. This will "clean" the save and remove the dependency. The three main places to do so are Ludeon Forums: https://ludeon.com/forums/index.php?topic=22130.0 Steam Workshop: http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/comments/730936602 GitHub: https://github.com/pardeike/Achtung2/releases/latest LICENSE Free. name: Auto-Open Garage (VVE)
author: Iaw
description: You've just finished preparing a large caravan. You've carefully selected every colonist, packed all the supplies, confirmed everything, and clicked Send Caravan - only to realize the garage door is still closed. Now you have to cancel the process, open the garage door, and start everything over again. This mod automatically opens designated garage doors whenever a caravan is sent or returns to your colony, eliminating unnecessary interruptions and making caravan management just a bit smoother. This is the first mod I've worked on, so feel free to leave bug reports or feedback in the comments. FEATURES - Per-door toggle. Every Vanilla Vehicles Expanded garage door gains an "Auto-open for caravans" button, so only the doors you choose will open. Doors with the toggle off are always left alone. The setting is saved per door. - Opens when you send. The moment you open the Form Caravan dialog the door starts opening, so by the time you finish selecting items and press Send, the vehicle already has a clear path out - no more silent "no accessible path" failures that lose your whole selection. - Opens when you return. A returning vehicle caravan gets the garage opened with the proper animation and sound, then drives in. - Respects power. On a returning caravan, only powered electric doors open by themselves. Manual or unpowered doors stay shut, so an unpowered base behaves normally. - Never closes on a vehicle. The auto-close option will not shut a door that a vehicle is sitting in. - Save-game compatible. Can be added to or removed from existing saves. - Includes configurable settings to tweak the mod to your liking. REQUIREMENTS - Harmony - Vanilla Vehicles Expanded (and its own requirement, Vehicle Framework) OPTIONAL - Automatic Parking - if installed, a returning vehicle drives to its saved parking spot once the door is open, and the "auto-close after parking" option becomes available. COMPATIBILITY Safe to add to an existing save, and safe to remove from one. All patches are applied by Harmony at runtime and resolve the game's and VVE's members by name, so if a future update renames something the mod simply logs a message and does nothing rather than breaking your game. Nothing in vanilla is overwritten, no defs are replaced, and no vanilla behaviour changes when the per-door toggle is off.

name: Automatic Subcore Scanning
author: Lomzie
description: Tired of manually managing subcore scanning all the time? Want to mass-produce deadly killing machines? Then this is the mod for you! Pawns can automatically fill scanners, and enter softscanners, or carry prisoners with the "Softscan"/"Ripscan" interaction to softscanners/ripscanners. This mods adds an "Autoload" option to subcore scanners, which when enabled allows you to set a target number of cores, and toggle whether colonists and prisoners can automatically enter it. When colonists are allowed, any colonist with the "Basic" work task will enter the subscanner whenever possible. For prisoners, you can set their interaction mode to either "Softscan" or "Ripscan", and wardens will automatically carry them to softscanners and ripscanners respectively. Recent changes: * Now allows slaves to enter softscanners. * Use left control/shift to incremenet/decrement target faster. * Set target count to below 0 to produce cores forever. * General polish and fixes. Arguably, automating the absolute eradication of living human brains with thoughts and emotions could be seen as somewhat barbaric, but then again this is Warcri- ahem, RimWorld. It should under no circumstances put one of your colonists into the ripscanner, but I have about as much faith in my software as I have in my driving, and I don't have a driver's licence and am generally terrified of driving. Should this happen, please let me know immediately, and I will solve it as soon as possible. Of course, if you imprison a colonist and set them to be ripscanned, then they will be. Perfectly safe to add and remove from saves. Integrates nicely with Custom Prisoner Interactions. You can set prisoners to be ripscanned by default, and turn everyone who dares attack your mechatropolis into subcores. There does seem to be a strange bug where, if the mod was added and a prisoner set to one of the mods interaction mode, then the mod was removed, then added again, would result in the prisoners interaction menu being bugged. I do not know which causes this, but please let me know if this happens to you. Includes patches for: * Vanilla Races Expanded - Androids: Subcore polyanalyser. Give me a poke if you have further requests for patches, or create a pull request on GitHub with one. GitHub: https://github.com/Lomztein/RimWorld-Minimods/tree/main/AutomaticSubcoreScanning Discord: https://discord.gg/QvNCcy8JHh I am almost entirely new to this whole modding business, so bugs and janky behaviour may occur. Please report any bugs or issues via the GitHub repository or the mods workshop page.

author: Holgast
description: This is a fork/remake of Bulk Stonecutting, by NECEROS and Fuglypump. Uses the existing stonecutting table, no research required, adds recipes for 3x, 5x and 10x stones. Support for Cupro's Stones, Extra Stone, Strike the Earth! Stone, and Alpha Biomes as well as Electric Stonecutting Table and Early Times. Stonecutting now also grants crafting exp.\n\n Disclaimer! - If you are using a mod that makes chunks stackable you will only get 20 blocks from any of the 'make any blocks' recipes and this is a problem with any 'Bulk Stonecutting' mod. For this reason the bulk 'make any blocks' recipes are disabled when 'Stackable Chunks' is installed. If you are NOT using a mod that makes chunks stackable, you get the full amount - the excess that can't be carried will otherwise simply be dropped onto the ground. This is to do with how stone blocks work and will need someone else to make an assembly to fix. The other recipes that specify a kind of block work fine.

name: Count Stacked Prosthetics in Recipes

If you make bill to create up to 10 prosthetic parts, you'll find yourself with 10 stacks of them - way more than intended.

name: Defensive Positions
author: UnlimitedHugs
description: Version: 1.14.0 Description Allows your colonists to remember their position during base defense. You can send off your colonists to their positions with a single click. How to use Set defensive positions for colonists 1) Draft your defenders and place them where you want them. 2) With your defenders selected, right-click the Defensive position button and select "Save defensive position". Done. The selected colonists will remember their held positions. Send colonists to saved positions 1) Select your defenders. 2) Click the Defensive position button (or press T). Your defenders will be drafted and will run to their saved positions. Advanced mode Hold the Alt key and click the Defensive position button to switch between basic and advanced mode. Advanced mode works exactly like Basic, but you have 4 positions to work with. Save a position using the right-click menu, then click the slot to send the selected colonists to the position they have been assigned under that number. Pressing T is the same as clicking the first slot. Squad hotkeys Colonists can be assigned to squads for easier selection. To assign, hold the Ctrl key and press 1-9 on the numeric keypad to assign the squad to that key. Press the numeric key of a squad to select the squad members, press again to focus on the squad location. Utility hotkeys There are three other keys on the keypad for quick colonist management: press period to select all colonists on the map, undraft everyone by pressing divide, and press zero to send all colonists to their assigned defensive position. In the Options > Mod Options window you can switch the Shift key from saving positions to queuing movement orders.

name: Flickable Storage
author: Mlie
description: [img]https://img.litet.net/logos/Self-Info.png[/img] Storage-buildings and stockpiles can be set to one of four settings [list] [*] Storage on - Works as normal [*] Storage off - Will not accept or release any items [*] Accept only - Pawns can only store items, not retrieve them [*] Retrieve only - Pawns can only retrieve items, not store them [/list] [h2]Examples[/h2] Your prison cells have a storage unit for food, but when there is no prisoners. You want to stop hauling food for it without changing storage filters or priorities. You turn the shelf to retrieve only when there are no prisoners. You want to have a stack of steel left at all times for emergency trap-building. You set one shelf to store only with highest priority. [h2]Technical[/h2] The blocking of storing new items is done by modifying the Accept-check for the storage. The blocking of retrieving items is done by modifying the Forbidden check for the items in the storage. Pawns with mental break ignores the forbidden check so they will still be able to fetch items. Should work with all mods that add storage buildings using the IHaulDestination class. Tested for example with [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1617282896]LWM's Deep Storage[/url] Will also change flick-setting in all linked storages. NOTE: Chunks cannot be forbidden so are ignored by this mods settings.
