name: Most Skilled Bill Restriction
author: MatheusWerneck
description: Most Skilled Bill Restriction makes your production dynamic. Just enable the "Most skilled" option on your bills, and the mod will automatically ensure that only the most capable colonist available takes on the task. Why use this? - Better Quality: Prevents low-skilled pawns from wasting materials when a better crafter is around. - Caravan Aware: Enable "Include Away" to keep your master crafters in caravans counting towards your colony's skill benchmark, protecting your production quality even while they travel. - Ignore Downed: If your colony's chef is downed, what happens to food production? With "Ignore downed" enabled, the mod will automatically skip incapacitated pawns, letting your second best cook take the job temporarily.. - Performance First: My priority is always on performance, and i'm pretty sure i achieved that here, but let me know if you notice any problems with it. - Universal Compatibility: Works perfectly alongside all Work Tab and management mods because it only checks conditions before a job starts. - Fully Localized: Includes translations for all official RimWorld languages. If you notice any mistranslation, please let me know.

name: Persistent Precepts
author: Alleykat
description: Persistent Precepts adds a simple toggle to the Ideology edit screen that prevents the re-randomization of Ideology precepts, rituals, buildings etc. when you change structure or memes. With this mod, you can ensure that your carefully crafted Ideology remains intact, even if you go back and change structure/memes. This also means your saved ideoligions can better act as templates when you load them in. When the toggle is on, ideology re-randomization for the player is blocked for: * Precepts * Roles * Rituals * Buildings * Relics * Weapons * Venerated Animals * Preferred Xenotypes * Preferred Apparel * Appearance (Hair, Beards, Tattoos) (this one is currently not working) Please note: The confirmation warning of re-randomizing precepts still comes up, please ignore it for now while I work out how to change the confirmation dialogue. If you start a new game and forget to turn the toggle off, your faction's ideology will be generated without any precepts/rituals etc. This is easily fixed by flicking the toggle back off and selecting "Randomize Precepts" button. Other factions generated at world creation and as part of events are not impacted. Compatibility The mod uses harmony to patch a few methods related to player actions on the ideology edit screen and precept randomization. It touches nothing else besides adding the checkbox so should be highly compatible with other mods. Thanks Mute for reviewing my code and being generally awesome with guidance, especially with how to approach limiting the toggle to only affect player actions. Mile for giving me advice and a friendly space to get help and feedback. Rimworld modding community, this is my first ever mod and I couldn't have done it without supportive people in discord. author: slofa
description: Quality of Life mod that allows you to quickly create a stockpile, shelf, or bookcase directly from an item, for just that item type, with a few other features. This works fine with modded items and item categories, and is safe to add to - and be removed from - existing games. Features • Selecting any haulable item gives a new command to create a new stockpile or shelves just for that item type • Right-clicking on that command lets you create stockpiles or shelves for any of the item's categories • Select multiple items at once and create a stockpile or shelves for all those items • Stockpiles created with this mod use intelligent names • Selecting an item already in a stockpile gives a command to let you disallow it in that stockpile • Right-click on that command to disallow the item's categories instead • You can undo any disallows in case you make a mistake Credits • Russian translation by Reiquard (https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198012474522) • Simplified Chinese translation by HawnHan (https://steamcommunity.com/id/HawnHan) • Spanish translation by Crusader (https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561197986639775)

name: RandomPlusPlus
author: hsariaslan
description: RandomPlusPlus RandomPlusPlus is a pawn randomizer for RimWorld. Set the filters you want, press Randomize, and the mod keeps rerolling until a matching pawn is found or the reroll limit is reached. Important This mod is forked from RandomPlus by mastertea (special thanks). Disable the original RandomPlus mod when using RandomPlusPlus to avoid conflicts. RandomPlusPlus already includes the original RandomPlus features. Reroll Modes - Normal: standard randomization flow. - Fast (beta): legacy faster reroll mode comes from RandomPlus mod. - Ultra Fast: balanced mode between speed and reliability. - Ultra Fast++: up to ~5x faster than Ultra Fast mode, depending on selected filters, but the found pawn may have inaccurate details. Filters - Trait whitelist and blacklist filters with Required, Pool, and Excluded behavior. - Childhood and adulthood backstory filters with scenario-aware backstory lists. - Possession filters with Required and Pool behavior, categories, and count ranges. - Custom health condition filters for start conditions, pregnancy, pain, scars, addictions, body modifications, and other conditions. - Custom incapable filters for skills and work types such as Violence, Firefighting, Dumb Labor, Cleaning, Hauling, and Childcare. - Skill level, passion, age, and gender filters. Quality Of Life - Reroll limits up to 1B. - Right-click cancellation while randomizing. - Focus-out cancellation to avoid long freezes when alt-tabbing. - Reroll count and time elapsed display. - Confirmation dialogs for reset, overwrite, delete, and other destructive actions. - Scenario-based percentage hints based on diagnostic reroll data. - Randomizing label helps to point easier the mod is currently randomizing. Source Code https://github.com/hsariaslan/RandomPlusPlus

description: [img]https://i.imgur.com/buuPQel.png[/img] Update of busted_bunnys mod https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2567877605 - Added option to not show the extra gizmos on items - Added option to not return components (or any complex items) when recycling - Load after any HAR race mods to avoid compatibility issues [img]https://i.imgur.com/pufA0kM.png[/img] [table] [tr][td][url=https://discord.gg/h5TY6DA][img]https://i.imgur.com/zdzzBrc.png[/img][/url][/td] [td][url=https://github.com/emipa606/RecycleThis][img]https://i.imgur.com/kTkpTOE.png[/img][/url][/td] [/tr] [tr] [td][img]https://i.imgur.com/WjDSfUn.png[/img][/td] [td][img]https://i.imgur.com/h5VwTNL.png[/img][/td] [/tr] [/table] [img]https://i.imgur.com/Z4GOv8H.png[/img] [i]Ever got tired of creating bills to smelt and destroy useless junk left from last cannibal raid? Not anymore. Just select all items you want to get rid of and pawns will do it.[/i] This mod allows you to recycle and destroy weapons and apparel through order icons, without creating annoying bills. It uses all vanilla values to calculate refund (around 25% of recipe) and job speed to make almost identical to vanilla bills (Smelt or burn weapons/apparel). Basically it adds 2 orders to menu and affected items: [olist] [*]Destroy item - selected weapons or apparel will be destroyed on closest campfire or smelter (including modded ones). [*]Recycle item - selected weapons or apparel will be either smelted or scrapped at the closest workbench yielding part of it's recipe resources back. [/olist] Post raid cleaning has never been this easy! New job (can be seen with [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=725219116&searchtext=Work+Tab]Fluffy's Work Tab[/url]) assosiated with added features exist in Crafting worktype right behind all vanilla jobs. [h1]Troubleshooting[/h1] There are 2 ways items get recycled: [olist] [*]For metal items, you must have a building that has "smelt weapons" bill and it must be either powered or fueled. [*]Everything else, like clothes, stone or wooden weapons get scrapped on tailor benches or crafting spots. [/olist] In order to destroy things you need any building that has "burn apparel" bill (ex: campfire, cremator) and it also must be powered, fueled or whatever else workbench uses. Unless these conditions are fully met - items won't get recycled or destroyed. author: 1trickPwnyta
description: Makes the bed ownership/assignment mechanic sensible. Specifically: • Everyone can have a bed assigned per map (with special rules for gravships - see 08/26/2025 update below), so beds don't get unassigned while caravaning. • Adds the ability to select a colonist or animal and right-click on a bed to assign. Multiple selected pawns can be assigned to a double bed at once. • Adds a search bar to the bed assignment dialog. • When assigning a second member to a double bed, brings the first member's love partners to the top of the list. • Adds an unassignment gizmo when you click on a bed. • Adds a gizmo to select and go to a bed's owner. • Also applies these features to other colonist-assigned buildings, such as thrones and deathrest caskets. • Allows pawns to find a chair to sleep in instead of resorting to the ground when no bed is available because chairs still provide comfort when sleeping (can be turned off in settings). ________________________________________________ <size=18px><color=#5aa9d6>Updates</color></size> 04/22/2026: Add go to owner gizmo 11/23/2025: Fix bugs with right-click assigning animals to beds and being able to assign humans to animal beds 10/09/2025: Add compatibility with Reverse Commands 09/03/2025: Add additional logging in dev mode 08/26/2025: Support for gravships by allowing one bed per pawn per map on substructure and one not on substructure. author: jamaicancastle
description: [img]https://img.litet.net/logos/Info.png[/img] Update of jamaicancastles mod https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1307441653 [img]https://img.litet.net/logos/Notice.png[/img] [table] [tr][td][url=https://discord.gg/h5TY6DA][img]https://img.litet.net/logos/Discord.png[/img][/url][/td] [td][url=https://github.com/emipa606/Shoo][img]https://img.litet.net/logos/Github.png[/img][/url][/td] [/tr] [tr] [td][img]https://img.litet.net/logos/SafeToAdd.png[/img][/td] [td][img]https://img.litet.net/logos/SafeToRemove.png[/img][/td] [/tr] [/table] [img]https://img.litet.net/logos/OriginalDescription.png[/img] Update 3/16/24: Now supports version 1.5. Rebalanced shooing chance so that it's more consistent across a broader spectrum of common animals, while still penalizing very large and untameable animals as intended. Adds a new designator that allows you to harmlessly shoo wild animals away from your base. Troubled by animals wandering into your buildings as you construct them? Need a way to discourage pests from eating up your fields? The Shoo designator (found in the Orders menu or when a wild animal is selected) will order a pawn assigned to Handling to shoo animals away from them. Animals inside your base will automatically move through doors if necessary to leave. Animals that are blocked by fences are still blocked though. They'll use fence gates if possible, but if not, they'll be stuck until you provide one. Note that not all animals are equally easy to shoo; wilder and larger animals are more likely to ignore your pawns, depending on that pawn's animal taming skill. If a pawn fails to shoo an animal, they must wait a short time before trying again. Dangerous animals have a small chance to attack. ---- Compatibility: Shoo! should be safe to add to games currently in progress. It should be safe to remove as long as no pawns are in the process of shooing animals, no animals are marked for shooing, and no animals are currently fleeing from having been shooed. --- Ludeon forums: https://ludeon.com/forums/index.php?topic=39160.0 Dropbox [1.1/Harmony 2]: https://www.dropbox.com/s/zqb708lysi4hyzm/Shoo%21.zip?dl=0 Dropbox [1.0/B19]: https://www.dropbox.com/s/t6hqzsm8k9pg8hn/Shoo%21%201.0.zip?dl=0 Dropbox [B18]: https://www.dropbox.com/s/ip67qrj1rb3vek3/Shoo%21%20B18.zip?dl=0 ---- This mod includes the Harmony 2.0 patching library. author: legodude17
description: [img]https://img.litet.net/logos/Info.png[/img] Update of legodude17s mod https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2398365712 [img]https://img.litet.net/logos/Notice.png[/img] [table] [tr][td][url=https://discord.gg/h5TY6DA][img]https://img.litet.net/logos/Discord.png[/img][/url][/td] [td][url=https://github.com/emipa606/SmarterDeconstructionAndMining][img]https://img.litet.net/logos/Github.png[/img][/url][/td] [/tr] [tr] [td][img]https://img.litet.net/logos/SafeToAdd.png[/img][/td] [td][img]https://img.litet.net/logos/SafeToRemove.png[/img][/td] [/tr] [/table] [img]https://img.litet.net/logos/OriginalDescription.png[/img] Stops your pawns from collapsing roofs on top of themselves while deconstructing and mining. Great for tearing down buildings all in one go, removing random structures without worrying about the roofs, removing mountains, and just generally not worrying so much. [h1]Mod Options[/h1] - Toggle roof checks on deconstruction - Toggle roof checks on mining - Toggle cancelling orders on mountain roofs - Toggle removing mountain roofs - Research required to remove mountain roofs When the option "Toggle removing mountain roofs" is off and the option "Toggle cancelling orders on mountain roofs" is on and pawns find a mountain roof that would collapse if they deconstructed or mined something, you will get a message and the designation will be cancelled. If you want to force them to do it, prioritize the work with the right click menu. [h1]Compatibility[/h1] Should work with everything. Drop a comment if something seems to break. Expanded Roofing and Raise the Roof: This mod will automatically pick up on these mods and configure itself accordingly, changing "Toggle removing mountain roofs" to true and "Research required to remove mountain roofs" to the research added by the mod. [h1]Performance[/h1] Should not have any noticeable impact. [h1]FAQ[/h1] Q: Does this mod allow you to remove mountain roofs? A: Only when colonists are preparing to mine/deconstruct, if the setting is on. It will not allow you to designate mountain roofs for removal manually. For that, use a mod like [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1624893841]Absolutely No Roof by NitroDev[/url] or [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=854279622]Roofless by Rakeki[/url]. author: Chicken Plucker, Taranchuk
description: Save precious time and arrest a downed prisoner without the need of a room! "Arrest here" allows you to turn downed pawns into prisoners without having to quickly build a prison during raids or defense where a prison room isn't readily available. The following mod adds: - Ability to arrest a downed pawn without prison room What is CPERS? Captured Persons or prisoners are types of protected persons covered by the law of armed conflict (LOAC). "CPERS" is the abbreviated short term for these individuals. What does "Arrest Here!" do? You can arrest a prisoner without the need of a prison room. What is the difference between this mod and "Imprisonment on the go!"? - 3 second delay until arrest is performed successfully, rather than instantly - zip tie sound effect played, rather than chains clinking - Says "Arrest Here", rather than "Imprison (name of pawn)" - Presentation and art style Combat Extended Compatible? name: Allow Tool
author: UnlimitedHugs
description: Version: 3.14.0 A set of tools to make your life on the Rim a bit easier. Easily forbid and unforbid items, select similar things, have things hauled urgently and affect the entire map with powerful new tool extensions. All tools are found in the Architect > Orders menu. Right-click tools with the small mouse icon to access their special context actions. Pressing the Context Action key ("Equals" by default) will activate the first right-click menu action of the tool you are holding. All tools are accessible from anywhere by pressing their shortcut key without opening the menu. See the Keyboard configuration panel in the options menu to customize the hotkeys.

name: Blueprints Forked - 1.6
author: Defi
description: Blueprints allow the quick construction of repetitive rooms/areas. Features Create blueprint Use the 'Create' designator to drag over an area with existing constructions. Floors, walls and furniture will all be designated, and included in the blueprint. once created, a popup will appear with a default name, giving you the option to set a more meaningful name. NOTE: Only constructions owned by you will be included, use the 'Claim' order if necessary. Place blueprint Once you've created a blueprint, you can use the new button to place copies of that blueprint. Blueprints can be rotated as normal. With a blueprint selected, you'll see an outline of what will be build on the main view, and a list of items and total cost in the lower left info panel. In this panel, you can click on furniture and walls made of stuff to change what stuff should be used in their construction. NOTE: You can shift-click with a designator selected to use the planning mode. In this case, any walls in the blueprint will be used to create a plan for your future rooms. This might be useful for mining out the required space. Rename, import & export blueprints Once you've created a blueprint, you can right click the blueprint button to rename, remove or export the blueprint. Exported blueprints will be saved in the same location as RimWorlds save games and config files, in a directory called "Blueprints". If a blueprint has been exported, an option to remove and delete the exported blueprint will also appear. You can import previously exported blueprints by right clicking the 'Create' button, and selecting the blueprint from the list of available blueprints. NOTE: While you can import/export blueprints between games, be careful with doing so when a blueprint contains (modded) items that are not available in the current game. If you import a blueprint containing items that are unavailable, an error will pop up, and the offending item will be deleted from the blueprint. I've tried to make sure the rest of the blueprint is still usable, but your results may vary.

Basically anything that has not been researched can be used but not repaired. name: No Hemogen Farm Medical Alert
author: Dark
description: Patches the "Medical Emergency" alert to ignore extreme blood loss on prisoners that are set to the "Hemogen Farm" or "Bloodfeed" interaction modes. Hemogen Farm prisoners are always suffering from blood loss, that's the point, so the alert that they have a life-threatening medical condition barely ever goes away in vanilla if you have more than a couple hemogen farm prisoners. Other life-threatening health conditions still trigger the alert. ## Performance Likely has a *small* negative impact on performance (especially in RimWorld 1.5+) since it has to check the prisoner's interaction mode every time. It should be fairly negligible but having many prisoners at once may make it noticeable (emphasis on *many* prisoners, though). _Thanks to zed-0xff on GitHub for a pull request that helped optimize the performance better than I was initially able to._ ## Compatibility - **Safe to add or remove from an ongoing save** - It's just one simple harmony patch, so it really shouldn't conflict with anything at all. Let me know if you find an incompatibility. ## Known issues - If you arrest a colonist who already has life-threatening blood loss, it will still display the alert once they are a prisoner. Not enough of a problem for me to bother fixing it (If you want to take a crack at it go ahead and submit a pull request on GitHub). ### Source [Source code on GitHub](https://github.com/JTJutajoh/RimWorld.NoHemogenFarmMedicalAlert). You have my permission to update this mod in the future if RimWorld updates break it and I don't fix it myself.

name: Pillar Planner
author: astryl
description: [h1]◆ Pillar Planner ◆[/h1] Roof collapses in RimWorld are almost always a planning failure you could not see coming. The support rules live inside the engine, invisible, until sixty tiles of overhead mountain land on your miners. Pillar Planner puts those rules on screen. One small widget in the bottom-right toggle row shows exactly where your roofs will lose support once your current mining and deconstruction orders finish, and where to stand the columns that stop it. Fully standalone, with Harmony as the only requirement, and safe to add or remove at any time. [h1]✦ One Widget, Three States[/h1] [list] [*][b]Lives with the vanilla toggles[/b]: one new column icon in the bottom-right row beside zones, beauty and the roof overlay. It behaves exactly like the native toggles, checkbox, tooltip and all. [*][b]Click to cycle[/b]: off by default, then the map view, then the room view, then off again. The icon changes with the state so you always know which view you are in. [*][b]Off means off[/b]: in the default state the mod draws nothing and computes nothing. [/list] [h1]✦ The Map View: Plan Before You Dig[/h1] The map view answers one question: if every order I have queued right now gets carried out, which roofs fall? [list] [*][b]Designation aware[/b]: rock marked for mining and buildings marked for deconstruction or uninstall are treated as already gone, so the overlay shows the future, not the present. [*][b]Plans count too[/b]: wall and column blueprints and frames are treated as supports you will have, and your build roof area is treated as roof you will want. Draw the plan first and the overlay tells you whether it stands. [*][b]Colour graded danger[/b]: cells that would lose support tint orange under thin roof and red under overhead mountain, where a collapse can kill. [*][b]Ghost columns show the fix[/b]: softly pulsing column ghosts mark suggested support positions, spaced against the same 6.9 tile rule the engine itself enforces. [/list] [h1]✦ The Room View: Point and Plan[/h1] Building a great hall and not sure the roof will hold? Switch to the room view and point at it. [list] [*][b]Hover any enclosed room[/b]: a blue outline confirms the room is recognized, and cells too far from a wall to keep a roof light up at once. [*][b]Pillar ghosts scoped to the room[/b]: suggested column positions appear only for the room under your cursor, so the rest of the map stays clean. [*][b]Great for pre-builds[/b]: because planned walls count as supports, you can hover a room that exists only as blueprints and place its pillars before a single wall is up. [/list] [h1]✦ Reads Like Vanilla, Runs Like Nothing[/h1] [list] [*][b]True engine rules[/b]: support is computed with the same 6.9 tile radius and roof connectivity the game uses, not an approximation. [*][b]Vanilla assets and effects[/b]: the ghosts are the real column graphic drawn through the game's own ghost and blueprint shaders, so the overlay looks native and costs almost nothing to draw. [*][b]Event driven[/b]: the overlay recomputes only when roofs, supports or orders actually change, and never while the widget is off. [*][b]Fails safe[/b]: if anything ever goes wrong the planner switches itself off and logs once. It can never break your game. [*][b]No save data[/b]: nothing is written to your save. Add it or remove it whenever you like. [/list] [h1]✦ Requirements[/h1] [list] [*][b]Harmony[/b] (brrainz.harmony), the only dependency. [/list] [hr][/hr] [i]Built for RimWorld 1.6. Pure overlay, no defs, no save data. Columns stay in the Structure build menu, the planner just tells you where they belong.[/i] [hr][/hr] [h3] My Quality Commitment:[/h3] [list] [*] [b]Fully Tested:[/b] Every feature and line of code has been thoroughly tested in-game to ensure it functions as intended and integrates smoothly. [*] [b]Active Support:[/b] I am fully committed to maintaining this mod. If you encounter any bugs, compatibility issues, or unintended behavior, please report them in the comments or a dedicated discussion thread. [*] [b]No Abandonware:[/b] I will actively patch, refine, and update this mod to keep it working and up to standard. [*] [b]No Coffee:[/b] I will never ask for donations for AI created / assisted mods. I share these in the hopes they spark joy for someone, making AI generated content and then begging for money that could go to artists and people more deserving is NOT responsible AI usage. [/list]

name: [LC] Consolidated Traits
author: Rainbeau Flambe (original) & Kiame Vivacity (exDev) & Luca (Current Maintainer)
description: When I started looking for a mod to add more traits to the game, I quickly realized three things about the various trait collection mods that are available: they all have some traits I really like, but also some I dislike, and none of them had all the traits I wanted; they don't necessarily work very well together due to conceptual overlaps or conflicts; and some of them are buggy in one way or another. So I decided to deal with the problem by... releasing yet another trait collection mod. *Shrug* What can I say? This one, at least, has the traits I like, all the traits I like, and nothing but the traits I like. And I'm reasonably certain it's bug-free. "Consolidated Traits" adds 45 traits to the game, almost doubling the number of traits available for pawns. The new traits are: - "Aesthete": Pawns with this trait love beautiful things, and care a lot about the beauty of their environment. - "Animal Hater": Some pawns just aren't "animal people." - "Animal Lover": Pawns with this trait, as you'd expect, are especially good at dealing with animals. - "Bipolar": Pawns with this trait will have more extreme mood swings than other pawns. - "Builder": Pawns with this trait are good at constructing things, at least if they have instructions. - "Butcher": Pawns with this trait are much faster when butchering animal corpses. - "Claustrophobic": Pawns who don't like confined spaces make poor miners. - "Cold Lover": Pawns with this trait will complain less when it's cold, but will whine more when it's hot. - "Coordinated": This one provides a slight boost to global work speed and to most skilled labor. - "Deadshot": This provides a boost to both shooting speed and accuracy. - "Deep Sleeper": Pawns with this trait won't be disturbed by others while sleeping. - "Dunce": Pawns with this trait will learn at a slower rate. - "Glutton": Pawns with this trait eat very quickly. - "Gourmet": Pawns with this trait prepare excellent food, but take their time in doing so. - "Heat Lover": This is the counterpoint to "Cold Lover." - "Inept": This trait is the counterpoint to "Coordinated." - "Inventor": Pawns with this trait are great researchers, but tend to be easily distracted. - "Ironman"/"Tough"/"Low Pain Tolerance": These traits affect a pawn's pain tolerance. - "Near-Sighted"/"Eagle-Eyed": These traits affect primarily a pawn's shooting accuracy. - "Neat Freak": Pawns with this trait appreciate the importance of a dirt-free environment. - "Nibbler": Pawns with this trait eat very slowly, picking at their food. - "Nyctophobe"/"Nyctophile": These traits make pawns either more or less afraid of the dark than usual. - "Perfectionist": Pawns with this trait try to make sure their work is done right, no matter how long it takes. - "Poor Medic"/"Skilled Medic"/"Master Medic": These traits provide penalties or buffs to medical skills. - "Quick Learner": This trait is the counterpart to "Dunce." - "Rockhound": Pawns with this trait excel at mining and stonecutting, but are a bit slow at other tasks. - "Savant": Pawns with this trait are creative geniuses, but terribly slow workers. - "Sluggish"/"Swift Reflexes": These traits affect a pawn's ability to dodge attacks. - "Sucker"/"Haggler"/"Master Trader": These traits affect prices when a pawn is trading. - "Uncouth"/"Diplomat"/"Master Diplomat": These traits affect the success of a pawn's diplomatic efforts. - "Weak Constitution"/"Strong Constitution": These traits affect a pawn's resistance to pathogens and diseases. - Rainbeau Flambe (dburgdorf) ===== Compatibility: "Consolidated Traits" should be compatible with most other mods. Even if those mods add similar traits, there shouldn't be any conflicts, as the traits are unlikely to have the same defNames. However, if you're using more than one mod that adds traits, you might end up seeing pawns with traits that don't really work well together, since the game won't have any way of knowing that trait X from mod Y duplicates or just isn't compatible with trait A from mod B. I'd recommend using my "More Trait Slots" mod. Combining a larger pool of traits with a larger set of traits per pawn can add some very interesting and uniquely individual personalities to your game. You should be able to add "Consolidated Traits" to an existing saved game without trouble, but removing the mod from a game in progress might cause problems if any pawns in the world have any of the mod's traits, which is of course very likely. ===== Credits: Some of the traits added by this mod are original. But most of them are based on traits found in "Additional Traits," "Extended Traits," "L-Traits," and/or the base version of "Pawns Are Capable!" Translators: ZombieReincarnation - Chinese ===== License: If you're a modpack maker and want to include "Consolidated Traits" in your pack, or if you're a modder and want to use it as the basis of a derivative mod, please feel free to do so. I ask only that you let me know about it. ===== If you have any (helpful) suggestions for improvement, please let me know!

name: Deathrest Pauses Biological Age
author: Crykosity
description: In base Rimworld, children do not gain growth score whilst in deathrest; this avoids an exploit in which a player could bring a child up to a maximum learning need and then suspend it whilst they deathrest, gaining high growth for no effort. However, this fix has the side-effect of disadvantaging deathresting children, as there are many days where they could be learning, but are instead forced to undertake deathrest. This mod avoids both problems by pausing biological age progression whilst a pawn deathrests. This change allows children to have the same total time to increase their growth score, while remaining thematically consistent.

name: Climate Preference Genes
author: alite
description: This mod adds 4 climate preference genes, 2 that shift the comfortable temperature range by 15°C and 2 that shift by 30°C. This means that a pawn with hot climate preference will only comfortable in climates that are 31-41°C, instead of the normal 16-26, while cold climate preference will move the range to be 1-11°C. These genes do stack with similar resistances, so hot climate preference can be combined with heat super-tolerant to allow a pawn to live in environments with a temp range of 31-61°C. They can't be combined with genes that would bring their preference closer to standard though, so cold tolerant genes can't be used alongside the hot climate gene. name: Consistent Gene Inheritance (1.6 VERSION)
author: Sea, RussianGolden
description: This is an unofficial 1.6 mod version. All credits go to Sea, the original creator of the mod. Please let me know if you want this mod to be taken down. In vanilla, gene inheritance between pawns of different xenotypes for genes which have a metabolism cost is inconsistent. The mod makes it more consistent. When a pawn is impregnated by a partner of a different xenotype, their offspring is assigned a maximum metabolism value based on the following logic: 70% chance for 1, 20% chance for 2, 10% chance for 3. A pawn with maximum metabolism of 1 will not be able to inherit any genes that would push their total metabolism outside of the range { -1, 1 }. Worse still, this mechanic is calculated one gene at a time. If a pawn is created with a maximum metabolic rating of 3 and the first gene it inherits is a 3 metabolism gene then it won't be able to inherit any more genes with a metabolism cost unless it first inherits one with a negative metabolism cost. This means that the likelihood to inherit genes is not only based on the cost of the gene but the order in which the genes are present on the pawn. This mod removes the maximum metabolism value entirely so that inheritance works consistently all the time: 50% chance per gene for each parent, like in vanilla.

name: Geist Xenotype
author: Sovereign
description: A race of faceless assassins, their genome refined over the centuries by competing geist clans. They're nimble, silent, and deadly, with genetically-instilled sense of duty that ensures complete dedication to their mission - and that any failure is deeply regretted. Geists strike unseen, hidden in the mist produced by their smoke glands, with an impossible precision granted by the electroreceptors embedded within the faceplates of their featureless skulls. However, the same ability that sharpens their senses makes them uniquely vulnerable to electromagnetic currents, able to be felled with a single concentrated burst of EMP.

description: A mod I commissioned Thekiborg to make and now maintain myself. Adds a gene to rip genes of your choice from downed pawns, killing the target in the process. You can adjust in the settings whether it becomes an endogene or a xenogene.

name: Genetics! Mushkin
author: The Biomes! Mod Team
description: The first of a potential series centered around adding new xenotypes and improving vanilla xenotypes by the Biomes! mod team. The mushkin in this mod originate from the first version of Biomes! Caverns back in 2016 when they were an HAR mod requiring race. They have since been heavily revamped in both lore and design. They are inspired in part from myconids from Dungeon and Dragons as well as other fictional fungi folk. Do you like fungi? Do you like bizarre humanoids? Well then prepare yourself for Mushkin, the xenotype formed from a fungal bond! This mod adds multiple mushkin castes/roles that each function a little differently with abilities based on their purpose. From the leader-role Crowncaps to the farmer-role Patchphae, you can have an entire colony of just the lovely little shroomy folk. You can even turn other pawns into mushkin if you have the right caste for it! Mushkin as a whole have unique upsides and downsides, some of which are shared across the castes, but others are not. They are all however meant to be as well-balanced as possible, especially when it comes to metabolism. Safe to add, not safe to remove. Requires Harmony and the Biotech DLC.

name: Goliann Xenotype
author: Sovereign
description: A xenohuman race of gentle giants, the Goliann were engineered as bodyguards for the wealthy. Unconcerned with long-term survival prospects of their race, Golianns' creators left their reproductive functions atrophied for the sake of increased physical performance, making them a rare sight in the wild reaches of rimworlds. Intended to bond fellow Goliann within their VIPs security detail and no-one else, the xenotype is deeply solitary, rarely staying long in all but the most accommodating communities.

Genes: -Greatly reduced hemogen capacity: x25% max hemogen (+3 metabolism) -Reduced hemogen capacity: x50% max hemogen (+2 metabolism) -Somewhat reduced hemogen capacity: x75% max hemogen (+1 metabolism) -Somewhat increased hemogen capacity: x125% max hemogen (-1 metabolism) -Increased hemogen capacity: x150% max hemogen (-2 metabolism) -Greatly increased hemogen capacity: x175% max hemogen (-3 metabolism) -Extremely increased hemogen capacity: x200% max hemogen (-4 metabolism) -Super increased hemogen capacity: x225% max hemogen (-5 metabolism) -Hyper increased hemogen capacity: x250% max hemogen (-6 metabolism) -Minor archite hemogen capacity: x200% max hemogen (costs 1 archite) -Archite hemogen capacity: x300% max hemogen (costs 2 archite) -Major archite hemogen capacity: x400% max hemogen (costs 3 archite) Also includes a gene to reset the multiplier to its default

name: ReSplice: Charmweavers
author: Helixien
description: ReSplice is the banner under which I will release any xenotype I feel like making. Similar to ReGrowth, I aim for my additions to be vanilla friendly in both artstyle and lore. Everything added was made to fit or mirror vanilla. From a simple UI texture to a new more complex system,being as performance and vanilla friendly is the main objective I have. Inspired by the well known Succubus (and Incubus), Charmweavers are a new archite powered xenotype you can encounter and add to your colonies. They are rare, similar to sanguophages, and quite unique, offering some interesting upsides and downsides. Charmweavers are a relatively simple xenotype. They should work fine in whatever load order you have and be a nice addition, if not for the xenotype itself, then for the genes they add. ReSplice is designed to be as lightweight as possible, adding the minimum of new code required for its additions to work.

name: ReSplice: Core
author: Helixien
description: ReSplice is a mod deeply influenced by the philosophy of the Vanilla Expanded Series and my desire to make rimworld feel more immersive. As well as the fact I love xenotypes and the gene system added by Biotech. Everything added was made to fit or mirror vanilla. From a simple UI texture to a new more complex system,being as performance and vanilla friendly as possible is the main objective we have. This mod is the Core, which is a requirement for all other ReSplice mods (one day, not just yet), but don't let yourself be fooled by the name. It in itself also adds a lot of new content to your game. ReSplice is designed to be as lightweight as possible, adding the minimum of new code required for its auditions to work.

name: Rim-Elves
author: VexedTrees
description:
Adds a new xenotype, the elves - a race of towering, majestic, and bigoted humanoids. Elves were perfected on a bygone glitterworld; from there, they've spread the influence of their imperium outwards from the core worlds and into the rim.

Take on the Elven Imperium: supremacists from the stars with a perchance for nature, slaughter, and general morally corrupt behavior. Do not rest until the elven scum has been pushed into the dirt, and their cities razed - least they do the same to you.

Elves sleep less, learn faster, and are more in tune with the physic wavelength of the universe. However they're less suited for hard labor, slightly racist assholes, and their bodies are less efficient at processing chemicals; meaning drugs and alcohol are two times as potent to them as they are to a baseline human. Regardless if you enjoy playing Rimworld for the long plays, dragged-out multi-generational colonies, or peaceful agrarian societies, you'll probably love playing as the elves.

(Important! If the size of your elves are wrong or weird, make sure any mods that have size scaling are loaded above Vanilla Expanded Framework, mods like Humanoid Alien Races, Character Editor, Varied Body Sizes, etc.)

(Also important: I do not support bigotry or any form of directed hate in any way, shape, or form. If you are a bigot or homo/trans/phobe, please, do me a favor, get off your computer and go learn how to be a less shitty human being. If you can't do that then don't sub to my mods, have a nice day!)

name: Rim-Gnoblins
author: VexedTrees
description:
Adds a new xenotype, the gnoblins - a race of short, green, and raucous humanoids. Gnoblins hail from the suffocating insides of some distant forgeworld, being perfectly adapted for quickly darting in and out of maintenance shafts and foundry exhausts. Perfectly designed for guerrilla warfare, zerg-rush tactics, or just general mischief.

Face the green tide with either the shard-addicted gnoblin punks with their guns and rockets or the endless legions of the medieval gnoblin horde.

Cultivate your own horde with a breeding populace for fast-developing gnoblins to feed headfirst into the battlefield, or use your gnoblins to kite raiders and pick off the weak before they can even retaliate - regardless, something malicious is always brewing with the gnoblins.

(Important! If the size of your gnoblins is wrong or weird, make sure any mods that have size scaling are loaded above Vanilla Expanded Framework, mods like Humanoid Alien Races, Character Editor, Varied Body Sizes, etc.)

name: Vanilla Vehicles Expanded - Tier 3 Russian
author: I'm sorry
description: Перевод мода cделал для себя. В нескольких местах адаптировал мод, чтобы не потерялся смысл вложенный автором. Загружать после оригинального мода. Сообщайте об ошибках в комментариях, если что исправлю. Углубитесь в мир технологических достижений транспортных средств с расширением третьего уровня для "Vanilla Vehicles Expanded". Хотя термин "Уровень 3" для некоторых может вызывать ассоциации с футуристическими научно-фантастическими машинами, мой фокус оставался на создании высокоспециализированных и редких транспортных средств, которые добавляют глубину и разнообразие вашему игровому опыту. В этом расширении представлено 11 тщательно разработанных транспортных средств. От долгожданной мобильной артиллерии и функциональных холодильных грузовиков до мощных танков, оснащенных коаксиальными пулеметами — здесь найдется транспортное средство на любой вкус. Добавив интерактивности в игровой процесс, эти транспортные средства не будут доступны сразу. Вы найдете их в разрушенном виде, разбросанные по карте. Чтобы получить знания и возможность производить эти транспортные средства, игрокам сначала нужно будет их найти, забрать и восстановить. Хотя эти разрушенные сокровища могут появляться на любом типе карты, на картах с дорогами их будет больше, что добавляет элемент стратегии в выбор и исследование территории. Этот мод добавляет множество новых транспортных средств, включая: Классические автомобили: Поднимите дух своих колонистов с помощью этих винтажных красавцев. Они не только для показа — они также улучшают настроение при использовании. Суперкары: Созданные для дороги, они являются вершиной скорости, но только если ваша колония соединена с пунктом назначения дорогами. Боевые танки и боевые машины пехоты: Они созданы для сражений и оснащены тяжелой броней и мощным оружием — настоящий актив для любой колонии, сталкивающейся с угрозами. Мобильная артиллерия: Отвечайте на угрозы в реальном времени, обрушивая на врагов различные виды снарядов. Универсальные вертолеты: От перевозки грузов до перемещения войск — эти воздушные средства удовлетворяют самые разные потребности.

name: Vanilla Vehicles Expanded Russian
author: I'm sorry
description: Перевод мода cделал для себя. В нескольких местах адаптировал мод, чтобы не потерялся смысл вложенный автором. Загружать после оригинального мода. Сообщайте об ошибках в комментариях, если что исправлю. "Vanilla Vehicles Expanded" - долгожданный мод, использующий фреймворк транспортных средств от Smash Phil. Основная цель мода - добавить реалистичную и увлекательную механику, связанную с транспортными средствами всех видов, в игру. Здесь речь идет не только о машинах, но и о лодках и самолетах. Мод полон контента и новых производственных цепочек, позволяющих игрокам углубиться в производство транспортных средств. Транспортные средства разделены на разные категории и уровни, способствуя общему прогрессу. Вы не просто будете создавать машину и кататься на ней - вы будете изучать другие транспортные средства и варианты, которые предлагает этот мод. Каждая машина, лодка и самолет будет иметь свою определенную цель, и благодаря системе уровней будет легко понять различия между разными транспортными средствами. Этот мод использует систему окрашивания, добавленную в фреймворк транспортных средств, что позволяет вам полностью настроить узор и цвета каждого из ваших транспортных средств. Будь то камуфлированный бронированный подразделение или розовый бомбардировочный эскадрилья, этот мод имеет всё это.

author: pashka
description: Русский язык для мода WVC - Work Modes. Для того, что бы дополнить существующий перевод (если он есть) - поместите выше основного мода. Что бы полностью применить данный перевод - поместите ниже основного мода. Данный мод добавляет 10 новых режимов поведения для механоидов: Поиск и уничтожение — Механоиды, независимо от их типа, будут искать врагов и пытаться их уничтожить. Работа и подзарядка — Механоиды будут работать автономно в зависимости от их типа. После выполнения работы или невозможности её выполнения — они отключатся. Сопровождение и подзарядка — Механоиды, независимо от их типа, будут сопровождать хозяина и, если необходимо, перейдут на зарядку. Работа, сопровождение и подзарядка — Механоиды будут сопровождать хозяина, если у них нет работы, а также при необходимости перейдут на зарядку. Ожидание противника — Механоиды отключатся до появления противника, затем они включатся и направятся к ним. Работа и ожидание — Механоиды, в зависимости от типа, будут работать, а когда появится враг, они бросят всё и отправятся его уничтожать. Если у них не будет работы, они просто отключатся. Засада — Механоиды будут отключены до тех пор, пока противник не приблизится к ним, а затем нападут на них. Защита — Механоиды, независимо от их типа, будет атаковать врагов, которые подойдут слишком близко. Сопровождение при врагах — Механоиды, независимо от типа, будут сопровождать хозяина, но только если на карте есть противники. Если их нет, механоиды отключатся. Работа если всё спокойно — Механоиды будут работать, до тех пор, пока на карте нет противников. В случае опасности они будут пытаться добраться до безопасного места.

name: Ranged DPS (Continued)
author: Pausbrak
description: [img]https://i.imgur.com/buuPQel.png[/img] Update of Pausbraks mod https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2132037199 [img]https://i.imgur.com/pufA0kM.png[/img] [table] [tr] [td][url=https://discord.gg/h5TY6DA][img]https://i.imgur.com/zdzzBrc.png[/img][/url][/td] [td][url=https://github.com/emipa606/RangedDPS][img]https://i.imgur.com/kTkpTOE.png[/img][/url][/td] [/tr] [tr] [td][img]https://i.imgur.com/WjDSfUn.png[/img][/td] [td][img]https://i.imgur.com/h5VwTNL.png[/img][/td] [/tr] [/table] [img]https://i.imgur.com/Z4GOv8H.png[/img] Finally, a way to easily compare ranged weapons and turrets! [h1]Added Stats[/h1] This mod adds several stats to weapons, pawns, and turrets: [h2]Weapons[/h2] [h3]Max ranged DPS[/h3] This stat represents the maximum possible DPS a weapon could achieve if every bullet hit. This is unlikely to offer a realistic DPS for most weapons, especially ones with low base accuracy. [h3]Average ranged DPS[/h3] This stat represents the best possible DPS a pawn could realistically achieve with this weapon, based only on the inherent accuracy of the weapon. Keep in mind that real DPS will always be lower because it's impossible for a pawn to achieve 100% shooting accuracy. The stat lists the range with the highest DPS -- click it for a detailed chart that covers the full range of the weapon. [h2]Pawns[/h2] [h3]Ranged DPS[/h3] (Only visible if the pawn has a ranged weapon equipped) This stat represents the best DPS this specific pawn can achieve with their currently equipped weapon, based on their current shooting accuracy. This is the most accurate DPS stat available and is the one you should use when trying to see how effective your pawns' current loadouts are. The stat lists the range with the highest DPS -- click it for a detailed chart that covers the full range of the weapon. Note that this can be a different range than the weapon's optimal range! Poor shooters suffer at long ranges even with a legendary sniper rifle. [h2]Turrets[/h2] [h3]Max ranged DPS[/h3] This stat represents the maximum possible DPS the turret could achieve if every bullet hit, and is equivalent to the same stat on weapons. [h3]Weapon ranged DPS[/h3] This stat is the equivalent to "Average ranged DPS" of weapons, and represents the stats of the built-in weapon of the turret. Turrets also have a separate Shooting Accuracy stat just like pawns, and this does NOT take that into account. Use this stat if you want to compare the turret to a gun, but keep in mind that real DPS will generally be lower because most turrets have less that 100% shooting accuracy. [h3]Ranged DPS[/h3] This stat is the equivalent to "Ranged DPS" for pawns. It represents the DPS this turret can achieve, factoring in both the inherent accuracy of the turret's weapon and the shooting accuracy of the turret mount. This is the most accurate DPS stat available and is the one you should use when trying to see how effective this turret is, or how it compares to a pawn's Ranged DPS. The stat lists the range with the highest DPS -- click it for a detailed chart that covers the full range of the turret. Note that this can be a different range than the turret weapon's optimal range! [h3]Damage per resource[/h3] Most turrets require resources to operate in the form of barrel refurbishment or ammunition. This stat measures how efficient the turret is at turning those resources into damage. For every unit of resource (e.g. steel) spent rearming the turret, you can expect about this much damage done at the turret's optimal range, accounting for missed shots. The stat lists the range with the highest damage per resource -- click it for a detailed chart that covers the full range of the turret. [h3]Max damage per resource[/h3] This stat represents the maximum possible damage per unit of resource the turret could achieve if every bullet hit. [h1]Compatibility Notes[/h1] This mod should be compatible with all XML-only weapon mods. It will almost certainly NOT give accurate results for modded weapons with exotic abilities and may even cause errors. 200% Not Compatible With Combat Extended™ Seriously, don't even ask. CE completely reworks ranged combat. A separate version would be need to be rewritten from the ground up to support CE [h1]Translation Credits[/h1] - Korean translation supplied by inbae on Steam Feel free to submit translations for your preferred language! Or corrections/updates to existing translations, for that matter. Unfortunately I can't do much to maintain these translations myself, so I'll be relying on fan submissions to keep them updated. Pull requests on Github are best, but I can also accept the raw files. name: Verbose-Forked
author: Elduckerich
description: RimWorld is already quite mouthy when it comes to animal descriptions and specific items, but otherwise, the info-box may as well not exist. This mod expands RimWorld's descriptiveness and overall vocabulary in a more Dwarf Fortress kind of way. That doesn't mean that I've pumped a bunch of useless nonsense into item descriptions just for a fun one-time read. Only a handful of nonsense! Verbose generally splits its changes into three types: Casual, Actual, and Factual. Some entries overlap, and there are no hard or fast rules. My general goal is to ensure that when you look into surgery entries, you don't feel like you're missing out on critical information, and when reading a pawn's thoughts, they don't sound overly robotic. -- Mod Compatibility -- This mod is compatible with most mods. Since it primarily modifies text descriptions, there should be minimal chance of causing conflicts or crashes. If you've found an exception, please leave a comment so I can investigate. There is no cross-mod integration yet, but I plan to support this after finishing work on Vanilla and DLC content. If you have mod suggestions, please let me know in the comments. -- Addons and Permissions -- I give anyone full permission to add on to my work if they see fit. You also have permission to port this mod to other platforms that do not support Steam Workshop. Just note that all maintenance responsibilities will fall on you. I'm happy to explain how the mod works, but I can't offer direct support for forks. Add-On: "Verbose for the Faint of Heart" – This toned-down patch reduces swearing and removes potentially upsetting content. Ideal for users with emetophobia or those who prefer lighter descriptions. Available at: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2950364015 -- Report Spelling or Grammar Mistakes -- If you find typos or clumsy phrasing, feel free to report them. Include the entry name, error location, and your suggested fix. -- Support -- If you'd like to support my work, visit: https://ko-fi.com/dubiousphoenix

name: Time As a Slave
author: llunak
description: This simple mod provides 'Time as a slave' and 'Time as a visitor' records for each pawn. The game provides per-pawn records such as 'Time as a colonist', 'Time hauling', etc., but when Ideology introduced slavery, it omitted adding 'Time as a slave' record. This mod adds that. It also adds 'Time as a visitor'. This mod is also a weak dependency for the 'More Precepts' mod - if a 'Newcomer Attitude' precept is used, it uses this mod to count correctly stay at the colony for slaves. GitHub: https://github.com/llunak/rimworld-timeasslave

name: Who shot my leg off?
author: Tixiv
description: A quality of life mod for Rimworld Did you ever notice that your colonist had a scar or a missing body part, and you just asked yourself: How did that happen? This mod will solve that problem. Now what happened and when it occurred will be displayed on each Hediff (health condition) forever. The funny thing is: Rimworld actually already has this feature somewhat built in, since Heddifs already save the log string, and the timestamp when they occurred forever. However the log entry isn't displayed in the Hediff anymore after it has been purged from the battle log of the pawn, which might actually be a game bug or oversight. The nice thing is that this means the data is already there in savegames, so this mod will also work on injuries that occurred before it was installed! Additionally to fixing this game oversight, this mod also displays when the Hediff occurred right in the Hediff itself. No need to click to the battle log anymore! Compatibility: Absolutely no issues expected. This mod patches only the function that get's the battle log entry on a Hediff. That really shouldn't interfere with anything. The mod is also safe to remove at any time.

author: Fluffy

name: CanIReinstall
author: Lensrub
description: A simple mod that adds to the description of all buildings a line informing about the ability to packed a building into an item and reinstall it elsewhere. Have you ever had a situation where you built something in a temporary first available spot, hoping to move it to a more convenient place later, only to discover that it couldn't be possible? And the attempt to find information about this before building in the description window also failed? Then this mod is for you. Just before building anything, press "i" and check, can you place the building wherever convenient, or whether you should prepare spot where it will stand for the entire game. And why this isn't in vanilla?

name: Chronos Pointer - Schedule Menu Enhancement
author: CoolNether123, TreadTheDawnGames, ZManJim
description: Enhances the schedule panel with dynamic time indicators for improved colony management and time tracking. Features: - Hours Bar: A dedicated bar above the schedule's hour numbers, visually representing the day and night cycles. - Dynamic Time Pointers: - Arrow Pointer: An arrow that moves in real-time above the schedule, precisely indicating the current hour and minute. - Hours Bar Time Cursor: A small vertical line within the "Hours Bar" that accurately traces the current time, dynamically changing color with the daylight level. - Full-Height Time Indicator: A vertical line spanning all pawns' schedules, moving in sync with the other pointers to show the current time for all colonists at once. - Customizable Colors: Adjust colors for all indicators, cursors, and bar segments to match your visual preferences. - Incident Interactions: The "Hours Bar" updates its colors and visual effects to reflect current map conditions like Solar Flares, Eclipses, Toxic Fallout, Volcanic Winter, and Auroras. - Comprehensive Settings: All elements, including appearance, visibility, and behavior, are fully configurable through the settings menu. This mod provides an intuitive and visually appealing way to track time in RimWorld, making it easier to manage colonist schedules and activities throughout the day and night cycle. All features can be toggled and customized in the mod settings, allowing you to tailor the experience to your liking. Integration: - Other mods can reuse Chronos Pointer through its public API. Any issues or have some ideas? Come by my discord at: https://discord.gg/QYBBaRkKWs

This mod was born out of a simple need: Stop the UI clutter and let me find the best caster for the job instantly.

name: CM Color Coded Mood Bar [1.1+]
author: CrashM
description:
Color code each pawn's mood bar within the colonist bar based on their current mood.

Red: extreme mental break threshold
Orange: major mental break threshold
Yellow: minor mental break threshold
Gray: neutral mood
Light Blue: content
Green: happy

Also includes:

Break Box, an outline to highlight when the colonist is in a break mood, useful for "larger" colonists (default on). This can be drawn beneath or on top of the colonist to further highlight the colonist (default beneath).
Schedule Box, an outline to show the colonists current schedule (default off).
Illness Icon, an icon that is displayed when the colonist has an illness that requires immunity (default on).
Bleeding Icon, an icon that is displayed when the colonist is bleeding with 3 different sizes based on bleed rate, Large lt 8 hours until death, Medium lt 24 hours, Small gt 24 hours (default on).
Thermal Icons, icons for when colonists are suffereing hypotherma/heatstroke (minor and above).
Love Relationship Icons, icons for colonists that are in relationships (heart for lovers and fiancés, rings for married couples).

name: Dawn of a New Day
author: AlenDio
description: Adds a customizable header overlay that displays at the start of the day. Features Go to: Options > Mod options > "Dawn of a New Day" # Enabled => You can toggle the overlay anytime without restarting. # Screenshot Mode => When in Screenshot Mode (F11), if enabled the overlay won't be displayed. # Show Example => Shows your current overlay configuration in the next tick to ease and familarize with the settings. - Appearance Section # Show Highlight => Adds a low-opacity light background behind the overlay. # Scale => Scales the whole overlay to your like (From 0.5x to 4x). # Offset Presets => Helps you to choose an offset of your liking without trial and error. # Offset sliders (px) => Choose offsets on X and Y axis at pixel-precision (From 0 To {Screen Resolution}). # Line Width (%) => Choose the width in percentage of the line that divides the Upper from Bottom (From 0 to 100). # Line Thickness (px) => Choose the thickness in pixels of the line that divides the Upper from Bottom (From 0 to 100) # Line Padding (px) => Choose the padding in pixels that divides the line from the Upper and Bottom (From 0 to 100) - Duration Section # Total Display Duration => Choose the total duration of the overlay in seconds (From 0 to 120). # Fade In Duration => Choose the duration of the overlay fading-in in seconds (From 0 to {Total Display}). # Fade Out Duration => Choose the duration of the overlay fading-out in seconds (From 0 to {Total Display}). - Text Section # Choose Font Family => Choose an custom OS font to replace the default game font of the text. # Font Size => Choose the character size of the text (From 1 to 256). # Outline Thickness => Choose the thickness of the outline of the text (From 0 to 10). # Bold => Enable to add bold style to the text. # Italic => Enable to add italic style to the text. # Text Color => Choose from the color presets the color of the text. # Outline Color => Choose from the color presets the color of the outline of the text. - Label Format Section # Upper Text Format => Choose the format of the Upper text. # Bottom Text Format => Choose the format of the Bottom text. * {D/d} => Full Day * {Y/y} => Full Year [eg. 5500] / 2-Digit Year [eg. 00] * {Q/q} => CAPS Quadrum / Quadrum * {S/s} => CAPS Season / Season * {H/h} => Full Hour [eg. 06] / Hour [eg. 6] - Sound Section # Enabled => Toggle the sound that starts with the overlay. # Choose Sound => Choose a custom sound from the catalogue. # Sound Volume => Choose the volume of the sound (From 1 to 200). # Pitch Volume => Choose the pitch of the sound (From 1 to 200). - Extra Section # Starts at Zero => Enable to start the count of the days from 0 instead of 1. # Show Every X Days => Choose how often the overlay displays (From 1 to 1200) [eg. X=10 => DAY 10, DAY 20, DAY 30, ...]. # Trigger Hour => Choose at what hour of the day the overlay displays (From 0 to 23). # Day Relative => Choose what the value of day will be relative to. * Settle => Day will be relative to the day the colonists settled. * Quadrum => Day will be relative to the quadrum resetting itself after 15 days. * Season => Day will be relative to the season resetting itself after it ends. * Year => Day will be relative to the year resetting itself after 60 days. Can be safely added or removed from existing saves at any time.

Instead of implementing this per mod I wrote this mod instead. This mod adds two small buttons at the top of the mod-options window for all mods (apart from HugsLib as that uses its own options-file for all mod-settings). With these you can export the current mod-settings to a folder (default is the Desktop-folder but is changable in the mod-settings) and the file is then used to import the mod-settings. This can trigger warnings/errors depending on how the mod-settings are applied by the mod. If you notice some issues with a mods settings a simple way to reapply the imported settings is to restart the game. There is also an option to export or import all active mods settings from this mods settings-window. name: Improved Need Indicator
description: A pawn has several needs. If you hover over those needs, you'll see a tooltip. This tooltip has some helpful text, but it could be better. Improved Need Indicator adds helpful timers to a need's tooltip so you know exactly how long you have until that need is unfulfilled. Implemented: * Food * Indoors * Outdoors * Recreation * Rest Why? Because I spent three hours building a spreadsheet to figure out how long my pawns sleep and just knew there had to be a better way. Sleep alone is a complicated formula using the pawn's own 'Rest Rate Multiplier', bed type, bed material, bed quality, and number of sleep accelorators. Did you know making the bed out of marble to get that sweet beauty bonus makes your pawn sleep longer? Or that Jade doesn't count as stone and works the same as wood? Who knew?! I fricken didn't. Don't fall down the same rabbit hole I did. We've done the work for you here. Install the mod, shower us with praise, and sleep better than ever. Who AmCh: Coding and Translations (Chinese Simplified and Chinese Traditional) Ferchu: Translations (Spanish and Spanish Latin) Missionz3r0: Coding and DevOps I (missionz3r0) want to convey my thanks to AmCh. They did the lions share of the coding in this mod. Be sure to shower them with adulations. GitHub: https://github.com/AmCh-Q/RimWorldMod_ImprovedNeedIndicator Some of our other mods: More Sleep Accelerators: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3201556917 Need Bar Overflow: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2566316158

name: Mark That Pawn
author: Mlie
description: [img]https://img.litet.net/logos/Self-Info.png[/img] You get a large raid and looking through the pawns you find one that would be excellent to capture, but sadly you lose them in the action. You later find their corpse blown up by one of your rockets. With this mod you can mark any pawn with a selection of icons to make them easier to keep track of. Mod-options: [list] [*]Change the size and position of the icon [*]Change the icon-set used [*]Relative icon-size based on pawn-size [*]Increase the icon-size when zoomed out, selectable strength [*]Have different icon-sets based on the pawn type [*]Disable the gizmos based on the pawn type [*]Have the icons pulse like the question mark over traders in a caravan [*]Show all applicable icons [*]Rotating the active icon between the applicable icons [*]Show all icons when hovering the icons or selecting the pawn [*]Show on corpses [/list] You can define rules to make spawning pawns get marked automatically. The rules are defined based on: [list] [*]Weapons equipped [*]Weapon type equipped [*]Apparels equipped [*]Apparel type equipped [*]Pawn skill levels [*]Pawn traits [*]Pawn age [*]Pawn gender [*]Relations to colonists [*]Pawn category [*]Pawn has one or more permanent hediffs, like a bionic limb [*]Pawn has any bad permanent hediff, like a scar [*]Animal type [*]Faction icon [*]Ideology icon (Ideology DLC) [*]Ideology role (Ideology DLC) [*]Royalty titles (Royalty DLC) [*]Xenotype (Biotech DLC) [*]Genes (Biotech DLC) [/list] There are also priority rules that get applied based on events [list] [*]Pawn is drafted [*]Pawn is downed [*]Pawn is in a mental state [*]Pawn has one or more temporary hediffs, like an injury [/list] If you have [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2895299310]TD Find Lib[/url] active you can add rules that uses its search filters. These filters are saved in the save-game so they require and active game to add or edit. All applicable rules can also be set to only apply to one category of pawns. There is also support for the fog of war in [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2938891185]CAI 5000[/url] BadgeDefs from [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2526040241]Pawn Badge[/url] will be imported as marker-sets There are default sets of icons for each type of pawn but you can always set any icon for a specific pawn using the custom option. There is also support for vehicles using [url=https://steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/?id=3014915404]Vehicle Framework[/url]. It is very simple to add more Icon-sets as only a small xml-definition is needed to make it be selectable in the mod options. If you have suggestions for new icon-sets or new rules, please leave a comment here or on the Discord server and Ill see if I can add it to the mod! name: Modern Empire Tab
author: Astryl
description: [h1]◆ Modern Empire Tab ◆[/h1] The Empire screen from Vanilla Factions Expanded – Empire, rebuilt as a floating, resizable, dark-flat window in the style of the Modern / Nice tab suite. The Great Hierarchy becomes a pannable, zoomable org-chart of the Empire's nobility; Permits, Vassalage, and Honors are all reskinned to match. Presentation only — every action runs VFE–Empire's own logic underneath. [h1]✦ The Great Hierarchy[/h1] [list] [*][b]Top-down org / lineage tree[/b] — the Emperor at the top, each rank a row of portrait node-cards wired to the rank above, instead of a flat side-scroll. [*][b]Pan & zoom[/b] — drag to move, scroll to zoom (40–200%) toward the cursor; zoom out for a clean portrait-only overview. The view is remembered, and first opens centered on the Emperor. [*][b]Your nobles glow gold[/b] — colony colonists who hold an Imperial title get a soft gold glow on their card edge, standing out from Empire NPCs. [*][b]Click to act[/b] — click your colonist to jump the camera to them; click an Empire noble to invite them for a visit (honor cost and all). Jump-to-rank buttons and a search box round it out. [/list] [h1]✦ Permits, Vassalage & Honors[/h1] [list] [*][b]Permits[/b] — the royal permit tree redrawn flat, with prerequisite lines and colour-coded nodes (unlocked / available / locked), a detail card, and the points + return-all footer. [*][b]Vassalage[/b] — current vassals with delivery bars and tithe settings, potential vassals in a grid with range checks, and a built-in [b]mini-map[/b]: click a settlement to recentre it, click the map to jump there. [*][b]Honors[/b] — drag honors onto a noble to assign, drag them back to remove; pending honors tint gold. [*][b]Flat scrollbars[/b] throughout, matching the suite. [/list] [h1]✦ Quality of Life[/h1] [list] [*][b]One-click vanilla toggle[/b] — an icon next to the close button swaps Permits, Vassalage & Honors back to VFE-Empire's original screens (the Great Hierarchy keeps its tree). Your choice is remembered. [*][b]Always-show option[/b] — keep the Empire tab available even before you have a titled colonist, so you can browse the hierarchy at any time (toggleable). [*][b]Floating, resizable, borderless[/b] window with a clean flat close button. [*]Layout measured at runtime — UI-scale and tiny-text friendly. [*]Safe to add or remove mid-save; stores no data of its own. [/list] [h1]✦ Requirements[/h1] [list] [*][b]Vanilla Factions Expanded – Empire[/b] — required. This mod re-skins its screens; it does nothing on its own. [*][b]Vanilla Expanded Framework[/b] and [b]Harmony[/b] — as required by VFE–Empire. [/list] [h1]✦ Compatibility[/h1] [list] [*][b]No Harmony patches[/b] — the entire mod is XML class-swaps on VFE–Empire's own defs, so it slots in cleanly. [*]Conflicts only with another mod that replaces the same Empire screens. [/list] [hr][/hr] [i]Built for RimWorld 1.6. The Empire, the modern way.[/i] [hr][/hr] [h2]🛠️ Mod Disclaimer & Quality Assurance[/h2] [quote][b]A Note on Development:[/b] Parts of the code for this mod were generated using [b]Claude AI[/b]. However, this is [b]not[/b] a low-effort "AI slop" upload.[/quote] [h3]🔍 My Quality Commitment:[/h3] [list] [*][b]Fully Tested:[/b] Every feature has been tested in-game to ensure it functions as intended and integrates smoothly. [*][b]Active Support:[/b] If you encounter any bugs or compatibility issues, please report them in the comments or a discussion thread. [*][b]No Abandonware:[/b] I will actively patch and refine this mod to keep it up to standard. [/list] [i]Thank you for downloading, and happy gaming![/i] [hr][/hr]

name: Modern Faction Menu
author: Astryl
description: [h1]⚑ Modern Faction Menu[/h1] A complete, modern replacement for the Factions tab — a dark dashboard in the [b]Modern X[/b] style with faction cards, pinning, relation filters, live trend graphs, a framed territory map for every settlement, and a flavor ticker that tells you what each faction is up to right now. Modded factions are supported automatically. Click the Factions button to open it; click again to close. A toggle inside switches back to the vanilla tab at any time. [h1]✦ The Faction List[/h1] [list] [*][b]Faction cards[/b] — color-striped cards with faction icon, type, and live goodwill. [*][b]Pinning[/b] — pin the factions you care about to the top (saved per game). [*][b]Relation filters[/b] — one-click chips to show/hide hostile, neutral, and allied factions, with live counts. [*][b]Search[/b] — find any faction by name or type. [/list] [h1]✦ The Faction Page[/h1] [list] [*][b]Pinned overview[/b] — relation, goodwill bar, leader, ideoligion, lore, and the territory map stay fixed at the top while everything else scrolls. [*][b]Settlement browser[/b] — a framed map preview of any of their settlements; arrows step through them all, a crown marks the capital, and clicking jumps straight to it on the world map. [*][b]At-a-glance actions[/b] — caravan, trade, and comms icons under the map: distance from your colony, what the settlement's trader will buy and when it restocks, and who answers the comms console. [*][b]Flavor ticker[/b] — a rotating status line: relics of theirs you hold, war parties on the move, active quests, fresh events, and royal titles your colonists carry. [*][b]Collapsible sections[/b] — fold away anything you don't need. [/list] [h1]✦ Trend Graphs[/h1] Up to eight historical graphs per faction, sampled four times a day from the moment the mod is installed: [b]Wealth · Inflation · Relations · Settlements · Population · Territory · Military · Stability[/b]. Hover any curve for the exact value and calendar date. With Economics & Demography installed, Wealth, Inflation, and Population are the [i]real[/i] simulated figures — not estimates. [h1]✦ And there's more[/h1] [list] [*][b]Diplomacy[/b] — see how each faction relates to every [i]other[/i] faction, and click through to jump between them. [*][b]Power Rankings[/b] — a live leaderboard of every faction (and your own colony) by strength, territory, population, stability, or settlements. [*][b]Our Colony[/b] — your own faction gets the full treatment too, pinned to the top of the list. [*][b]Every number, explained[/b] — hover relations, natural goodwill, or stability for a full breakdown of what's driving it. [/list] [h1]✦ Integrations[/h1] Everything below is [b]optional[/b] and detected automatically — the menu works fine with none of them installed: [list] [*][b]Cybranian – Rim Languages[/b] — each faction's dialect, your colony's fluency, and who else speaks it. [*][b]Faction Territories and Vassalage[/b] — territory painted onto the map preview, claimed-tile counts, vassal outposts, and vassalage points. [*][b]Air Territories[/b] — airspace transit permits, passes remaining, and overflight risk. [*][b]World Domination Experimental[/b] — settlement tiers and strengths, share of world power, industry breakdown, and live troop movement in the ticker. Counts match WD's own stats exactly. [*][b]Economics & Demography[/b] — real population pyramids (adults/children/elders), faction wealth and silver, economic archetypes, and true world inflation on the graphs. [*][b]Itemization Overhaul – Core[/b] — holding another faction's sacred relic shows a warning ticker on their page (they [i]will[/i] want it back). [*][b]Leadership Expanded – Faction Stability[/b] — a live stability bar and band on every faction, a Stability trend graph, and an "unrest" ticker when one is collapsing. [*][b]Vanilla Factions Expanded – Classical[/b] — a Senate panel listing the senators you've won over and the perk each grants; your unlocked perks show on the Our Colony page. [*][b]Vanilla Factions Expanded – Tribals[/b] — your tribe's era and chosen cornerstones on the Our Colony page. [*][b]Vanilla Outposts Expanded[/b] (and other Outpost-framework mods) — your outposts appear as browsable locations on the map. [*][b]Empire Refactored[/b] (and its add-ons) — your empire and your colony become one: the Our Colony entry takes your empire's name, your home colony is crowned as the capital, and a full Empire dashboard appears — settlements, workforce, prosperity, net income, garrison strength, next tax collection, policies & edicts, and active events.
