name: Modern History Menu
author: Astryl
description: [h1]⌛ Modern History Menu ⌛[/h1] The vanilla History tab is three grey pages you open twice a year. This replaces it with a single-screen colony dashboard — stat cards, modern graphs, a searchable event feed, colonist leaderboards, and per-pawn history cards, all visible at once. Built to match the dark, modern look of the Nice Tab suite, with no dependencies. [h1]✦ Features[/h1] [list] [*][b]Stat cards[/b] — colony wealth, population (with peak), days passed, enemy raids, colonists killed, and playtime at a glance. [*][b]Modern colony graphs[/b] — wealth, population, mood, and a brand-new [b]power graph[/b] (generation, usage, and battery storage, sampled hourly), all redrawn flat and clean: subtle grid, compact axis labels, event marks, legend chips. Hover any curve for its value and the in-game date. [*][b]Icon controls[/b] — switch graphs with icon buttons, zoom with pie-fill range buttons (30 / 100 / 300 days, or everything). [*][b]Slaves on the population graph[/b] — with Ideology active, your slave count is tracked alongside colonists and prisoners. [*][b]Event feed[/b] — every letter in a searchable, pinnable list. Click to reopen, right-click to jump to where it happened. [*][b]Wealth breakdown[/b] — a third pane lists everything on the map by wealth impact, grouped (“Human ×25”) and expandable down to every individual item, building, and pawn. Searchable, sorted by value, click anything to jump to it. [*][b]One-click vanilla toggle[/b] — a small button in the top-right swaps back to the stock History window any time, and back again. [/list] [h1]✦ Leaderboards[/h1] Rank your colonists in a proper bar chart — gold, silver, and bronze podium columns with portraits underneath, click any column to jump to the pawn. Around [b]40 searchable categories[/b] with hand-drawn icons: kills, damage, construction, cooking, mining, research, surgeries, time drafted, every skill, and more. The crown jewel is [b]Biggest gainers[/b] — who gained the most skill levels in the last 30 days, computed from this mod's own daily history. No other mod can show it. [h1]✦ Pinned Colonist Cards[/h1] Pin your favourite colonists to the dashboard (saved with your game). Every card gets a rendered portrait, lifetime records, and [b]six switchable history graphs[/b]: [list] [*][b]Skills[/b] — all twelve skills as coloured curves over your colony's lifetime. [*][b]Mood, Health, Rest, Food, Recreation[/b] — daily tracked percentages, each its own colour-coded curve. [/list] History is sampled once per in-game day and stored in your save — the longer you play, the richer the story. [h1]✦ Quality of Life[/h1] [list] [*]Type-to-search stat picker — find any leaderboard category in two keystrokes. [*]All text heights measured at runtime — plays nice with font-replacement mods and the tiny-text accessibility option. [*]Everything cached per tick and curves downsampled — negligible performance cost, even on huge colonies. [*]Click anything that looks like a pawn to jump the camera to them. [/list] [h1]✦ Optional Integrations[/h1] [list] [*][b]Isekai RPG Leveling[/b] — pawn cards gain a seventh graph: [b]RPG level over time[/b], tracked daily like everything else. The leaderboards gain seven new boards: [b]Isekai level[/b] plus all six attributes — Strength, Dexterity, Vitality, Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma. [/list] Detected at runtime — no patches, no hard dependency, nothing breaks without it. [h1]✦ Compatibility[/h1] [list] [*][b]No dependencies, no Harmony[/b] — styled after (but not requiring) the Nice Tab suite by Andromeda. [*]Safe to add mid-save; history starts recording from install. [*]Replaces the History tab's window via XML patch — conflicts only with mods that replace that same window. Mods that add new recorder graphs show up automatically. [*]Works without any DLC. Ideology adds the slave curve; Biotech adds xenotypes to the card headers. [/list] [hr][/hr] [i]Built for RimWorld 1.6. Your colony's whole story, on one screen.[/i]

name: Modern Ideology Menu
author: Astryl
description: [h1]⚑ Modern Ideology Menu[/h1] A complete, modern replacement for the ideology screens — a dark master-detail browser in the [b]Modern[/b] suite style. Searchable ideoligion list on the left, a rich detail page on the right: story, memes and precepts as icon grids, role cards with holder portraits, a follower gallery with live certainty bars, and a full leadership dashboard. Modded memes and precepts are supported automatically. Every route opens it: the Ideoligion button on the menu bar, Bio-tab ideology plates, Social-tab links, ritual outcomes, the Needs tab, faction UI, pawn tables. A toggle inside switches back to the vanilla view at any time — and your choice is remembered. [h1]✦ The Ideoligion Browser[/h1] [list] [*][b]Ideoligion cards[/b] — color-striped cards with icon, adjective, believer count, and primary/fluid tags. [*][b]Search[/b] — find any ideoligion by name. [*][b]One scroll surface[/b] — collapsible sections, no nested scrollbars, no squinting. [*][b]Non-modal[/b] — doesn't pause, doesn't lock the camera, drag it anywhere. [/list] [h1]✦ The Ideoligion Page[/h1] [list] [*][b]Hero[/b] — icon, name, titles, culture — and when opened from a pawn, their certainty bar sits right in the header. [*][b]Overview[/b] — full story text, believer counts, member name, leader title, and fluid development progress with reform availability. [*][b]Memes[/b] — icon tiles tinted in the ideoligion's color, with full descriptions on hover. [*][b]Roles[/b] — every role with its holders' portraits; click to jump to the pawn. [*][b]Followers[/b] — a portrait gallery of every believer with live certainty bars; the dead remembered, dimmed at the end. Click any portrait to jump the camera. [/list] [h1]✦ Precepts at a Glance[/h1] Every precept is a tile with its moral status told twice — a corner badge and a color-coded status word: [b]Exalted[/b] gold, [b]Approved[/b] green, [b]Disapproved[/b] orange, [b]Horrible[/b] red, [b]Abhorrent[/b] dark red. Relics, altars, and apparel render their [i]actual item[/i] with your ideoligion's style. Grouped by kind: precepts, roles, rituals, sacred buildings, relics, weapons, venerated animals, xenotypes, apparel. [h1]✦ Leadership[/h1] With [b]Ideology Leadership Expanded[/b] installed, the Leadership section becomes a political dashboard: governance classification (Elective · Autocratic · Triumvirate · Royal · Theocratic), the sitting leader with reign duration, designated heirs, election countdowns, and a reign history with official portraits and color-coded end reasons — died, deposed, abdicated, replaced. Without it you still get the leader role and its holder. [h1]✦ Dev Mode Editing[/h1] With dev mode on, an edit toggle turns the window into a live ideoligion editor — no vanilla dialogs, no leaving the window: [list] [*]Rename inline, straight in the header. [*]Add memes and precepts from "+" tiles in every category — rituals, roles, relics, buildings, all of it. [*]Click any precept tile to edit, replace, regenerate, or remove it. [*]Remove memes with a click — compatible precepts are kept, not rerolled. [/list] [h1]✦ Integrations[/h1] Everything below is [b]optional[/b] and detected automatically — the window works fine with none of them installed: [list] [*][b]Ideology Leadership Expanded[/b] — the full leadership dashboard: governance types, elections, heirs, reign history with official portraits. [*][b]Itemization Overhaul – Core[/b] — relic tiles show the bound item's affix card on hover: relic tier, "Desired by" faction, corruption/cleansed state, and the full affix list with ★/✦ potency marks. [/list] [h1]✦ Compatibility[/h1] [list] [*]Adds no defs and changes no game balance — pure UI. [*]Safe to add or remove mid-save; nothing is written into the save file. [*]Modded memes, precepts, and ideology content appear automatically. [*]The vanilla Ideos tab is untouched and reachable any time — your view choice is remembered. [*]All integrations are soft (reflection-based) — load order doesn't matter. [*]Requires [b]Harmony[/b] and the [b]Ideology[/b] DLC. [/list] [h1]✦ The Modern X Suite[/h1] Designed to sit alongside Modern Bio Tab, Modern Social Tab, Modern Xenotype Tab, Modern Faction Menu, Modern History Menu, Modern Quest Tab, and the rest of the suite — same palette, same chrome, same philosophy: the information you want, none of the squinting. If you encounter any bugs, compatibility issues, or unintended behavior, please report them in the comments or a dedicated discussion thread. name: Modern Needs Tab
author: Astryl
description: [h1]◆ Modern Needs Tab ◆[/h1] The vanilla needs tab tells you where a need is — never where it's been, how fast it's moving, or what just shifted it. This replaces it with a two-pane dashboard: compact, reorderable need cards on the left, and a live detail panel on the right. The default view is your pawn's [b]overall mood[/b] with a 15-day history graph; click any card to drill into that need, click again to return. [h1]✦ Need Cards[/h1] [img]https://i.imgur.com/sNLhpkg.png[/img] [list] [*][b]A card for every need[/b] — vanilla, DLC, and modded needs all get a card automatically. VAE's Fulfilment, and anything else that shows up on the vanilla list is tracked without configuration. [*][b]Drag to reorder[/b] — press and drag any card to rearrange the column. Order is saved globally and persists across sessions; a reset button is in settings. [*][b]Each card shows[/b]: accent color by need type, current percentage, trend arrows (▲/▼), a styled bar with threshold ticks (Mood uses live mental-break thresholds), an instant-level marker, and a measured [b]%/hour rate[/b]. [*][b]Toggle to inspect[/b] — click a card to open its full detail panel. Click the same card again to return to the mood overview. [/list] [h1]✦ The Detail Panel[/h1] [img]https://i.imgur.com/kUtalzb.png[/img] [list] [*][b]Hero[/b] — need name, large percentage, vanilla description. [*][b]15-day history graph[/b] — sampled hourly for every colonist, prisoner, and slave on maps and in caravans, stored in your save. Zoom 24 h / 5 days / 15 days. Hover the graph for exact values and in-game dates. Overlay all needs in the background for comparison. [*][b]Recovery stats[/b] — current rate (%/hour), 24-hour net change, and estimated time to full or empty at the current trend. [*][b]RELATED THOUGHTS[/b] — the active mood thoughts this specific need causes. Hungry and Ate lavish meal appear on the Food panel; Slept outside appears on Rest; joy thoughts appear on Recreation. [*][b]RECENT ACTIVITY[/b] — every recorded need event, filtered to this need only: "1.3h ago · Eating fine meal · +38%". Smart job attribution means credit lands on the job that actually moved the need, not whatever the pawn started next. [/list] [h1]✦ Mood — Always In View[/h1] [img]https://i.imgur.com/6QbFANv.png[/img] A persistent mood box sits at the bottom of the right panel at all times, independent of which card is selected. It shows the overall mood percentage colored by mental-break zone and every active buff and debuff with its offset. [b]Hover any need card[/b] and the thoughts that need is responsible for [b]light up in that need's color[/b] with a color stripe — Food card hover tints Hungry and Ate fine meal in orange; Recreation card hover tints Bored in purple. Every other row stays at full brightness. Hovering the Mood card lights up the entire list. [h1]✦ Integrations[/h1] [img]https://i.imgur.com/K7afLtO.png[/img] [list] [*][b]Vanilla Aspirations Expanded[/b] — the Fulfilment need card shows each aspiration icon [b]centered under its segment[/b] of the progress bar. Fulfilled aspirations glow green with a stripe; pending ones stay dim. VAE's own "Satisfied when…" and completion-date tooltips are used as-is. [*][b]Comforts[/b] — a synthetic [b]Wants card[/b] appears with all six preference-category icons centered under a segmented satisfaction bar. The detail panel lists per-item icons, PREFERENCES rows with "Fulfilled by…" tooltips, and scrolls cleanly through any length of content. [*][b]RimHUD[/b] — fully compatible. The tab sizes itself to RimHUD's raised inspect pane so it never clips off-screen, and RimHUD's mood bar click opens this tab. [*][b]Open API[/b] — other mods can add rows, icons, and descriptions to any need card via reflection (no hard dependency). [/list] [h1]✦ Quality of Life[/h1] [list] [*][b]Flat, auto-hiding scrollbars[/b] — slim 4px thumbs that appear only on overflow, matching the dashboard aesthetic. [*][b]One-click toggle[/b] — same icon both directions: Modern → vanilla (header button) and vanilla → Modern (glowing button on the vanilla tab). Choice remembered across sessions. [*][b]Window-scale slider (60–100%)[/b] in settings — shrinks the whole tab uniformly, UI-scale safe. [*][b]Auto-fit sizing[/b] — clamps against the live inspect-pane height (RimHUD-safe) at any resolution. [*][b]Performance[/b] — history data cached once per second; graph and rate data refreshed on a slow cadence. Negligible cost on large colonies. [/list] [h1]✦ More Controls[/h1] [list] [*][b]Per-colonist layouts[/b] — opt a single pawn out of the shared layout (a toggle in the detail header) to give them their own card order and pins, saved with the game. [*][b]Importance staircase[/b] — Food, Rest and Hygiene are sized larger so the survival needs read at a glance; everything else is a uniform compact card. Toggle it off for a flat list. [*][b]Vanilla theme[/b] — a settings toggle reskins the whole tab in vanilla's lighter panel colors for a more stock feel. [*][b]Gene resources[/b] — with Biotech, hemogen (and modded gene resources) appear as bar cards right in the need list. [*][b]Moodlet timers[/b] — hover any buff or debuff to see how long until it wears off. [*][b]Per-need preference icons[/b] — Comforts and aspiration icons sit right under each card's bar. [*][b]Grouped settings[/b] — Display / Behavior / Integration sections, each option with its own tooltip. [/list] [h1]✦ Compatibility[/h1] [list] [*]Requires [b]Harmony[/b]. Compatible with all DLCs (none required). [*]Modded needs work generically — any need visible on the vanilla list gets a card, color, history, rates, and activity feed. [*]Safe to add mid-save; history starts recording from the moment the mod is installed. Removing it only discards the recorded history. [/list] [hr][/hr] [i]Built for RimWorld 1.6. Every need, graphed — and the story of what moved it.[/i] [hr][/hr] [h2]🛠️ Mod Disclaimer & Quality Assurance[/h2] [quote][b]A Note on Development:[/b] Parts of the code for this mod were generated using [b]Claude AI[/b]. If you encounter any bugs, compatibility issues, or unintended behavior, please report them in the comments or a dedicated discussion thread. name: Modern Notifications
author: astryl
description: [h1]◆ Modern Notifications ◆[/h1] RimWorld scatters everything that wants your attention across three different corners in three different styles. The pop-up messages float as plain text at the top-left, the alerts stack on the right, the clock and controls cluster at the bottom-right, and the letters pile up beside them. Modern Notifications pulls all of it into one clean, dark, icon-driven card system, so a single glance tells you what is happening, how bad it is, and where. A built-in calendar even tracks the days your colony cares about, from birthdays to deadlines. Fully standalone, with Harmony as the only requirement, and safe to add or remove at any time. [h1]✦ One Place For Everything[/h1] [img]REPLACE_HUB[/img] [list] [*][b]Docked notifications[/b]: the top-left text pop-ups become tidy cards that stack in the bottom-right, right above your alerts and letters, so everything lives in one column. Prefer them at the top-left? A single toggle floats them back into a draggable strip you can place anywhere. [*][b]Type-coloured cards[/b]: every message carries a coloured left edge, red for threats, amber for setbacks, teal for tasks, green for good news, so you read the tone before you read the text. [*][b]Faithful behaviour[/b]: click to jump, right-click to dismiss, hover to highlight on the map, all exactly as the base game does it. [/list] [h1]✦ Alerts With a Live Timer[/h1] [list] [*][b]Cards that fit[/b]: alerts size themselves to the full label, so no more clipped, wrapped warnings. [*][b]A draining urgency bar[/b]: the left edge of each alert starts full and bright, then shrinks and fades the longer you leave it unaddressed. A fresh problem looks nothing like one you have been ignoring for a season. [*][b]Right-click to snooze[/b]: silence an alert for a while. It returns on its own, or sooner if its situation changes. [*][b]Critical means critical[/b]: the worst alerts gain a red background and a warning badge so they cannot be missed. [*][b]Hover to read it all[/b]: mouse over any alert for a tooltip with its full label and a short explanation, so a clipped warning never hides what it means. [*][b]Shift-click to hide[/b]: hide an alert you never want to see again. It stops appearing, even while its cause is still active, and you can bring it back at any time from a restore list in the settings. [/list] [h1]✦ A Rebuilt Bottom-Right[/h1] [list] [*][b]Styled speed controls[/b]: five crisp icon buttons for pause through ultrafast, with ultrafast unlocked from the start and no developer mode required. The active speed glows, and every keyboard shortcut still works. [*][b]A widget drawer[/b]: the vanilla display toggles tuck into a clean drop-down grid, so the corner stays calm until you want them. Widgets added by other mods are tidied into the same grid, sized, spaced and tinted to match, and active toggles stay bright while inactive ones dim, so the whole drawer reads at a glance. [*][b]One information panel[/b]: weather with the current wind strength, temperature, the date and the season share one tidy column, each row with its own icon. Temperature is colour-graded from freezing blue to scorching red at a glance, and you choose whether it reads in Celsius, Fahrenheit, Kelvin, both at once, or your game's own unit. [*][b]An optional performance meter[/b]: a tidy FPS and TPS readout sits at the top of the panel in clean white, each with a small trend arrow that turns green as it climbs and red as it dips. TPS shows the ticks per second your game actually achieves against the current speed's cap, the same number profiling tools report, so late-game slowdown is visible the moment it starts. Off by default, one toggle away. [*][b]A colony vitals row[/b]: an optional line of four quick readouts, colony health, average mood, days of food and current threat, each colour-graded from green to red, with the full breakdown on hover. Off by default. [*][b]Clean condition rows[/b]: a timed event such as a toxic fallout or an eclipse sits on its own row with its icon, and the time left stays out of the way until you hover, for a calmer readout. Prefer the countdown always in view? One setting puts it back on the row. [/list] [h1]✦ Weather and Effects, Read at a Glance[/h1] [list] [*][b]Live weather icons[/b]: clear skies, rain, thunder, snow, fog, wind, sandstorm and more, each drawn to match. [*][b]Wind at a glance[/b]: the weather row shows the current wind strength in plain words, from calm to strong gale, following the wind the game actually simulates, so you know how your turbines are doing before you look at them. With Combat Extended loaded, the row also shows the wind's compass heading in CE's own wind names, with the full story on hover. [*][b]Temperature on its own row[/b]: the colour-graded outdoor temperature sits on a dedicated row under the weather, together with the temperature of the room under your cursor. [*][b]Effects in the weather area[/b]: a toxic fallout, a solar flare, an eclipse or a cold snap shows up right beside the weather with its own icon, not as a stray floating box. [*][b]Danger you can see[/b]: hazardous conditions glow red or amber and wear a warning badge, so you know the difference between a pretty aurora and a deadly pall. [*][b]A heat overlay on demand[/b]: right-click the temperature row to wash the map in a temperature gradient, from cold blue to hot orange in the same colours as the readout, with every enclosed room labelled by its own temperature. Right-click again to clear it. It works on its own, and drives Heat Map (Continued)'s richer overlay when that mod is installed. [/list] [h1]✦ Letters That Show What Happened[/h1] [list] [*][b]Event icons[/b]: a letter from a raid shows crossed swords, a manhunter pack shows a fang, disease shows a virus, a trader shows coins, a crash shows a drop pod, a quest shows a scroll. You know what it is before you open it. [*][b]Plain letters keep an envelope[/b]: story and manual letters with no incident behind them stay clean and simple. [*][b]Urgent events glow[/b]: a raid or other pause-worthy letter pulses with a soft glow in its own colour, so the thing that needs you most stands out at a glance. [*][b]Hover to preview[/b]: mouse over a letter to read its full text without opening it. [/list] [h1]✦ A Living Calendar[/h1] Modern Notifications quietly tracks the days that matter to your colony, then surfaces them right where you are already looking. [list] [*][b]A date that knows what is coming[/b]: the date in the bottom-right lights up as notable days approach, with a small icon for the next thing on the horizon and a soft glow on the day itself. [*][b]Click for the full calendar[/b]: a clean, dark, one quadrum view in the Modern style. Step backward and forward through the seasons and years, hover any day to read its events, and click an event to jump straight to it. [*][b]Grid or agenda[/b]: read the season as a calendar grid, or flip to an agenda list that lines up everything coming next in order, grouped by day. [*][b]It knows your colony[/b]: colonist and bonded animal birthdays, the start of each quadrum and the turn of the year, quest deadlines, caravan arrivals, incoming shuttles, child growth moments, pregnancy due dates, research completion estimates, royal titles and ideology rituals all land on the right day on their own. [*][b]It remembers[/b]: deaths, raids, marriages, births, completed research, solar events and major incidents are recorded as they happen, with the telling details captured in the moment. Hover a past event to read them (a raid's faction and size, a colonist's age and cause of death, a project's research cost) and click it to open your history. [*][b]Your own reminders[/b]: right-click any day to leave yourself a note. Give it a title, a colour-coded severity and an icon, set it to repeat every quadrum or every year, and right-click it again any time to edit or delete it. It arrives as a matching letter when the day comes. [*][b]Filter everything[/b]: a row of category icons chooses exactly what shows, on both the calendar and the date line, and your choices stick. [*][b]A week at a glance[/b]: an optional seven-day strip sits above the date with a dot for each upcoming event, and a click jumps the calendar straight to that day. [/list] [h1]✦ Plays Nicely With Your Mods[/h1] There are no hard dependencies here beyond Harmony. The icon matching was tuned against a deep scan of large content mods, so their weather, conditions and event letters are recognized automatically and given a fitting icon and the right danger colour. Anything unfamiliar still falls back to a clean neutral icon or the plain envelope, never blank. [list] [*][b]Alpha Biomes[/b]: acid rain and moldy air show the toxic mark, volcanic ash falls as ashfall, forsaken nights show a moon, petal storms a bloom, and ambient radiation a radiation symbol. [*][b]The Ashlands[/b]: ashfall and ash storms use the ashfall icon, sulphuric rain the toxic mark, volcanic wind and eruptions the volcano, and the wandering beasts a paw. [*][b]Vanilla Events Expanded[/b]: dust storms become sandstorms, hail and ice ages snow, fertile rains and crop sprouts a bloom, geomagnetic storms the interference mark, tidal flooding rain, meteorite showers a comet, and earthquakes the seismograph. [*][b]Vanilla Psycasts Expanded[/b]: eternal nights, umbral veils and void storms show a moon, psychic flashstorms a bolt, time quakes the seismograph, and solar rifts the solar flare. [*][b]ReGrowth[/b]: blizzards and foggy snow read as snow, drizzle and monsoons as rain, sandstorms and foggy sandstorms as sandstorms, and windy weather as wind. [*][b]Nature's Pretty Sweet[/b]: dust storms become sandstorms, lava smoke the volcano, thick fog the fog mark, superblooms a bloom, and its diseases the virus. [*][b]Nuclear war mods[/b]: nuclear heat and winter show the radiation symbol, while missile and satellite strikes show the crossed swords. [*][b]Spaceports[/b]: kessler syndrome shows a comet, shuttle arrivals and mystery cargo the trade and visitor icons, and derelicts a drop pod. [*][b]Custom races such as Kiiro and Milira[/b]: their join and refugee events show the newcomer icon, festivals and trades the coins, raids the swords, and fallen angels a visitor. [*][b]Medieval creatures and DankPyon events[/b]: roaming beasts and golems show a paw or drop pod, eclipses the eclipse, and mineshaft infestations the insect. [*][b]Vanilla Factions and Mechanoids Expanded[/b]: pillage and outpost raids show the swords, and junk chunk drops a drop pod. [*][b]Days Matter[/b]: its custom anniversaries and holidays appear on the calendar and the date line on their own, with no setup. [*][b]Declutter UI[/b]: detected on its own. Modern Notifications steps aside for its widget menu, and when you switch off the vanilla weather, conditions or date readouts in Declutter, this panel hides its matching rows to suit, so you declutter once in one place. Prefer this panel's own widget drawer? A one-click override keeps it while still deferring to Declutter for the rest. [*][b]Ideology Leadership Expanded[/b]: upcoming elections, conclaves, leadership challenges and triumvirate appointments land on the calendar, each with its own icon, royal coronations are marked with a crown, and past elections show their winner and vote tallies on hover. [*][b]Modern History Menu[/b]: clicking any recorded event on the calendar opens straight into your history. [*][b]Modded panel widgets[/b]: play-settings toggles added by other mods, such as Dubs Mint Minimap, Better Pawn Control and TailorMade, appear in the panel's widget drawer alongside the vanilla ones, normalized to the same cell size and grid spacing and tinted to match the panel, with switched-on toggles kept bright so their state reads at a glance. [*][b]Food Alert (Continued)[/b]: when it is loaded, the vitals row's days of food defers to its smarter counter, which respects its food preference setting and your colonists' real appetites, so the two readouts always agree. [*][b]Combat Extended[/b]: CE's wind information lives on the weather row. Its wind direction appears as a compact compass heading beside the strength, in CE's own translated wind names, and the row's hover pane carries the full heading and CE's wind explanation. [*][b]Vanilla Temperature Expanded[/b]: its proximity heat mechanic shows up right in the panel. Point at an outdoor tile warmed or chilled by a nearby campfire, heater or cooling unit and the temperature row shows the local temperature, colour-graded and marked heated or cooled, with the full story on hover. The standalone Proxy Heat mod is covered too. [*][b]Heat Map (Continued)[/b]: the temperature row's right-click overlay hands the display to Heat Map when it is installed, so you get its enhanced gradient and its own room readouts, all toggled from the same place. [/list] Every match is automatic and keyword based, so newer and smaller content mods are usually picked up too. None of these are required. [h1]✦ Make It Yours[/h1] [list] [*]Turn any surface on or off on its own: the styled messages, the alerts, the letters and each row of the bottom-right panel. [*]Dock messages to the bottom-right, or float them top-left and drag them anywhere. [*]Scale the notification cards and the whole bottom-right panel, with text scaling to match. [*][b]Resize and hide each panel area on its own[/b]: the widget drawer, speed buttons, FPS and TPS meter, vitals, weather, conditions, week strip, date and season each get their own show toggle and size slider, all sharing one tidy column width, so you can enlarge the speed buttons, shrink the date, or hide a row entirely. [*][b]Pick your font[/b]: choose any font installed on your system, with optional bold or italic, applied across the messages, alerts, letters and the bottom-right panel. Leave it on the game default for the original look. [*]Show the real time of day in the corner, in your system's clock format or as a 24 hour clock. [*]Set panel opacity over the map. author: astryl
description: [h1]Modern Psycasts UI[/h1] [i]A clean, single-page reskin of the Vanilla Psycasts Expanded psycast tab. Part of the Modern UI family.[/i] [h1]What it does[/h1] Modern Psycasts UI replaces VPE's tabbed psycast screen with one polished, scrollable page that shows every psycast tree at once, vanilla and modded alike. Categories are stripped away, so nothing is buried behind sub-tabs. You just scroll, search, and spend. [h1]Features[/h1] [list] [*][b]All trees, one page.[/b] Every psycast path from VPE and any add-on is merged into a single, sortable grid. [*][b]Real path art.[/b] Each tree shows its proper background through a loader that fixes VPE's card art failing to load on RimWorld 1.6, and it respects retexture mods. [*][b]Search and filter.[/b] Find a tree by name or ability, and cycle a three-state filter: all trees, unlockable and invested, or invested only. [*][b]Prerequisite glow.[/b] Hover an ability to light up its prerequisite chain across the whole grid. [*][b]Clear requirements.[/b] Locked trees show a tidy breakdown of meme, gene, mechanitor, focus, and background, each marked with a check or cross for the selected pawn. [*][b]Built-in psyset editor.[/b] Customize psysets right inside the tab. The panel swaps to a psyset list, then to an editor where you click a psycast to add it to a set and click it again to remove it. No fiddly dragging. [*][b]Modern chrome.[/b] Flat scrollbars, stylized black card borders, azure accents, a gold card-selection glow, and a trees panel you can resize from its corner. The width is remembered between sessions. [*][b]Matching options page.[/b] The mod settings use the same flat, dark styling, with a tree-size slider and toggles for sort order and background style. [*][b]Old-style toggle.[/b] Switch between VPE's main and alternative card backgrounds, from the tab or the options. [*][b]Everything still works.[/b] Unlock paths, learn abilities, spend points, manage psysets and meditation foci, all intact. [/list] [h1]Compatibility[/h1] [list] [*][b]Requires Vanilla Psycasts Expanded[/b], plus Harmony and Vanilla Expanded Framework. [*]Add-on psycast mods that build on VPE appear automatically in the unified grid, with their own artwork. [*]Retexture mods that replace VPE's card art are respected, with the last loaded winning. [*]RimHUD-aware, so the tab stays on screen even with a taller inspect pane. [*]Safe to add or remove at any time, since it only changes how the psycast tab is drawn. [/list] [h1]A note on the screenshots[/h1] [i]The in-game UI is [b]not[/b] as dark as some screenshots may suggest. The dark theme shown comes from [b]PrettyUI[/b], a separate UI-overhaul mod, not from Modern Psycasts UI. Without PrettyUI, the panels follow RimWorld's standard UI tone.[/i] [h1]Part of the Modern UI family[/h1] Modern Bio Tab, Modern Health Tab, Modern Needs Tab, Modern Social Tab, Modern Xenotype Tab, Modern Faction Menu, Modern Quest Menu, Modern Learning Menu, and more. name: Modern Social Tab
author: Astryl
description: [h1]◆ Modern Social Tab ◆[/h1] The vanilla Social tab is a wall of grey text. Modern Social Tab replaces it with a clean two-pane dashboard: relationship cards on the left, a live social-standing graph on the right, all in the same dark, flat style as the Modern Needs and Modern Bio tabs. You can read every relationship at a glance, and the graph shows you whether things are getting better or worse. [h1]✦ Relationship cards[/h1] [list] [*][b]A card for everyone they know.[/b] Each one shows a portrait, the relationship, both opinion bars (how the two feel about each other), and a romance-chance bar with the full breakdown on hover. [*][b]Every relationship is labelled.[/b] Family, lovers, fiancés and spouses show their proper title, including ones added by other mods. Everyone else gets the tier the base game uses: Acquaintance, Friend or Rival, plus any extra tiers a relationship mod adds. When a pawn fills more than one role with someone, say a cousin who is also a fiancé, the card cycles through each title in turn and shows a small chevron beside the label so you know there is more. [*][b]Click to graph, double-click to follow.[/b] A single click swaps the right-hand graph to that one relationship over time. A double click jumps the camera to the pawn and re-centres the tab on them. [*][b]Pin the ones that matter.[/b] Pin any pawn with the thumbtack and they stay at the top of the list. [*][b]Action icons on every card.[/b] Quick controls sit in the top-right corner: the pregnancy-approach toggle for couples (Biotech), plus break-up and proposal buttons when Romance on the Rim is installed. Other mods can add their own buttons here too, lined up with the rest. [*][b]Try romance.[/b] A heart button under the list opens the game's romance picker (Biotech). It dims while a colonist is on cooldown. [*][b]Status at a glance.[/b] Off-map colonists show a caravan wagon or an away signpost on their portrait. Hover any portrait for faction, location and situation, such as Slave, Faction leader, Kidnapped, Lent or guest. [/list] [h1]✦ Social-standing graph[/h1] [list] [*][b]Always something to see.[/b] The graph opens on the pawn's social standing, which is how the colony feels about them on average. No clicking needed. [*][b]A fortnight of history.[/b] Standing is sampled every in-game hour and saved with your game, so the line fills in as time passes. The current value anchors it right away, so it is never blank. [*][b]Easy to read.[/b] The axis runs from -100 to +100 with the zero line picked out, green above and red below. Hover for the exact value and date. [*][b]Per-relationship view.[/b] Select a card and the graph switches to that single relationship over time, with the full opinion breakdown on hover. [/list] [h1]✦ Social stats[/h1] [list] [*][b]A compact stat strip.[/b] The bottom-left corner shows a small panel of social stats for the selected pawn. [*][b]Pick what you see.[/b] Click Choose to set which stats appear, from anything in the social category. It starts with Social Impact, Negotiation Ability and Trade Price Improvement. [*][b]Proper tooltips.[/b] Hover a stat for what it does and exactly how the value was worked out. Modded social stats show up in the picker on their own. [/list] [h1]✦ Plays nicely with your mods[/h1] Wherever it can, the tab calls the game's own social-card code, so other mods' additions simply appear. It is all optional, and nothing breaks when a mod is missing. [list] [*][b]Ideology.[/b] A strip across the top shows the ideoligion and certainty, and lets you assign or change the pawn's role right there using the normal role-change ritual. Hidden without the DLC. [*][b]Romance on the Rim.[/b] Couples get break-up and proposal buttons, with the acceptance chance shown in the proposal tooltip. [*][b]Vanilla Expanded Framework.[/b] Modded pregnancy approaches, such as psychic conception and lovin' for pleasure, appear in the pregnancy menu. [*][b]Intimacy, Friends n' Lovers.[/b] The pregnancy-approach control also shows up for mutually attracted non-couples, just as Intimacy intends. [*][b]Hospitality.[/b] Visiting guests read as Guest in the portrait status. [*][b]Animals Logic.[/b] With its animal-relations option turned on, unnamed animals show their relationships too. [*][b]RimPsyche.[/b] Romance bars gain an attraction reading and orientation details. [*][b]RimJobWorld.[/b] Sex Drive becomes one of the options in the stat picker. [*][b]RimHUD.[/b] The tab measures itself against the taller inspect pane so nothing clips. [/list] [h1]✦ Quality of life[/h1] [list] [*][b]Switch back any time.[/b] A small icon in the top corner returns you to the stock Social tab, and it remembers your choice. [*][b]Resizable and tidy.[/b] Drag the divider between the relationship list and the stat strip to size them, and the split is saved. Scrollbars are thin and only appear when needed. [*][b]Sort and filter.[/b] Order the list by opinion, relationship or name, and filter to family, lovers or rivals. [*][b]Safe at any scale, and mid-save.[/b] The layout reflows cleanly at any UI scale, and you can add the mod to an existing colony whenever you like. Removing it only loses the recorded history. [/list] [h1]✦ Requirements[/h1] Just Harmony (brrainz.harmony). That is the only dependency. [hr][/hr] [i]Built for RimWorld 1.6. name: Readable Numbers
author: 7h0m4s
description: [h2]What does the mod do?[/h2]Makes numbers in Rimworld easier to read by adding digit separators. [b]e.g. 1000000 -> 1,000,000[/b] [h2]Details[/h2][b]Separators and Decimals can be any character you want:[/b] [list] [*] [b](1,000,000.00)[/b] Comma separator with Period decimal [b] -Default-[/b] [*] [b](1.000.000,00)[/b] Period separator with Comma decimal [*] [b](1 000 000.00)[/b] Space separator with Period decimal [*] [b](1 000 000,00)[/b] Space separator with Comma decimal [*] [b](1'000'000.00)[/b] Apostrophe separator with Period decimal [*] [b](1'000'000,00)[/b] Apostrophe separator with Comma decimal [*] [b](1#000#000@00)[/b] [B]Custom:[/B] [u]Any[/u] combination of 2 characters [/list] [b]Choose Your Preferred Digit Grouping Style:[/b] [list] [*] [b](100,000,000,000)[/b] Three Digits [b]-Default-[/b] [*] [b](1,00,00,00,00,000)[/b] Three Then Two Digits [*] [b](1000,0000,0000)[/b] Four Digits [*] [b](100000000000)[/b] None [/list] Formatting will be applied to most modded UI elements. Can easily enabled/disabled number formatting mid-game from the Mod Settings. A blacklist feature is available in settings to exclude for any text that shouldn't be modified. You can customise how long a number must be before formatting is applied. [h2]F.A.Q.[/h2] [b]Q.[/b] [b]The mod is formatting a number I don't want it to! How can I fix this? [/b] [b]A.[/b] [*] For years (for example 2026 -> 2,026), go to mod settings and increase the minimum number of digits a number must have to get separator formatting. [*] For everything else such as pawn or item names (for example M1911 -> M,1911). There is a blacklist available in the mod settings. Add all or part of the text that is incorrectly being modified. The mod will avoid formatting any text in game that contains those specific characters. WARNING: An exceptionally long blacklist might cause performance impact. [b]Q.[/b] [b]Will this affect performance?[/b] [b]A.[/b] There should be no noticeable impact on performance. All processed text in game is cached for fast retrieval. Even without the cache, a lot of effort has been put in to optimising the formatting process to take as few CPU operations as possible and to quickly skip over any text that doesn't have enough sequential digits to need processing. [b]Q.[/b] [b]Was this vibe coded with AI?[/b] [b]A. [/b]No AI generated code was used in this project. Feel free to peruse the commits in the [url=https://github.com/7h0m4s/RimworldReadableNumbers]Github[/url] to confirm. I got a lot of practice in optimising a simple task to be as performant as possible. [h2]Compatibility[/h2]This mod is safe to be added and removed at any point. As it does not make any changes to the save file. There shouldn't be any clashes with the majority of mods so long as they don't make changes to how text is rendered on screen in game. [h2]Change Log[/h2][b]1.2.0:[/b] [list] [*] Improved support for all Mods. Will now be far less likely for text in modded screens to be displayed incorrectly. [*] Added mod setting to set the minimum number of digits a number must have before separators are added. Specifically to allow users to exclude years (e.g. 2,026) and weapon names (e.g. M1,911) from being formatted. [*] Minor performance improvements [/list][b]1.1.0:[/b] [list] [*] Tidied Mod Settings [*] Expanded Separator And Decimal choices to include Apostrophe separator [*] Added support for any characters to be used as Separator and Decimal [*] Added Digit Grouping options [*] Allowed mod to format the Decimal for numbers less than 1000 by default (e.g. 9.18kg -> 9,18kg) [*] Added setting option to disable small number formatting [*] Removed redundant Harmony.dll and PNG files [*] Bug Fix: Quest Rewards not displaying $ value [*] Bug Fix: Date year in History->Messages dialogue getting formatted [/list][b]1.0.0:[/b] [list] [*]Mod Release [/list] [h2]License[/h2] GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE V3 [h3][url=https://github.com/7h0m4s/RimworldReadableNumbers]Github[/url][/h3] [h3][url=https://ko-fi.com/7h0m4s65028]Ko-Fi[/url][/h3]

name: Rizryn's Family Tree Mod
author: Rizryn
description: Adds a Family Tree tab to RimWorld, allowing you to visualize the bloodlines and relationships of your colonists. Features: - Interactive Tree: A scrollable family tree that maps out living and dead colonists along with their extended blood relatives. - Zoom Controls: Zoom in, zoom out, and reset the view using on-screen buttons. - Pawn Search Bar: Find pawns using a search bar with autocomplete. Clicking a name centers the camera and isolates their bloodline. - Double-Click to Find: Double left-click a portrait to close the tree and jump to that pawn (or their corpse/grave) on the local or world map. - Bloodline Isolation: Right-click a pawn's portrait to dim unrelated pawns and highlight their direct bloodline. - Tree Reorganization: Ctrl + Right-click a pawn to reorganize the tree, showing only that pawn's extended bloodline. Use the "Back to Full Tree" button to return to the default view. - Genes Integration: Left-click a pawn to open a scrollable Genes panel. - Gene Inheritance Tracking: The Genes panel traces genes up the family tree to show which ancestor they originated from. Click the originator's name to jump to their portrait. - Hybrid Xenotype Tracking: Displays hybrid xenotypes by tracing and combining the xenotypes of a pawn's ancestors. - Death Tooltips and Portraits: Hover over the skull icon of a deceased pawn to see their cause and date of death. Dead pawns retain a portrait of how they looked at the time of death. - Line Coloring and Labels: Family branches are color-coded to help distinguish family units. Non-blood relationships (married, engaged, etc.) are dynamically labeled. - Name Display: Full names and relationship labels are displayed for every node. Optional Compatibility: - lydocia.AdoptiveRelationships (Lydocia's Adoptive Relationships): adoptive family members appear in the tree with gold branch lines and adoptive relationship labels. Adoptive family is not treated as blood for gene tracing or reincarnation. - vanillaexpanded.outposts (Vanilla Outposts Expanded): double-click find pawn jumps to the outpost on the world map when a colonist is stationed there. Compatibility: Safe to add or remove from existing save games.

name: Sleek Research Tab
author: squishyjellyfish
description: [h1]Sleek Research Tab[/h1] [b]Sleek Research Tab[/b] is a clean, lightweight overhaul of RimWorld's research screen, made for heavily modded games where the vanilla tab turns into a huge wall of nodes and endless sub-tabs. It is part of my [b]Sleek[/b] design family. Same idea as the other Sleek mods: make the UI cleaner, easier to read, and less annoying to use, while keeping the game's systems intact. [h1]The All View[/h1] [list] [*] [b]Everything on one screen[/b] - see every mod's research at once, laid out as a clean left-to-right tech tree: early tech on the left, later tech on the right, with connection lines drawn between linked projects. [*] [b]Tech-era bands[/b] - the tree is split into labelled era zones, from Neolithic through to Archotech, so you always know which age you are looking at. [*] [b]Tidy sorting[/b] - research is sorted by tech era and prerequisite depth, so the tree reads more naturally instead of becoming a tangle. [*] [b]Per-mod sections[/b] - prefer research grouped into tidy per-mod blocks like Core, Vanilla Expanded, Progression, and so on? That is a single toggle. [/list] [h1]Navigation & Search[/h1] [list] [*] [b]Smooth zoom and pan[/b] - scroll to zoom, drag to pan, and use the Fit button to frame the whole tree instantly. [*] [b]Readable at any zoom[/b] - node names stay legible even when zoomed right out. [*] [b]Minimap[/b] - the All view has a small corner overview of the whole tree. Click or drag it to move around quickly, and search hits light up on it so you can see where results are. [*] [b]Search and filters[/b] - find projects by name, source mod, or tech level, then jump between matches. [*] [b]Jump tools[/b] - jump straight to your current project, follow prerequisite chains, and use the back button to return to where you were. [/list] [h1]Reading the Tree[/h1] [list] [*] [b]Prerequisite highlighting[/b] - select a project to light up everything it needs. [*] [b]Hover highlight[/b] - hover a project to preview its direct prerequisites and everything it unlocks before you even click. [*] [b]Focus mode[/b] - fade everything outside the selected project's chain so the path stands out. This is optional. [*] [b]Available-now glow[/b] - see at a glance what your colony can start researching right now. [*] [b]Cleaner visuals[/b] - calmer colours, clearer nodes, and optional per-tech-level tinting. [*] [b]Completed research options[/b] - dim, hide, or show finished projects. [/list] [h1]Built for Big Modlists[/h1] Performance was one of the main goals, because big research trees get heavy fast. At overview zoom, Sleek batches the tree draw for better performance, and heavier checks are cached instead of being recalculated every frame. On very large modlists, the layout is built in the background the first time you open the tab. You may see a brief building note instead of the game freezing, then opening the tab after that should be instant. In short: it is built to stay smooth with large modlists and hundreds of research projects. [h1]Research Path Planner[/h1] With [b]Research Queue[/b] installed, selecting a locked project shows every step needed to reach it in research order, with a one-click button to queue the whole chain. [h1]Recommended Pairing[/h1] [list] [*] [b]Research Icons[/b] - Sleek already draws its own icons out of the box, pulled from what each project unlocks, so this is not required. Research Icons swaps those for nicer, hand-curated icons, including research that does not unlock a visible item. Sleek detects it automatically and uses its art on the nodes and detail panel. [*] [b]Research Tab Colors[/b] - tints research nodes by tech level, from Neolithic through to Archotech, turning the zoomed-out overview into a quick tech map. [/list] [h1]Compatibility[/h1] Sleek augments the vanilla research tree and tries not to fight other research mods. Compatibility is split into two tiers. [h2]Works with Sleek[/h2] These are detected automatically and shown inside the Sleek tab where relevant: [list] [*] [b]Research Queue[/b] - queue position numbers on nodes plus a Queue/Dequeue button in the detail panel. Also powers the research path planner: select a locked project and queue everything needed to reach it in one click. [*] [b]Research Tab Colors[/b] [*] [b]Research Icons[/b] [*] [b]Alternate Research Projects[/b] [*] [b]Discoveries[/b] [*] [b]Clean Research Sort[/b] - prefer its layout? When Clean Research Sort is installed, a "Use Clean Research Sort's sorting" option appears in Sleek's settings. Turn it on and every tab, plus the All view, uses Clean Research Sort's layout instead of Sleek's own. [*] [b]Semi Random Research[/b] - coexists with its selection system. [*] [b]Node Research[/b] - fully compatible. Sleek enables when you switch to the normal research tree, while Node Research keeps handling its own selection system. [*] [b]Progression modpack[/b] [*] [b]Combat Extended[/b] [/list] [h2]Not Compatible[/h2] These mods take over the research window completely, so they cannot be combined with Sleek. Only one mod can own the research tab. If one of them is active, Sleek detects it and disables itself so nothing breaks, but you will see that mod's interface instead of Sleek's. [h1]The grid[/h1] By default, the vanilla work boxes are replaced with small, colour-coded priority cells. Each priority has its own colour, making it easier to read an entire colonist’s row without checking every number individually. When Manual priorities is disabled, an independent option can use Filled, Tick only, or Outlined Sleek checkboxes instead of solid on/off tiles; numbered cells are unchanged. Vanilla+ mode keeps the normal work boxes, but adds light row shading, cleaner headers, and a priority legend. Work-type headers can use: [b]Classic[/b] staggered labels, with Automatic, Standard two-row, or Dense four-row layouts [b]Slanted[/b] diagonal labels [b]Vertical[/b] text Divider lines separate Slanted or Vertical work-type labels while staying out of the pawn grid. They are enabled by default on fresh and Recommended profiles and remain optional. Classic intentionally remains divider-free. Columns automatically narrow where possible to fit more work types on screen. The window grows with your colony and uses the available screen space before adding a scrollbar. When manual priorities are disabled, a small note explains that work types on the left are handled before those on the right. It disappears once numbered priorities are enabled. [h1]Focus Cards[/h1] Left-click a work-type header to open its Focus Card beside the grid. The card lists every colonist alongside their current priority, relevant skill, passion, and useful warnings. For example, it can point out a highly skilled colonist who is not assigned to the work, or someone with very little skill who has been given priority 1. From the Focus Card, you can: [list] [*]Set priorities using buttons or number keys [*]Change the entire list at once [*]Save and apply presets for individual work types [*]Copy one colonist’s setup onto others [*]Undo changes with Ctrl+Z [*]Drag across several colonists to paint priorities [/list] The small arrow on a colonist’s row opens their Pawn Focus Card instead. This shows one colonist across every work type, along with their portrait and current job. An open Focus Card is a borderless companion window beside Work. Its default-on top grip changes only card height. Its default-on outer width grip grows the card away from Work, so ordinary resizing never covers or changes the grid. A separate default-on [b]Allow Focus to expand over Work[/b] option shows a second grip on the Work-facing edge. The card normally starts beside Work with zero overlap; if a dense table or high UI scale leaves neither side enough readable space, Focus temporarily overlaps Work instead of being cut off. Drag the inner grip to control overlap manually. Focus owns input wherever it visibly covers Work, while the main Work window itself never changes size. Both docking sides mirror these controls. Double-click a width grip to restore Normal/Wide, or the top grip to match Work height. The card stays bottom-aligned, scrolls internally, and remains screen-safe. Expanded per-job rows keep a small gutter before their scrollbar. A separate Layout & Focus option can limit the automatic height of the main Work window; dense columns use horizontal overflow while Name stays frozen without a trailing divider. [h1]Per-job priorities[/h1] Work types can be expanded to change the order of the individual jobs inside them. Focus Cards retain their detailed vertical editor, while an optional disclosure control on eligible grid headers opens the same jobs as horizontal child columns beside the parent. This is an accordion: opening another parent collapses the first, and entering Reorder or closing Work collapses it safely. Inline expansion follows the final live parent columns and each parent's WorkGiver list. Ordinary modded WorkTypes and XML splitters, including Complex Jobs, Many Jobs, and Some more jobs, are supported directly rather than treated as table owners. PWC categories, GPL row layouts, and BPC's footer do not lock the setting. Full Work-tab replacements remain separate because they render their own table instead of Sleek's. For example, you can place Tend before Rescue within Doctor, or decide which Construction tasks should be attempted first. Where inline expansion is available, child cells support click, automatic-axis left-drag lines, optional wheel editing, number keys, Backspace/Delete to restore priority 3, and ordinary priority undo. The main priority still controls when the work type is considered. Per-job priorities only change the order inside that category. Untouched jobs use [b]priority 3[/b] and keep RimWorld’s normal job order among equal ranks, including changes made by other mods. Choosing 3 clears redundant custom data. In both Focus Cards, [b]All jobs[/b] stays first and the individual jobs follow that final vanilla/modded execution order rather than alphabetical labels. A single button restores the entire work type to priority 3, and the change can be undone normally. [h1]Priority scale[/h1] The priority scale can use 4, 5, 6, or 9 levels instead of vanilla’s fixed four. Five remains the default, while nine is an optional expert scale. Priority 1 is always the most urgent. If you later lower the maximum, any priorities above the new limit are moved down automatically. This applies to both colonist priorities and per-job settings. When Work Manager is active, it owns the parent work-type range. Sleek's selected scale continues to control manual per-job ordering only. [h1]Search and information[/h1] The optional search box can find colonists by name or title. It is enabled by default and can be hidden to reclaim toolbar space. It can also search for work using: [list] [*]Job names [*]Work types [*]Work scanners [*]Workstations [/list] For example, searching for “drying rack” can locate the related bill job and its parent work type. Coverage warnings mark work that currently has nobody assigned. They distinguish between work that is simply unassigned and work that none of your colonists are capable of doing. Sleek Classic keeps shaped markers attached beside each label. Vanilla+ instead uses amber/red label tint and the same detailed tooltips; in colourblind mode, one neutral underline means unassigned and two mean nobody capable. There is also an optional map alert for missing coverage. An idle button selects and jumps to the next colonist who currently has nothing to do. [h1]Grouping[/h1] Grouping is disabled by default. When enabled, colonists are placed into collapsible groups using the selected grouping lens: [list] [*]Life stage [*]Best work [*]Assigned work [*]Health [*]Mood risk [*]Colonist / slave [*]Gender [*]Origin [*]Xenotype [*]Ideology role [*]Pawn title [*]Royal title [*]Custom groups [/list] Groups can be collapsed, viewed one at a time, or replaced with your own named groups. Colonists can also be pinned to custom groups regardless of the current grouping lens. Groups and their collapsed state are saved with the colony. [h1]Make it yours[/h1] The searchable settings window is split into seven pages: [b]Appearance[/b] [b]Layout & Focus[/b] [b]Priorities & controls[/b] [b]Groups & insights[/b] [b]Accessibility[/b] [b]Compatibility[/b] [b]Advanced[/b] Most features have their own setting, so there is no single all-or-nothing layout. You can choose between the Sleek grid and Vanilla+, select your header and number styles, then enable or disable individual features such as: [list] [*]Alternating row shading [*]Header divider lines for Slanted and Vertical styles [*]Hover crosshair [*]Search box [*]Coverage warnings with Sleek markers or Vanilla+ label cues [*]Idle colonist button [*]Column-order reminder [*]Per-job editing [*]Drag editing [*]Scroll-wheel editing [*]Help button [*]Passion icons and borders [*]Rename controls [/list] Features that are easy to trigger accidentally, including scroll-wheel editing and rename controls, begin disabled. Passion marks and low-skill warning borders begin enabled, and can be turned off independently. Search by feature name to open and briefly highlight the exact option. Every ordinary section has its own recommended reset, and the sidebar can restore all feature settings while preserving saved presets, colour themes, work-type order data, per-colony groups, report history, and the settings-window size. The Sleek options window can be dragged by its background and resized with RimWorld's bottom-right window handle; it remembers its chosen size. A default-Off Compatibility option can keep this dialog open when clicking outside it or onto another monitor; it affects no other mod's settings window, and X, Close, and Escape remain normal. [b]Advanced[/b] is a permanent dedicated page for exact and complex customization. Merely opening it changes nothing. It contains granular controls for: [list] [*]Board, accent, header-text, and normal-text colours [*]Normal Slate, Deep black, and Cool steel base palettes, plus Advanced saveable colour themes. Themes change colours only, never geometry [*]Cell, Name-column, and work-column dimensions [*]Slanted-header angle and guide strengths [*]Group-band geometry [*]Focus Card width, spacing, and row heights [*]Drag-axis, wheel, header-button, cross-link, and group double-click behavior [/list] Advanced values remain active when you leave the page. Unsafe combinations are adjusted only at render time - for example, a narrow Slanted column receives a safe effective angle, and an oversized Focus Card is capped on a narrow UI canvas - while the configured value remains saved. [h1]Accessibility[/h1] Colour-vision settings are included for red-green and blue-yellow colour deficiencies. Priority cells use differences in brightness and shape as well as colour, so the grid does not rely entirely on hue. [b]High Contrast[/b] brightens text and increases border thickness. [b]Calm mode[/b] removes some of the movement and visual emphasis from the grid, including hover bands, sheen, and coloured group accents. Skill indicators are available in three sizes, and passions can optionally be displayed directly on priority cells. [h1]Compatibility[/h1] Sleek only changes the colonist Work tab. Other pawn tables, including Numbers and Mech Work Tab, are left alone. Full replacements for the Work tab take priority, and Sleek disables itself when any of these are active: [list] [*]Work Tab by Fluffy [*]Better Work Tab [*]Compact Work Tab [*]Enhanced Work Tab [/list] Version 2.4.1 adds a public opt-in API that a full Work-tab replacement can use to negotiate selected Sleek features without patching Sleek's private compatibility logic. No Better Work Tab integration is bundled in this release, so Better Work Tab continues to own the entire Work tab unless and until it adds API support. More Work Priorities also causes Sleek to stand aside by default. Optional compatibility settings allow some Sleek features to remain active, including the option to use Sleek cells with MWP’s stored priorities. Grouped Pawns Lists controls Work-tab grouping by default. Inline child columns remain available on its Work-table row layout; choosing the existing Sleek Work-tab takeover changes grouping ownership only. Better Pawn Control remains the Work-policy owner. Sleek preserves extended parent priorities and stores explicit per-job ordering with each policy. Inline child columns remain available alongside BPC's native footer, while Focus Card per-job editing remains available. Work Manager remains the automation and range owner. Its columns, controls, exclusions, and separate header lane stay available, while Sleek’s manual per-job ordering remains independent. Oracle’s Skill Icon Retextures are read directly from Oracle’s loaded content, including compatible Vanilla Skills Expanded passion art. No Oracle artwork is copied into Sleek. More Than Capable keeps full control of hated-work behavior; Sleek only adds read-only amber markers and tooltips. WorkRoles is incompatible because it directly controls both priorities and job order. The following are supported: [list] [*]Smart Priorities [*]Personal Work Categories [*]Complex Jobs [*]Many Jobs [*]Some more jobs [*]Better Pawn Control (parent and per-job Work policies) [*]Work Manager (external parent-priority automation and Work-tab controls) [*]More Than Capable (hated work gets an amber corner flag) [*]Vanilla Skills Expanded and Alpha Skills passions [*]Oracle's Skill Icon Retextures [*]Grouped Pawns Lists [*]Colony Groups [*]Mod-added work types [/list] [h1]Disclaimer[/h1] This mod involved AI-assisted tools during development. I do not release something unless I have actually put time into making sure it works as intended. I also intend to actively support all mods I publish. If bugs are reported, I will try to fix them as soon as I can and keep the mod maintained properly. Made with the help of AI and Modmixer. name: Sleek Work Schedule Tab
author: Squishyjellyfish
description: [h1]Sleek Work Schedule Tab[/h1] [b]Sleek Work Schedule Tab[/b] turns RimWorld’s Schedule tab from a cramped block grid into a clean, readable timeline. Pawn schedules are shown as merged, labelled bars instead of tiny isolated squares, so you can understand a whole day at a glance. Sleep, Work, Recreation, Meditation, Anything, and custom assignments stay readable, with a calmer visual style that feels like it belongs in a polished UI overhaul. [h1]Built to Work Alongside Your Other Schedule Mods[/h1] This mod is the visual and editing layer. It is not a preset system, not automation, and not a competing schedule manager. Designed to sit neatly beside: [list] [*] Preset Work Schedules [*] Schedule Everything! [*] Automatic Night Owl [*] Chronos Pointer [*] Grouped Pawns Lists [*] Too Many Areas [*] RimHUD [*] PrettyUI [*] AOBA Exosuit Framework [*] Rimbody [*] Rimbody Vanilla-Style Integration Patch [*] TD Enhancement Pack (hidden areas respected) [*] Hospitality (Continued) [*] Gastronomy (Continued) [*] Zone To Schedule [*] Work-type mods and custom schedule assignments [/list] Preset mods can handle saved schedules. Chronos can handle time-pointer features. Grouping mods can handle organisation. Sleek Work Schedule Tab focuses on making the actual Schedule tab look better and feel better to edit. [h1]Features[/h1] [list] [*] Clean merged timeline blocks with readable labels [*] Optional subtle top-edge hour notches [*] Anything blocks that stay clear without dotted visual noise [*] Softer, more cohesive schedule colours [*] Selectable allowed-area styles: segmented strip or compact pill [*] Optional compact-pill swatch rail [*] Drag-paint schedule and allowed-area editing [*] Right-click erase to Anything [*] Copy and paste schedules [*] Fill-day and selected-pawn bulk actions [*] Batched undo support [*] Rich hover tooltips [*] Optional paint preview [*] Mod options with recommended defaults [/list] [h1]Compatibility-First Design[/h1] Sleek Work Schedule Tab uses normal RimWorld timetable assignments, so custom TimeAssignmentDefs from mods like Schedule Everything! and AOBA Exosuit Framework work naturally. Progression: Education class schedule blocks are protected from Sleek paint/fill/paste actions and should be edited in Progression's Education tab. It avoids adding presets, sorting, automation, or extra management UI, so it can sit cleanly beside the mods that already do those jobs. No bloat. No preset overlap. No fighting your mod list. Just a prettier, smoother, more readable Schedule tab. [h1]Disclaimer[/h1] I will not hide the fact that AI helped during development. The mod has still been tested and worked on by me, and I hope it is useful to the people who choose to install it. Made with the help of AI and Modmixer.

name: Tab-sorting
author: Mlie
description: [img]https://img.litet.net/logos/Self-Info.png[/img] Sort your stuff! This mod can sort furniture/structures into appropriate tabs. It started as an improved version of the LigtsTab (by betaALPHAs) but since that version relied on patches it was very complex and hard to maintain. Instead this mod uses C#-code to sort things after they have loaded, removing the need for specific patch-files for each mod/item. The downside is that it requires a rescan of the changed tabs at startup but this should add no more than at most a few seconds depending on how many tabs has been changed. Currently the mod supports the following sorting: - All lights to a separate Lights-tab - All walls and doors to the Structure-tab - All floors to the Floors-tab - All beds and linkable furniture to a separate Bedroom-tab - All hospitalbeds and linkable medical furniture to a separate Hospital-tab - All tables and sittable furniture to a separate Tables/Chairs-tab - All decorative items to a separate Decorations-tab - All kitchen furniture and linkables to a separate Kitchen-tab - All research furniture to a separate Research-tab - All Ideology ritual-furniture to a separate Ideology-tab Special case - All storage-containers to the Storage-tab If [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=731732064]Extended Storage[/url] or [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1617282896]LWM's Deep Storage[/url] is loaded their Storage-tab will be used instead. Options dependent of other mods: - All garden-tools to the Garden Tools-tab of [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2007063961]VGP Garden Tools[/url] - All fences the Fences-tab of [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2012420113]Fences and Floors[/url] Other options: - If a tab is empty after the sorting the mod can remove it - If a tab does not currently show anything due to research missing, it can be hidden - You can sort all tabs alphabetically, the Zones and Orders-tab can be skipped - You can also sort the tabs manually - Items that use the same button can be moved all at once, for example stuffed floors - Manual sorting - if some items gets in the wrong place, move them around. - Create new tabs to sort to - Added support for marcin212's [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1195427067]Architect Icons[/url] - Sort the main buttons - Sort the order of buildable items - Sort buildable items alphabetically If you find any item that don't get sorted or gets sorted in the wrong tab, please leave a report of what item and from what mod it comes from. Either here in the comments or at the support-channel via the Discord-link below. Also, if you have any ideas on more stuff that can be categorized, just let me know and Ill look into it. - Added Korean translation, thanks isty2e - Added Russian translation, thanks Reiquard - Thanks to some performace updates and the "Move all"-feature by Taranchuk - Kitchen room role worker fix by slippycheeze [table] [tr] [td][url=https://discord.gg/h5TY6DA][img]https://img.litet.net/logos/Discord.png[/img][/url][/td] [td][url=https://github.com/emipa606/TabSorting][img]https://img.litet.net/logos/Github.png[/img][/url][/td] [/tr] [tr] [td][img]https://img.litet.net/logos/SafeToAdd.png[/img][/td] [td][img]https://img.litet.net/logos/SafeToRemove.png[/img][/td] [/tr] [/table] Big thanks to [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/smashphil/myworkshopfiles/?appid=294100]SmashPhil[/url] for the help and coding examples when I made a better (good) version of the settings menu! author: Mlie
description: [img]https://img.litet.net/logos/Self-Info.png[/img] [b]TLDR: This mod scans your installed mods and suggest working/more updated replacements for those mods[/b] Continuations of mods has many names and has become an large part of the RimWorld modding community. It can be hard to keep track of when mods gets a new version by another modder. This mod tries to remedy that by keeping track and informing about when a mod has a replacement version on the workshop. Data from my own [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1541984105]collection[/url] of continued mods is a large part of this mod. Another large part is from my friends continuations; the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/?id=2787987321]collection[/url] by [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/zaljerem]Zaljerem[/url] and the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/?id=2099979037]collection[/url] by [url=https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198032065507]velcroboy333[/url]. The mod also uses info about mods that have been requested on my Discord server and continued by another modder as well as any mod published on the workshop using the usual suffixes for continued mods (as seen in the preview image). This mod should work well together with my [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3218690663]Show Mod Updates[/url] to make it easier to keep track of you favorite mods during those major RimWorld updates! The replacement-rules is updated regularly to include new releases and the mod will download the latest version of the rules as soon as they get published. I hope this will be of use and if you have info about a mod-continuation not showing up in the mod or a faulty replacement suggestion, please report it in the comments or on the linked Discord-server. name: Visible Raid Points
author: 1trickPwnyta
description: Ever wondered just how many points the game used to generate a raid? Are you getting the maximum 10,000 point raids yet? Now you'll know because you can see exactly how many raid points are used to generate every raid and many other types of incidents. For an even more educational experience, you can also view a threat points breakdown that shows the details of how the points were calculated, line by line. This option will not work and/or make sense with mods that alter the way threat points are calculated. Spanish translation by Ferchu. Korean translation by PenguinsCanFly. Note: This mod is now fully compatible with my other mod, Unlimited Threat Scale: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2562732435 in version 1.5+ of RimWorld. Unlimited Threat Scale must be before this mod in the mod order list. === Updates === 06/11/2025: Updated to 1.6 04/13/2025: Fix mod conflict with Quality Recasting Table 04/09/2025: Add threat points for sanguophage hunters, add link to points breakdown in letter 11/09/2024: Corrected threat point breakdown for royalty ending raids 05/22/2024: Added threat points for Anomaly endgame events 04/22/2024: Added/fixed threat points for events summoned by psychic rituals 04/20/2024: Fixed empty settings on first install bug, add enable/disable all button in event type menu 04/19/2024: Massive overhaul that adds support for many Anomaly events, more accurate threat points for non-raid events and some quest-related raids, adds option to toggle threat point display for different event types 03/14/2024: Updated to 1.5 07/11/2023: Fixed points breakdown for children and slaves 10/26/2022: Updated to 1.4 03/09/2022: Created alternate version of the mod for compatibility with Unlimited Threat Scale 09/28/2021: Added extra error logging. 08/26/2021: Added threat points breakdown feature. 08/09/2021: Added Korean translation. 08/06/2021: Enabled visible threat points for additional incident types including infestations, crashed ship parts, mechanoid clusters, manhunter packs, animal mass insanity, and caravan ambushes. Added Spanish translation. === Credits === Mod icon: twitter.com/mouse_draws

name: Visible Wealth
author: 1trickPwnyta
description: Did you know that your thrumbofur stockpile makes up a massive portion of your colony's wealth? Did you know that your snowhare corpse is worth $18? Well now you can see a detailed breakdown of your colony's wealth, including all your items, buildings, and pawns. You can visualize your wealth as a list or as a pie chart, each with options to further customize their appearance. Do you want to see all your sources of wealth laid out in order from most to least expensive? You can do that. Do you want to see how much your building wealth counts toward raid points compared to other wealth? You can enable raid point mode. There are three ways to open the wealth breakdown window. By default, you can click the $ symbol in the bottom right corner of your screen (same area as the roof overlay button etc.) or you can press Shift+4 (like you're typing a $, and this shortcut key can be changed in the settings). In the settings you can also enable a main button that appears at the bottom of your screen near the History tab button. === Updates === 09/05/2025: Separate buildings made from stuff into their own wealth entries to fix broken info card 07/09/2025: Fix bug when using keyboard shortcut to open wealth breakdown when it's already open 06/11/2025: Updated to 1.6 05/20/2025: Add pie chart and many more options === Credits === Mod icon: twitter.com/mouse_draws

name: Work Box Highlight
author: Nuff
description: In the Work Tab, highlights the work type of the colonist's current job.

name: Work History
author: lebek
description: Adds a bar chart to the bottom of the colonist inspect pane showing where their time has gone — work types, sleep, joy, meals, drafted, mental breaks, downed, idle, medical, travel. Buttons in the chart's top-right switch between [b]Day · Quadrum · Year · Lifetime[/b]. Selecting multiple colonists sums the chart across them. [h1]Performance[/h1] Per-colonist storage is bounded: 60 days of daily category counts, after which older days are folded into a lifetime total. Savegame overhead is roughly 1.5 MB for a 20-colonist colony, and stays that size at year 1 or year 100. The background sampler does one tally per colonist per in-game second. The inspect chart reuses its last result for 5 seconds of real time, so an open pane at 60 fps does not drive any per-frame recomputation. [h1]Compatibility[/h1] Does not touch the Work tab, so it sits alongside Fluffy's Work Tab, PriorityMaster, and similar without interaction. The one expected conflict is other mods that also resize or redraw the colonist inspect pane. If the pane looks the wrong size, check for another mod patching it. Safe to add to an existing save. Safe to remove — the tracked data is discarded along with the mod. [h1]Settings[/h1] - Categories visible before "+N more" (3–25, default 8). - On/off toggle for each synthetic category: sleep, joy, meal, drafted, mental, downed, idle, medical, travel. Sampling rate and retention window are not exposed; they are fixed at values that make every range button accurate. [h1]Notes[/h1] - Tracks colonists, prisoners, and slaves. Does not track guests, animals, or mechs. - 1.6 only. Bug reports welcome — please include your log and active mod list.

name: Xenotype Summary
author: Waggish Pluto
description: Ever felt lost in the wall of text that is a complex xenotype? Xenotype Summary provides a clean, organized overview of everything a xenotype actually DOES. Inspired by Mr. Samuel Streamer to help navigate the genetic chaos! Features: - Full Description List: Read all gene descriptions and custom effects in one scrollable list. - Aggregated Stats: See total offsets and multipliers for stats, capacities, and damage factors. - Breakdown Tooltips: Hover over any aggregated stat to see exactly which genes are contributing to the value. - Chemical & Global Factors: Summary of pain, resource loss, and chemical modifiers. - Work & Mood: Consolidated list of disabled work types and nullified thoughts. - Abilities & Traits: Quick reference for all gained abilities and forced/suppressed traits. - Universal Access: Accessible from the Pawn Gene tab, Info Cards, Xenotype Editor, and Gene Assembler. No more hovering over 50 icons to figure out why your colonist is glowing or why they're suddenly immune to fire. One button, one summary, total clarity.

name: Yet Another Research Tree (YART)
author: SeoHyeon
description: Yet Another Research Tree (YART) replaces the vanilla research tab with a custom, graph-based tech tree. Features - Automatic graph layout of all research, including projects and tabs added by other mods. - Per-channel research queue (vanilla bench, Anomaly knowledge, Vanilla Gravship Expanded, and more). - Fast search by research name, unlocked content, description, or @mod. Compatibility - World Tech Level: OK. hides research above the world's tech level. - Vanilla Gravship Expanded: OK. shows Gravtech research as its own channel. - Semi Random Research: OK. its "Go to Tech Tree" button opens YART. - other Research Tree mods: NO.

name: Vanilla Animals Expanded — Royal Animals
author: Oskar Potocki, Sarg Bjornson, Erin
description: Royal animals is something we have promised a long time ago, and never quite found the time to deliver. From the very initial notions, what we wanted to do is to introduce some special animals with unique gimmicks that could go alongside the pampered nobles in the Royalty DLC. This is a great opportunity for us to create something super unique and not entirely realistic - whilst also making the Royalty DLC more attractive by utilising mechanics and code added in it. I hope this selection of animals will make you want to collect them all, as each of them comes with a unique function that’s bound to come in handy.
